Historical accounts describe Babul Opera’s mid-20th-century performances at venues such as Jashore Town Hall as productions marked by artistic excellence and emotional depth, without the vulgarity that later became associated with some jatra shows.

But the art form’s decline gathered pace after the 1980s.

Artistes blame social neglect, financial insecurity and safety concerns for its dwindling popularity.

Shipra said jatra performers were never given the recognition they deserved.

“Performers were neglected and deprived of the respect they deserved as artistes, which prevented the younger generation from being drawn to the art form,” she said.

Irregular performances made it difficult for artistes to earn a living, while negative campaigns against jatra exposed performers to harassment and physical attacks in some areas, she added.

Sagar believes the shift away from traditional storytelling contributed significantly to its decline.

Image A scene from a Jatra performance.

“Earlier, performances depicted traditional folk and historical narratives like Laili-Majnu, Rupban, and Nawab Sirajuddaula. Since late 1980’s, such narratives were replaced by various forms of vulgarity and obscenity that crept into jatra performances, initially in a bid to attract audience. However, it instigated unwarranted controversies and negative campaigns against jatra gained momentum, from which this traditional folk theater could never recover,” he said.

The jatra community also lost one of its most influential figures this year with the death of Milan Kanti Dey (1948-2026), who died aged 77 on February 7.

A Bangla Academy Literary Award winner, Milan was a playwright, director, actor, researcher and university instructor who played a pioneering role in jatra in Chattogram and across Bangladesh.

His autobiography, Ami Je Ek Jatrawala, remains the only autobiographical account by a jatra artiste in Bangla literature.

Image The historical context of the fall of Nawab Sirajuddaula still remains a popular Jatra play. Photo: Star File

Despite its decline, jatra retains a loyal audience in some rural areas, including parts of the Chattogram Hill Tracts.

Organisations such as the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy and Jatra Shilpa Unnayan Parishad continue to organise festivals and other initiatives, with government support, to preserve the tradition.

The Ministry of Cultural Affairs introduced the Jatra Industry Development Policy 2012 to revive rural cultural traditions, establish formal registration for troupes and streamline permission procedures for performances.

Syed Ayaz Mabud, cultural officer at the Chattogram District Shilpakala Academy, said government initiatives had helped the struggling industry.

“Under the Jatra Industry Development Policy 2012, troupes scattered across the country have been brought under formal registration,” he said.

“Every year, the Shilpakala Academy organises central festivals featuring these registered troupes. Furthermore, the list of registered troupes is forwarded to district magistrates so local administrations can ensure full security whenever a troupe stages a performance,” Ayaz added.

Yet artistes say these initiatives remain insufficient to revive jatra.

With too few performances to sustain a livelihood, many artistes now pursue jatra out of passion or alongside other occupations.

They also say government financial assistance remains inadequate. Although veteran performers are eligible for allowances, bureaucratic delays and alleged irregularities often prevent deserving artistes from receiving support.

For an art form that once brought entire villages together on winter nights, survival now rests on scattered performances, devoted artistes and efforts to preserve a fading cultural tradition.

title: 'A good Christmas gift': Chase eyes Bangladesh series win to propel Windies up WTC table
text:
West Indies have had the luxury of an extended build-up to their Test series against Bangladesh. Now, captain Roston Chase wants his side to turn that preparation into wins, and give their World Test Championship campaign a much-needed lift.

The Caribbean side spent time in a camp in Chennai before arriving in Dhaka on October 18, giving them time to adjust to conditions ahead of the two-Test series. Bangladesh, in contrast, have had a shorter window to prepare as a team, with most of their players returning after the ODI tri-series in the UAE ended for them on October 21.

With the opening Test starting at Mirpur on Wednesday, Chase said West Indies had already put in the work needed to cope with Dhaka's heat. Most of the squad had trained in Chennai, while those who missed the camp were in India for the white-ball series. The team have since completed two full-unit practice sessions and played a practice match.

“Most of the guys were in the camp in Chennai and those who weren't there were in India for the white-ball series. And then we had two good practices, as you said, as a full unit, and we also got in a practice game,” Chase said at a press conference in Mirpur on Tuesday.

West Indies did not train on Tuesday, the eve of the first Test, but Chase insisted the conditions had not unsettled his players.

“I think the guys are comfortable in the conditions. We've been putting in the hard yards. It's been a bit hot, hotter than usual, but as I said, the guys are enjoying the conditions so far and we've been obviously suited to them as well,” he said.

West Indies will also draw confidence from their recent Test results, having won a home series against Sri Lanka and drawn another against Pakistan. They have played four Tests this year, winning two, drawing one and losing one.

Now eighth in the WTC standings, they have one last opportunity in this cycle to improve their position, with the Bangladesh series their final assignment. Chase is targeting two wins to push his team up the table and potentially finish fifth or sixth.

“If we want to make any strides in terms of going up the table, it has to be in this series,” he said.

“We're in some good form coming into this series, so we want to take two wins and try to take ourselves up the ladder and finish probably in fifth or sixth position and that would be a good Christmas gift for the team as well,” he added.

title: Kvaratskhelia undergoes 'successful' knee surgery
text:
Khvicha Kvaratskhelia "underwent successful surgery for a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee," his club, Paris Saint-Germain, announced on Tuesday.

The Georgian attacker, who finished sixth in Monday's Ballon d'Or, underwent surgery at a clinic in Doha, Qatar, and "will now begin his rehabilitation", PSG said.

Kvaratskhelia suffered the injury in PSG's Champions League victory over Barcelona last week.

His entourage told AFP last week that "it was difficult" to discuss a return date, but that this type of injury usually sidelines players for at least six months.

title: Sri Lanka end England hopes with crushing win over Pakistan
text:
Pacer Dilshan Madushanka grabbed a career best 5-34 as Sri Lanka cruised to a thumping eight-wicket win over Pakistan in Lahore on Tuesday which ends England's hopes of reaching the tri-series final.

The left-armer was well supported by spinner Sahan Arachchige, who took 2-24, to dismiss Pakistan for a paltry 110 in just 25.3 overs. The Sri Lankan batters reached the target in just 18.1 overs.

The victory is Sri Lanka's second in three games, enough to deprive the third team England of a spot in Sunday's final, for which Pakistan have already qualified with three wins.

The English, who have contrived to lose successive matches against Sri Lanka and Pakistan from winning positions, needed the hosts to win to have any hope of joining them in the final.

Consequently, Thursday's match between Sri Lanka and England is a dead rubber.

Kamindu Mendis struck two sixes and eight fours in his 62 not out from 60 balls, reaching his fifth ODI half-century with a six off Shaheen Shah Afridi. Pavan Rathnayake was unbeaten on 23.

Avishka Fernando fell for 16 and skipper Kusal Mendis made eight, with wickets going to Shaheen and Arafat Minhas.

Mendis praised the efforts of his bowlers, particularly Madushanka.

"We executed our plans well and Dilshan bowled superbly, everyone is happy at the team's progress," said Mendis, whose team hunted down 430 against England on Thursday -- the second highest successful chase in all ODIs.

Shaheen put on a brave face after an abject display by his team.

"We must forget this match and get ready for the final," said Shaheen. "We will come back in the final and bat stronger."

Earlier, it was Madushanka's demolition act that wrecked Pakistan, who were put in to bat. Their 110 was their second lowest ODI total at home behind the 75 they made against the same opposition and at the same venue in 2009.

Pakistan, who chased down 242 in a thrilling one-wicket win against England on Sunday, batted poorly on a flat Gaddafi Stadium pitch with token resistance from Babar Azam, top-scoring with 29, and Hasan Nawaz who made 17.

Madushanka dismissed out-of-form opener Fakhar Zaman for five in the fourth over to start the slide.

Azam and Saad Baig put on 23 for the third wicket before Madushanka had Baig caught at cover for five, while Arachchige removed Salman Agha for nine.

The next over saw Azam falling leg before to Eshan Malinga.

Madushanka ensured Pakistan fell way short of a decent total by taking the wickets of Shaheen (15) and Haris Rauf (one) to complete a five-wicket haul.

Madushanka's previous best figure of 5-80 came against India in Mumbai in the 2023 World Cup.

title: Ronaldo in line for Portugal return in November after fallout with coach
text:
Cristiano Ronaldo is in Portugal's preliminary squad for next month's Nations League matches, opening the door to an international return after his fallout with coach Jorge Jesus, a federation source told AFP on Tuesday.

The 41-year-old abruptly left the Portugal camp on September 30 during the opening qualifiers for the Nations League, before accusing Jesus of breaking his word about giving him game time.

A spokesperson for the Portuguese football federation (FPF) confirmed reports Ronaldo was in line for a return to the squad ahead of games at home to Denmark and in Wales on November 14 and 17.

Jesus will announce his final squad on November 6, the spokesperson added.

The FPF last week announced it had handed Ronaldo a 30-day suspension for walking out. The suspension was backdated, meaning he will be free to return by the end of this week.

Ronaldo apologised to supporters earlier in October, adding he would accept any punishment that was imposed.

In a social media post shortly after deserting his teammates, he accused Jesus of promising to give him playing time against Norway before failing to honour it but insisted he was not retiring from international duty.

He said a further bone of contention between him and the coach was Jesus had not mentioned at a press conference prior to the game with Denmark a series of points they had agreed upon.

Reigning champions Portugal won all four of their Nations League matches, three of them without Ronaldo, and qualified for the quarter-finals with two games to spare.

The five-time Ballon d'Or winner is the all-time top goalscorer and record appearance-maker in men's international football.

Ronaldo, who made his Portugal debut in 2003 at the age of 18, has said this will "probably" be his final year in football.

title: Chinese state TV suspends La Liga broadcasts after Mbappe remark
text:
Chinese state television has suspended broadcasts of La Liga matches following remarks by Real Madrid star Kylian Mbappe about Mao Zedong, state-owned China Media Group announced Tuesday.

CMG, which oversees public broadcaster CCTV, said in a release that it had suspended the broadcast of La Liga matches, as well as advertisements involving the French player, following his comments in a viral video.

title: Abhishek–Sooryavanshi mayhem sets records tumbling
text:
An explosive opening partnership between Abhishek Sharma and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi powered India to a six-wicket victory over New Zealand in the third T20I in Wellington on Tuesday, sealing the five-match series with two matches to spare.

Chasing a target of 199, India raced to 201 in just 13.2 overs, with Abhishek smashing a breathtaking 113 and Sooryavanshi contributing a blistering 45. The opening pair added 133 runs in just 7.1 overs, dismantling the New Zealand bowling attack in a remarkable display of power-hitting.

India’s extraordinary chase rewrote several records in men’s T20 cricket, with Abhishek’s century further cementing his reputation as one of the format’s most destructive batters.

Here are the key records from India’s emphatic victory:

118: Highest powerplay score in men’s T20Is

India smashed 118 runs in the powerplay, setting a new record for the highest score in the first six overs of a men’s T20 International. The previous record was 116, scored by Romania against Serbia in 2021 in just 5.4 overs.

7.4 overs: Fastest team to reach 150 in men’s T20 cricket

India reached 150 in just 7.4 overs, setting a new benchmark in men’s T20 cricket. The previous fastest was 8.2 overs, achieved by Sunrisers Hyderabad against Lucknow Super Giants in the IPL in 2024, with Abhishek also featuring in that innings. Turkey held the previous T20I record, reaching the milestone in 8.3 overs against Bulgaria in 2025.

2.2 overs: Joint-fastest team to reach 50 in men’s T20Is

India raced to 50 in just 2.2 overs, equalling the fastest recorded team fifty in men’s T20Is among matches with available ball-by-ball data. It was also the joint-second-fastest fifty in men’s T20 cricket overall, behind the Colombo Kings’ two-over effort against the Galle Gladiators in the Lanka Premier League in 2020.

Image

Five overs: India’s 100-run milestone

India reached 100 in just five overs, recording the second-fastest team century in men’s T20 cricket. Only Eswatini, who reached the mark in 4.5 overs against Mozambique earlier this year, have done it quicker.

26 runs: Record-breaking first over

India plundered 26 runs in the opening over of the chase, the most by a Full Member nation in a men’s T20 International. Australia previously held the record with 24 runs against West Indies in 2010, off an over bowled by Kemar Roach.

11 centuries: Abhishek becomes India’s leading T20 centurion

Abhishek’s stunning 113 took his tally to 11 centuries in T20 cricket, making him India’s leading century-maker in the format and moving him past Virat Kohli’s 10. Globally, he now ranks third on the list of most T20 hundreds, behind Chris Gayle with 22 and Babar Azam with 13.

Four T20I centuries: Among India’s elite

Four of Abhishek’s 11 T20 centuries have come in T20 Internationals. He became the third Indian batter to reach four T20I hundreds, joining Rohit Sharma, who has five, and Suryakumar Yadav, who also has four.

Three centuries in fewer than 40 balls

Three of Abhishek’s four T20I centuries have come in fewer than 40 balls, a feat unmatched by any other batter, with no other player having more than one such hundred. His Wellington century was also his fifth T20 hundred in fewer than 40 balls, an overall record.

Nine lightning-fast T20I fifties

Abhishek has now registered nine half-centuries in T20 Internationals in 20 balls or fewer. No other batter has managed even five such rapid fifties, underlining his extraordinary ability to score at an exceptional rate.

13.2 overs: India’s second-fastest chase of a 190-plus target

India completed their chase of 199 in just 13.2 overs, making it the second-fastest successful chase of a target exceeding 190 in men’s T20 cricket. Estonia hold the record after chasing 192 against Cyprus in 13 overs in 2024.

Image

title: Abhishek’s 35-ball ton, record Powerplay blitz seal India’s series win over New Zealand
text:
India clinched an unassailable 3-0 lead in the five-match T20I series against New Zealand after cruising to a six-wicket victory in the third match in Wellington on Tuesday, with Abhishek Sharma producing a breathtaking century to headline a record-breaking chase.

Chasing a target of 199, India reached 199-4 in just 13.2 overs, thanks to Abhishek’s explosive 113 off only 38 deliveries. The left-hander smashed his fourth T20I century, dismantling the New Zealand bowling attack with a sensational display of power-hitting.

Vaibhav Sooryavanshi provided the perfect support at the top of the order, scoring a blistering 44 off 19 balls after being promoted to open the innings. Having batted at No. 3 in the second T20I, the youngster made an immediate impact in his new role as India raced towards the target.

The opening partnership set the tone for an extraordinary chase, with India plundering 118 runs in the Powerplay -- the highest powerplay total in T20I cricket. The visitors also reached their team fifty in just 2.2 overs, setting a new benchmark for a full-member nation.

Abhishek’s remarkable innings, combined with Sooryavanshi’s aggressive approach, left New Zealand struggling to contain India’s relentless assault. The visitors required only 80 balls to complete the chase, underlining their dominance with both bat and intent.

Image

Earlier, Daryl Mitchell had kept New Zealand competitive with an unbeaten 89, helping the hosts post 198-3 after being put under pressure by the Indian bowlers. Mitchell anchored the innings while finding the boundary regularly, ensuring New Zealand finished with a challenging total.

Finn Allen contributed 40, while Bevon Jacobs remained unbeaten on 39 to provide valuable late momentum. The pair’s contributions helped the hosts build a strong platform, but their efforts ultimately proved insufficient against India’s extraordinary batting display.

Arshdeep Singh was India’s standout bowler, conceding just 33 runs in his four overs and dismissing Tim Seifert. His economical spell helped prevent New Zealand from pushing the total beyond the 200-run mark.

title: Shanto wants Bangladesh to focus on small targets
text:
Bangladesh Test captain Najmul Hossain Shanto wants his team to focus on the immediate task rather than the prospect of reaching the World Test Championship (WTC) final, as the Tigers prepare to begin their two-match series against West Indies in Mirpur on Wednesday.

Bangladesh are currently fourth in the WTC standings, with six Tests remaining in the current cycle, four at home and two in South Africa. A strong run in those matches could put them in contention for a place in the final, but Shanto insisted on Tuesday that the team were not looking too far ahead.

“To be very honest, I am thinking only about this Test match, not even the two-match series,” Shanto told reporters ahead of the opening Test.

“As a team, we always focus on how we are going to play the next match or series. If we win these matches and series, we can achieve those bigger goals automatically.”

The captain said the possibility of reaching the WTC final was inspiring rather than a source of pressure, adding that the team had no intention of doing anything beyond its established preparation and processes.

“This is certainly an important series, but we want to execute the same process that has been producing results for us,” he said.

Bangladesh have had mixed results in recent Tests, including an innings defeat against Zimbabwe, a victory in Australia and a draw against Afghanistan. Shanto acknowledged that consistency remained an area for improvement, although he felt the team had made progress in handling pressure.

“We have many discussions about that in the dressing room. If you look at recent times, I would say that tendency has reduced considerably. I would not say we have overcome it completely, but we have improved,” he said.

Shanto also believes Bangladesh can improve significantly from their current level, provided they continue to address their shortcomings.

“You can expect this team to improve by another 20 to 30 per cent from where we are now, Inshallah,” he said.

The captain welcomed the growing public and media interest in Test cricket, saying the culture of better performances in the format had begun to develop two or three years ago. However, he stressed that the team were not satisfied with their progress.

“Whatever we have achieved so far is not enough. We have the ability to improve further, and that is what we discuss in the dressing room whenever we talk about Test cricket,” Shanto said.

With the West Indies series offering an opportunity to strengthen Bangladesh's position in the WTC standings, Shanto's message remained centred on incremental progress rather than calculations about the final.

“We have been focusing on small targets over the last couple of years. I am not thinking too far ahead, and that approach helps our team perform well on the field,” he said.

title: Mushfiqur injured in training ahead of first Test
text:
Bangladesh batter Mushfiqur Rahim was hit on the hand during

Image Mushfiqur Rahim. Photo: Firoz Ahmed

a net session on Tuesday as the hosts continued their preparations for the first Test against West Indies.

Mushfiqur was given ice at the ground before leaving the training session.

The extent of the injury, though, was not immediately clear.

The first of the two Tests, part of the ICC World Test Championship, gets underway at the Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium tomorrow.

title: Chaos building towards a perfect storm?
text:
Bangladesh cricket cannot seem to escape chaos. Although the Test team have reasons for optimism ahead of the home series against West Indies, beginning tomorrow, a turbulent buildup has left them with plenty to address before the first ball is bowled.

“Is this the first time there's chaos before a match?” Bangladesh head coach Phil Simmons asked with a wry smile when questioned about the buildup to the two-match series yesterday.

Batting coach Mohammad Ashraful had attended a session on Saturday, only to be discontinued by evening. The sudden axing came on the back of Bangladesh’s faltering batting in the recent ODI tri-series in the UAE, which had already cost them momentum ahead of their red-ball assignments. More troubling, however, is the debate over players’ accountability and dedication that has followed the tri-series.





The Tigers’ Test side, on the other hand, had been on a high, despite a slightly deflating draw in the one-off Abu Dhabi Test against Afghanistan. Yet the squad had been unable to prepare together before the crucial Mirpur Test, as the World Test Championship (WTC) campaign gathers pace.

“Every series is important,” Simmons said. “Those that we were playing at the start of these two years were important too. But the thing is how we go about our business, our preparation for the series.”

Following the second Test in Sylhet, Bangladesh will travel to Johannesburg to face South Africa six days later in another WTC assignment, leaving little time between matches to prepare for the upcoming challenges. “It's not what's happening outside, it's what we do as a team to prepare,” added the former West Indies coach.

The players had met Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) president Tamim Iqbal in the UAE after the defeat against Zimbabwe. On Sunday, Tamim again sat down with five national team players, with a few members of the team management also present.

“I was there.” Simmons said. “The meeting was more about the things we need to put together to push Bangladesh cricket forward.”

With the team in form in the red-ball format, the focus on broader development ahead of a Test series raised questions. The Bangladesh coach, however, dismissed concerns that the meeting had been a distraction “because it was not about the series”.

The Tigers will be without Nahid Rana for the first Test. The push for results in Zimbabwe had already cost them the services of the express pacer. His absence could make the South Africa Tests considerably harder, but team management, still harbouring hopes of securing Rana’s services, may take risks that only add to the uncertainty.

Litton Das, meanwhile, has yet to receive clearance for the series opener, leaving another question mark, although Simmons understands the wicketkeeper-batter is available.





A perfect storm may be brewing, threatening to engulf Bangladesh as it has in the past, particularly at ICC events. Whether they can keep their heads above water will depend on how they navigate the mounting distractions and respond when the Test series gets underway.

title: South Africa select 'enforcer' Coetzee for Australia decider
text:
Fast bowler Gerald Coetzee will replace injured fellow paceman Anrich Nortje in the South African team for the series-deciding third Test against Australia, starting at Newlands on Tuesday.

Australia, meanwhile, are waiting on the fitness of key batsman Steve Smith, who is recovering from a neck injury.

"He's the closest we've got to a like-for-like replacement for Anrich Nortje," South African captain Temba Bavuma said of Coetzee at his pre-match press conference on Monday.

Like Nortje, Coetzee is capable of bowling at speeds of up to 150km/h (93 mph).

And, like Nortje, bowling at high pace has led to lengthy periods on the sidelines because of injuries.

Nortje played in the first two Tests against Australia after a three-year lay-off – and was ruled out of the third Test by a groin injury.

Coetzee last played in the Test team two years ago but played in two of the three one-day internationals between South Africa and Australia last month.

"It's about the balance of the attack," said Bavuma, who said Coetzee and the medium-paced Wiaan Mulder added different strengths to the strike duo of Kagiso Rabada and Marco Jansen.

"Gerald's got that extra bit of pace. You need someone in that enforcer role who can pick up a wicket when the wicket is flat."

Mulder made crucial breakthroughs during South Africa's innings and 31 runs win in the second Test by bowling with tight control. "When you want someone who brings the stumps into play Wiaan comes into the conversation," said Bavuma.

Australia will delay naming their team until the morning of the match but are set to make changes in their batting line-up.

Opening batsman Nic Maddinson has been released from the squad after three failures in four innings. Matt Renshaw, player of the match in Australia's 214-run win in the first Test, is set to return to his accustomed position as an opening batsman after batting at number five in the first two Tests.

Australian captain Pat Cummins said Cameron Green would return in the middle order after recovering from an abdominal injury, while Smith would be given "every chance" to recover from a neck injury which hampered him in the second Test in Gqeberha.

Smith only faced gentle throwdowns on Sunday and his availability depended on how he feels on Tuesday after a more thorough examination in the nets on Monday.

"Hopefully it all goes well and he will be there," said Cummins.

title: Dhaka close in on first NCL win as Amite, Rihad, Fazle hit tons
text:
Dhaka Division moved closer to their first victory in the National Cricket League (NCL) 2026-27 after reducing Rajshahi Division to 215 for five in their second innings, following on, on the third day of the fourth round in Rajshahi on Monday.

Resuming their first innings at 103 for six, Rajshahi added 59 runs before being bowled out for 162. Dhaka, who had posted 521, enforced the follow-on, with pacer Sumon Khan claiming four wickets.

Rajshahi struggled again in their second innings, losing five wickets for 181 runs. Sabbir Hossan scored 52, while Sabbir Rahman remained unbeaten on 64 as Rajshahi ended the day 144 runs behind Dhaka's first-innings total.

In Cox's Bazar, Amite Hasan struck an unbeaten 171 off 296 balls for his 12th first-class century, while Ashraful Hasan Rihad made an unbeaten 101 off 200 balls, his second first-class hundred, as Sylhet Division piled up 575 for four in their first innings.

Resuming at 280 for two, Sylhet lost Zakir Hasan for 160 in the first over of the day. Amite and Rihad then shared an unbroken 222-run partnership for the fifth wicket to put Sylhet in a commanding position. With only one innings completed in the match so far, a draw appears the likeliest outcome.

In Bogura, Chattogram Division reached 424 for six in their first innings against Mymensingh Division, who had resumed the day at 134 for two. Shahadat Hossain Dipu top-scored with 95 off 188 balls, while Tasamul Haque (63), Sabbir Hossain Shikder (54) and Irfan Shukkur (53) also struck half-centuries. Chattogram reduced their first-innings deficit to 41 runs.

Meanwhile, Rangpur Division ended the day at five without loss in their second innings, trailing Barishal Division by 36 runs after the latter declared at 443 for nine.

Resuming at 179 for three, Barishal were powered by Fazle Mahmud's 124 off 200 balls, his 11th first-class century, and Md Abdullah's 67. Fazle also crossed 7,000 first-class runs during his innings. Pacer Mehedi Hasan claimed three wickets for Rangpur.

title: Shoriful fetches 2.3 crore points, highest price in D3 auction
text:
Bangladesh pacer Shoriful Islam fetched the highest price among Category A players at the D3 Trophy Player Auction, with Citizens Bank securing his services for 2.3 crore points at a city hotel on Monday.

Pacer Taskin Ahmed was snapped up by Walton Group for 2.1 crore points, while Fortune secured several national team players, including opener Tanzid Hasan Tamim for 2 crore points, batter Najmul Hossain Shanto for 1.55 crore, all-rounder Soumya Sarkar for 75 lakh and leg-spinner Rishad Hossain for 60 lakh points.

All-rounder Mahedi Hasan was picked by Blue Star for 1.6 crore points, while Litton Das joined Walton for 1.55 crore points.

Seven Rings Cement signed left-arm spinner Taijul Islam for 80 lakh points and left-arm pacer Mustafizur Rahman for 70 lakh points.

Meanwhile, wicketkeeper-batter Jaker Ali joined Citizens Bank for 1.8 crore points.

Each team must pick 22 players during the auction. In addition, the six franchises have already selected one icon player apiece at the tournament's launch ceremony on September 27.

The six teams have a total budget of 10 crore points each, taking the combined auction purse to 60 crore points. A total of 275 players were listed for the auction.

Image

Teams will have to name a 15-member squad for each of the three tournaments, with any changes to those squads to be made from their remaining pool of players.

The six teams will compete in three formats across 42 matches, comprising seven four-day games, 16 one-day matches and 19 T20 fixtures.

The T20 tournament is scheduled to begin on December 15 in Barishal, followed by the four-day and one-day competitions in January and May next year, respectively.

Teams

Team owners: Blue Star, Acme, Citizens Bank, Seven Rings Cement, Fortune and Walton, with ownership rights for three seasons.

Icon players: Mehidy Hasan Miraz (Walton), Towhid Hridoy (Fortune), Mosaddek Hossain (Acme), Mushfiqur Rahim (Seven Rings Cement), Nurul Hasan Sohan (Blue Star) and Mohammad Naim (Citizens Bank).

Head coaches: Mohammad Salahuddin (Fortune), Sohel Islam (Blue Star), Rajin Saleh (Acme), Abdur Razzak (Walton), Hannan Sarkar (Seven Rings Cement) and Mizanur Rahman Babul (Citizens Bank).

title: ‘Is this the first time there's chaos before a match?’
text:
Nothing appears to surprise Bangladesh head coach Phil Simmons anymore.

Having witnessed three changes in the Bangladesh Cricket Board's presidency in a relatively short period, Simmons hardly seemed taken aback when asked about the turbulence surrounding the Tigers ahead of their crucial two-match Test series against West Indies, part of the World Test Championship (WTC).

Bangladesh discontinued batting coach Mohammad Ashraful from his role with the national team just four days before the first Test in Mirpur, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the team's preparations. The Tigers have also had little time to regroup as a full squad, having been occupied with the UAE tri-nation ODI series, from which their exit also drew criticism.

But Simmons was in no mood to dwell on the off-field developments, instead emphasising the importance of preparation and the work that lies ahead.

“You have been in Bangladesh a lot longer than me. You've seen world cricket a lot longer than me. Is this the first time there's chaos before a match? No, right. So every series is important,” Simmons said when asked about the situation ahead of the series.

Asked whether Ashraful's removal was unfair, the Bangladesh coach chose not to comment, saying: “I don't think that's a question for me.”

With Bangladesh currently fourth in the WTC standings and still in contention for a place in the final, Simmons stressed that the team's focus must remain on what happens inside the dressing room rather than the noise surrounding it.

He also highlighted the importance of the final two days of training before the first Test, insisting that the players who had been preparing in Mirpur had shown the right attitude.

“Those that we were playing at the start of this two years were important too. But the thing is how we go about our business, our preparation for the series. And I think that the group that was here have been excellent in the last three or four days. They've been doing their work and now the whole team joins together. It's what we do over the next two days. It's not what's happening outside, it's what we do as a team to prepare,” he added.

Simmons, however, acknowledged that the scheduling had not provided Bangladesh with the ideal build-up to a Test series, particularly given the limited time the entire squad had spent together.

The tri-nation series meant several players involved in both ODI and Test cricket had been occupied with national duties, leaving little room for a full-squad preparation camp. Still, the coach was keen to point out that the players had not been idle.

“We didn't get the whole team because we were in the middle of a series. We were in the middle of a tri-nation series and it just so happens that quite a few of our players who play in both ODI and Test cricket were involved. So no, it's not the total ideal situation, but the guys weren't sitting down, so they were playing cricket. So there's still a lot there. It's just for these two days for us to put things together as a whole squad,” he said.

With the first Test approaching, Simmons' message was clear: Bangladesh may have had to contend with uncertainty off the field, but the immediate priority is to make the most of the time available and ensure the team is ready when the action begins.

title: Bongo secures global digital rights for SAFF Championship
text:
Bangladesh-based OTT platform Bongo has acquired the global digital broadcasting rights for the upcoming SAFF Championship through an agreement with sports marketing agency TSA Sports & Entertainment, allowing football fans worldwide to watch the tournament live, except in India and Pakistan.

The agreement was signed at the SAFF headquarters in Banani, Dhaka, on Tuesday, with SAFF General Secretary Purushottam Kattel, Bongo Chief of Business & Corporate Affairs Mamun Atik and Head of Content Mohammad Haider Ali present at the ceremony, said a press release from Bongo.

The tournament, scheduled to take place in Dhaka from November 4 to 17, will feature six teams. Bongo will stream all matches live on its digital platforms, making the competition accessible to viewers in Bangladesh and abroad, subject to the territorial restrictions.

The platform has also introduced an early-bird offer, allowing viewers to purchase a season pass for Tk 49 to watch the entire tournament. The pass can be purchased through the Bongo website or mobile app using available payment methods.

Matches will be available on the Bongo app for Android and iOS smartphones, Android TV and other major smart TV platforms.

title: SAFF sets Tk 1,000 ticket price, confirms VAR Lite
text:
The SAFF Championship will feature VAR Lite from the final matchday of the group stage, as well as in the semifinals and final, while gallery ticket prices have been set at Tk 1,000 per matchday, the regional body's general secretary Purushottam Kattel confirmed on Wednesday.

Speaking to The Daily Star, Kattel also dismissed rumours about India's non-participation in the tournament, saying that whichever squad the country sends will be treated as its senior national team.

The six-team tournament will run from November 5 to 17 in Dhaka.

“We will use VAR Lite in the semifinals and the final, and also during the last matchday as a test case,” Kattel told The Daily Star over the phone.

VAR Lite is a budget-friendly, simplified version of the standard Video Assistant Referee system approved by FIFA and The IFAB. It is designed for lower-tier leagues and tournaments with smaller budgets or limited broadcast infrastructure.

“We are not able to use the full version of VAR as the facilities at the venue (the National Stadium in Dhaka) do not allow that. The VAR personnel will operate from a remote location,” he said.

Kattel also defended the ticket prices, citing inflation and the rising costs associated with staging the tournament.

The ticketing rights have been awarded to TSA Sports and Entertainment, a Bangladesh-registered sports marketing and event management company. TSA will be responsible for the tournament's marketing, broadcasting, sponsorship, commercial activities, and event management.

Tickets will be available online, on tickify, from Thursday, with a package of two gallery tickets priced at Tk 1000 for each matchday.

Image

“There is inflation, and many other expenses related to organising and staging events, including high airfares, which make it hard for the company to reduce ticket prices,” Kattel said.

Meanwhile, the Nepal-born football official said all matches in the tournament would be recognised as Tier 1 international fixtures by FIFA.

“I don't know where the rumours of India not sending a team originated from. They will definitely play and they submitted a preliminary list,” Kattel said.

He added that some senior Indian players might be unavailable because India are scheduled to play friendly matches against New Zealand during the same period.

“But that is not our concern. All the matches will be of Tier 1 category and we will treat the India team as their senior national team,” he added.

title: Ballon d’Or leak: Kane, Mbappe, Yamal all ‘win’ before final verdict
text:
A series of prematurely published articles naming Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe and Lamine Yamal as the 2026 Ballon d’Or winner sparked confusion online hours before the official ceremony, raising questions over how the award’s organisers had managed to keep the results under wraps.

An article titled “Harry Kane wins the 2026 Ballon d’Or” began circulating online ahead of Monday night’s ceremony, sparking confusion among football fans and raising questions about how the organisers had managed to keep the results secret.

However, further investigation revealed that similar articles had also been prepared for other leading contenders, including Real Madrid’s Kylian Mbappe and Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal.

The incident fuelled speculation on social media, with many questioning whether France Football, the organisers of the prestigious individual award, had accidentally revealed the winner before the ceremony.

The controversy deepened after reports suggested that separate leaked articles had presented Kane, Mbappe and Yamal as the winner of the men’s award.

One of the articles reportedly credited Mbappe’s record-breaking World Cup campaign and prolific goalscoring for Real Madrid as the reasons behind his supposed victory.

Another highlighted Yamal’s remarkable achievements, suggesting that the Barcelona youngster had become the youngest winner in the award’s history at just 19.

But the premature publications did not necessarily indicate the final outcome, as the articles had reportedly been prepared for multiple nominees ahead of the ceremony.

When contacted by BBC Sport, a Ballon d’Or spokesperson clarified that the profiles had been published by mistake.

“Some profiles of nominees prepared by BallonDor.com were inadvertently published online,” the spokesperson said.

“These articles had been prepared for all nominees and should in no way be considered as an indication of the final results or rankings.”

The articles featuring Kane and Mbappe were subsequently removed from the website.

Similar profiles had also been prepared for the women’s award, including those featuring London City Lionesses star Alexia Putellas and Barcelona’s Ewa Pajor. Putellas was later officially confirmed as the winner of the women’s Ballon d’Or.

According to reports, the organisers were left concerned by the incident and were expected to investigate how the articles had appeared online before the official announcement.

The episode added an unexpected twist to the build-up to one of football’s most prestigious award ceremonies, with the premature publications triggering widespread debate over the secrecy surrounding the voting process and the final results.

For Kane, however, the confusion eventually gave way to celebration, as the England captain was officially crowned the men’s Ballon d’Or winner on Monday night.

title: Mbappe, LaLiga apologise to China over Mao Zedong remarks
text:
Mengniu, Shanghai Milkground and Eastroc end cooperation with Mbappe immediately

China state TV reportedly halts LaLiga and Mbappe broadcasts

LaLiga president apologises on X for alleged comments that caused offence in China

Mbappe apologises for 'ill-judged' comment about Mao Zedong

Kylian Mbappe apologised on Tuesday for his "ill-judged" comment about former Chinese leader Mao Zedong, which has led to Chinese brands dropping the Real Madrid forward.

"My comment was ill-judged, and I now understand that it hurt many people in China and in Chinese communities around the world. I apologise to everyone my words have upset," the Frenchman said in a statement.

Meanwhile, Spain's LaLiga on Tuesday condemned and apologised to China over remarks made by Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe, who called former Chinese leader Mao Zedong a "dictator".

"LaLiga deeply regrets the offence that Kylian Mbappe's recent comments have caused among Chinese fans. These comments were made in a personal capacity and do not represent LaLiga," the league said in a statement.

A number of Chinese brands have cut ties with France soccer captain Kylian Mbappe over comments he reportedly made referring to the late Chinese leader Mao Zedong, underscoring how swiftly international celebrities can come unstuck in a crucial market.

In a video that emerged online on Monday, Mbappe is heard saying that the funniest meme he had seen of himself was one where his face had been photoshopped on to that of "some guy — I think he's a Chinese dictator".

Reuters has not been able to authenticate the video.

His comments were believed to be an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the soccer player's face and other historical figures.

In China, satire or jokes about Mao, the country's founding leader who ruled the country from 1949 until his death in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.

"A remark about an internet meme has triggered a backlash among his Chinese fans, threatened his lucrative commercial relationships and offered a sharp reminder of the limits of celebrity influence," state media outlet China Daily said.

The furore makes Mbappe - one of the world's most prominent sports stars who has ties with firms from sportswear brand On Holding 49G.BN to hotel chain Accor ACCP.PA and toy maker Lego - the latest to fall foul of a faux pas in China.

Other leading firms and organizations that have previously incurred the wrath of Beijing, netizens and Chinese media include fashion brand Dolce & Gabbana, Swiss watchmaker Swatch and the National Basketball Association.

'WHAT DID HE SAY?'

Many Chinese media outlets on Tuesday condemned Mbappe's apparent remarks, but did not repeat them.

"What did he say? Many Chinese would rather not repeat it," the state-backed Global Times said.

"The message from Chinese consumers is clear: Respect is not optional; one doesn't get to profit from China while disrespecting it. Not a chance."

Brands including dairy companies Mengniu 2319.HK and Shanghai Milkground Food Tech 600882.SS as well as Eastroc Beverage 605499.SS said they were ceasing all cooperation with Mbappe, who plays his club soccer for Real Madrid, effective immediately.

The companies said they "firmly oppose and have zero tolerance for any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people."

China's state television has halted broadcasts of all matches and events involving LaLiga and Mbappe, and all advertisements involving Mbappe have been removed, state-backed media outlet the Paper reported on Tuesday.

Mbappe's representatives did not immediately respond to a request for comment. His club Real Madrid declined to comment.

Spain's LaLiga did not immediately respond to a request for comment, but its president, Javier Tebas, issued an apology on X and said that the organization deeply regretted the alleged comments that "have caused discomfort and offence in China".

"We are taking the measures within our reach and working directly with our partners and interlocutors in China to overcome this situation," Tebas wrote. "A relationship built over so many years cannot be damaged by a single episode."

Denmark's Lego, which has a Mbappe building set on sale in China, said it could not comment. The Mbappe set still featured on Lego's Chinese website on Tuesday. On Holding and Accor did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

TRENDING ON WEIBO

As of 0700 GMT, four topics related to Mbappe were still among the top 10 trending searches on China's social media platform Weibo. Some netizens called for China to "blacklist" Mbappe and reduce his commercial value to zero. These comments received hundreds of likes.

Fans have been creating memes superimposing Mbappe's face on images of military and political leaders to suggest that he has the power to influence decisions at the teams he plays for.

In an interview with L'Equipe last month, Mbappe said that while some aspects of the meme trend were harmless fun, the viral ones depicting him as a dictator showed "a lack of political and human awareness."

When asked about the incident, a spokesperson for China's Foreign Ministry said that words and actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people "will naturally be met with joint opposition from all sectors of Chinese society."

title: ‘Cubarsi deserved it’: Yamal’s heartfelt words for Barca teammate after Kopa hattrick
text:
Lamine Yamal may have made history with his third consecutive Kopa Trophy, but the Barcelona sensation had a special word of praise for teammate Pau Cubarsi, admitting he would have loved to see the young defender take home the prestigious award.

“I would have liked Cubarsi to have won, he deserves it, he has been great for a long time,” Yamal said after receiving the award.

The 19-year-old winger became the first footballer in the history of the award to win it three times in a row, further cementing his reputation as one of the most exciting talents in world football.

Named after French football legend Raymond Kopa, the trophy recognises the best player aged under 21. Established by France Football in 2018, it has become a coveted prize for emerging stars, with Barcelona enjoying considerable success in the category.

Yamal, who previously won the award in 2024 and 2025, continued his remarkable run by claiming the 2026 edition. His latest triumph came after another influential campaign with Barcelona, during which he played a key role in the club’s La Liga and Spanish Super Cup successes.

Image

However, despite his individual achievement, the winger was quick to acknowledge Cubarsi’s contribution and growing reputation.

The 19-year-old defender was among the nominees and has established himself as a dependable presence at the heart of Barcelona’s defence. His composure, tactical awareness and maturity have earned him recognition well beyond his age.

Yamal’s comments reflected the strong bond between the teammates, who have also represented Spain together on the international stage.

At the awards ceremony in London, Yamal received the trophy from Ukrainian football great Andriy Shevchenko.

“It's an honour to receive this award,” Yamal said. “I am very happy and I want to thank my club, the national team, everyone.”

The Barcelona number 10's words offered a glimpse of the humility behind his growing list of individual accolades.

His performances throughout the 2025-26 season have been instrumental in Barcelona’s success. Across 45 appearances, he registered 24 goals and 18 assists, demonstrating his ability to hurt opponents both as a finisher and as a creator.

He also earned the Best Player in La Liga award after contributing 16 goals and 11 assists in the domestic competition, finishing as the league’s leading assist provider.

On the international stage, Yamal was part of Spain’s World Cup-winning campaign, featuring in eight matches and scoring once.

Despite finishing third in the Ballon d’Or rankings behind Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe, Yamal has continued to collect honours at an extraordinary rate.

title: Spain dominate Ballon d’Or night
text:
Spain dominated the 2026 Ballon d’Or awards, claiming eight of the 13 honours at Monday's ceremony in London, despite England captain Harry Kane taking home the men’s top prize.

The Spanish sweep across individual and team categories underlined the country’s strength in both men’s and women’s football, from established stars to emerging talents, goalkeepers and coaches. Kane, however, ended England’s 25-year wait for a men’s Ballon d’Or winner, becoming the first Englishman since Michael Owen in 2001 to receive the prestigious award.

Alexia Putellas headlined Spain’s success by winning the Women’s Ballon d’Or for the third time, adding to her triumphs in 2021 and 2022. The midfielder, who joined London City Lionesses ahead of the 2026-27 season, was recognised following an outstanding campaign with Barcelona, helping the club win the UEFA Women’s Champions League.

Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal claimed the men’s young player award for the third consecutive year, while Vicky López won the women’s equivalent for the second successive time.

Spain’s dominance extended to the coaching and goalkeeping categories. National team coach Luis de la Fuente was named men’s coach of the year, while Barcelona boss Pere Romeu received the women’s award. Unai Simón won the men’s goalkeeper honour, with Barcelona’s Cata Coll taking the women’s prize.

Barcelona Femení were named women’s club of the year after another trophy-laden season, completing Spain’s haul across the major categories. Paris Saint-Germain, however, claimed the men’s club award.

Kane’s victory was the main exception to Spain’s dominance. The Bayern Munich striker scored 73 goals for club and country during the 2025-26 campaign, helping the German champions retain their Bundesliga title and win a domestic treble. He finished ahead of France’s Kylian Mbappé, with Yamal third.

The results highlighted Spain’s influence across the modern game, with the country’s success extending beyond its senior stars to youth development, coaching and women’s football.

• Women's Ballon d'Or: Alexia Putellas (London City Lionesses/Spain) won her third career title.

• Men's Coach of the Year: Luis de la Fuente won after guiding Spain to the 2026 World Cup.

• Women's Coach of the Year: Pere Romeu won after a quadruple-winning season with Barcelona Femení.

• Men's Young Player of the Year (Trophy): Lamine Yamal claimed his third consecutive title.

• Women's Young Player of the Year (Trophy): Vicky López secured her second straight award.

• Men's Goalkeeper of the Year (Yashin Trophy): Unai Simón won for his exploits with Spain.

• Women's Goalkeeper of the Year: Cata Coll won for her performances with Spain and Barcelona Femení.

• Women's Club of the Year: Barcelona Femení swept Liga F, Copa de la Reina, Spanish Super Cup, and the UEFA Women's Champions League.

title: Why Pele and Maradona never won a Ballon d'Or
text:
The list of Ballon d’Or winners features some of the greatest names in world football, including Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo, Michel Platini, Johan Cruyff, Franz Beckenbauer, Eusébio, Zinedine Zidane and Ronaldo Nazario.

Now, Harry Kane can be added to that list. Yet two of football’s all-time greats, Argentina’s Diego Maradona and Brazil’s Pelé, never had the opportunity to win the prestigious award.

Why? Because the Ballon d’Or was originally reserved for European players and was often referred to as the European Footballer of the Year award. That rule remained in place from the inaugural edition in 1956 until 1995, when the award was opened to players of any nationality playing for a European club.

Image

Consequently, the first non-European winner emerged in 1995, when Liberian striker George Weah, then playing for AC Milan, claimed the prize.

Since then, Brazilian stars Ronaldo, Ronaldinho, Rivaldo and Kaká, along with Messi, have joined the list of winners.

In 2007, the award was opened to players of any nationality playing for clubs anywhere in the world.

Under the original eligibility rules, however, Pelé and Maradona never had a chance to compete for the Ballon d’Or.

Pelé, who died in December 2022 at the age of 82, ended his playing career with the New York Cosmos in 1977, nearly two decades before the award was first won by a non-European.

Image Photo: Collected

Maradona, meanwhile, spent 11 years playing in Europe with Barcelona, Napoli and Sevilla before returning to Argentina in 1993 for the final four seasons of his career. By then, his powers were waning, following a 15-month ban in 1991 after he tested positive for cocaine.

title: From injury to glory: Putellas claims third Ballon d’Or
text:
Alexia Putellas picked up her third Ballon d'Or in her new home city of London on Monday, crowning a spectacular return to the top of women's football after injury cut her down in her prime.

Putellas previously picked up the prize for the best player in the world in 2021 and 2022 as the creative heartbeat of an all-conquering Barcelona side.

But an anterior cruciate ligament tear just as she was preparing for Spain's bid to win Euro 2022 derailed her rise to global stardom.

Putellas recovered to play a bit part role in Spain's World Cup triumph a year later, but was overshadowed by team-mate Aitana Bonmati for both club and country as it took nearly two years to rediscover her best form.

"Ever since I suffered the injury, I've been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it'll happen again," Putellas told AFP in an interview last month.

Bonmati took on the mantle of the world's best player, becoming a three-time Ballon d'Or winner between 2023 and 2025 until she was also sidelined by a leg break.

With the emphasis back on Putellas, she rose to the challenge, helping Barcelona regain the Champions League last season in dominant fashion.

"I never felt that the (Ballon d'Or) trophy was 'mine'... Having already experienced it once, I’m able to enjoy it even more now," she added.

Having achieved all that she could in Catalonia, Putellas embarked on a new adventure, joining London City Lionesses.

Owned by American businesswoman Michele Kang, the Lionesses are aiming to break the mould as the only fully independent team in England's top division.

"It's a complete change in my life. It's a constant, daily learning process: the culture, the language, moving to a new country, a new city," said the 32-year-old.

"I knew that if I ever had to end my time at Barca, it wouldn't make much sense to repeat what I'd already experienced in the next chapter, mainly because it's impossible.

"It had to be something completely different. It's practically a brand-new club, with everything yet to be written, so I'm trying to bring that winning culture and mentality with me."

The Putellas effect is already being felt in the English Women's Super League with the Lionesses sat just behind Chelsea and Manchester City at the top of the table and ahead of traditional giants Arsenal.

The move could also benefit Spain's chances of retaining the World Cup next year with their star player facing a lesser workload without European football this season.

"It was one of the things I took into account. There’s a long way to go, and my focus is on the day-to-day, but I also believe that these kinds of environments are what will prepare me to perform at my best," she said.

For now, there is a Ballon d’Or to savor and a new life in London to build.

title: The former goalkeeper eyeing No 9 spot
text:
Rafayel Tudu has made a habit of making an impact when it matters, even if his opportunities have been limited.

The Fortis FC forward scored in consecutive AFC Challenge League matches after coming off the bench, adding to a return of two goals and an assist in three Bangladesh Football League (BFL) appearances this season, all as a substitute.

Having come a long way from his days as a goalkeeper, the 25-year-old now wants to turn those cameos into a regular starting role and eventually claim Bangladesh’s No 9 spot.

Rafayel came on in the 91st minute against Al Qadsia, but made his mark in the next two matches. He scored in the 78th minute against FC Goa to draw Fortis level at 1-1, before they eventually lost 2-1. Against Regar-TadAZ, he entered at the start of the second half and found the net again as Fortis secured their first win in the main stage of the competition.

“I do not want to remain a substitute throughout my career. I want to play in the starting XI,” Rafayel told The Daily Star over the phone from his village home on Monday.

His path to becoming a forward was anything but conventional. The player from Amtalipara village in Godagari, Rajshahi, began training as a goalkeeper at Rajshahi Kishore Football Academy around 2018. After moving to Dhaka in 2020-21 to join Victoria Sporting Club in the Bangladesh Championship League, he found himself third or fourth in the goalkeeping pecking order, with few chances to play.

Back in Rajshahi, he began featuring as a striker in local tournaments and kept asking his academy coach to give him a chance up front. A goal against the academy’s team in a local tournament eventually persuaded the coach to make the switch permanent.

Image

The gamble paid off at Fakirerpool in the 2023-24 season. After missing his first few matches, Rafayel scored four goals against Uttara FC and went on to finish as the Championship League’s top scorer and best player. Fakirerpool won the title and earned promotion to the Bangladesh Premier League, now known as the BFL. Rafayel subsequently moved to Mohammedan before joining Fortis, where he has found a platform to test himself against opposition from across Asia.

The recent goals have showcased his attacking instincts, though he is clear-eyed about what he needs to improve.

“Moving forward, finding attacking positions and finishing chances are among my strengths. I am comfortable in one-on-one situations with the goalkeeper, and physical contests and pressing do not trouble me much,” he said. “My first touch needs improvement. Sometimes I could control the ball better and move more quickly.”

Rafayel was disappointed not to be included in Bangladesh’s preliminary squad for the SAFF Championship, as a call-up would have made him only the third player from the Santal community, after Hemanta Vincent Biswas and MS Bablu, to be called up for the men’s senior national team. However, he says the omission will not distract him from his work.

“I would have liked an opportunity, but I will remain prepared and keep working. I will also support Bangladesh because it is my country,” he said.

For Rafayel, the ambition extends beyond securing a place in the starting XI at club level. He wants to become the centre-forward Bangladesh have been searching for.

“I believe Bangladesh need a proper centre-forward, and I want to fill that gap. If I get an opportunity on merit, I want to help end the country’s goal-scoring problems.”

title: Mbappe loses Chinese sponsorship deals over apparent Mao Zedong joke
text:
Kylian Mbappe was dropped Tuesday by two major brands in China after a video circulated online in which the French football star apparently joked about former leader Mao Zedong.

In China jokes about Mao, the country's founding leader who died in 1976, are considered disrespectful and remain a social taboo.

"Our company firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any behaviour that offends national sentiments," drinks giant Dongpeng said in a statement, adding that "with immediate effect we are terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe".

Mengniu, China's largest dairy producer, also cut ties with the Real Madrid and France forward.

"With immediate effect our company is terminating all cooperation with Kylian Mbappe," Mengniu said in a statement.

"Mengniu firmly opposes and has a zero-tolerance policy towards any words or actions that hurt the feelings of the Chinese people," it added.

The announcements came after a video emerged online with Mbappe saying that the funniest internet meme he had seen was of his face photoshopped onto that of "some guy -- I think he's a Chinese dictator".

This was an apparent reference to a meme of Mbappe superimposed on an image of Mao, one of several using the footballer's face and other historical figures.

The authenticity of the video could not immediately be verified by AFP Fact Check.

"Dongpeng Beverage ends cooperation with Mbappe" was the top-trending topic on Chinese social media site Weibo.

One Weibo user said that the "extremely serious wrong remarks... crossed the red line. They are completely unacceptable".

Others urged Dongpeng to remove Mbappe's image from their energy drink bottles.

Dongqiudi, one of China's biggest online football outlets, said in a statement on Monday evening that Mbappe’s remarks were "offensive to China and the Chinese people" and "have hurt the feelings of Chinese football fans and the Chinese people".

Mbappe addressed the memes depicting him as historical figures, including strongmen leaders, in an interview with French sports newspaper L'Equipe in September.

"There's a part of it that's funny. You can tell that, for some people, it's all in good fun. But there is another part that's a bit less funny because of the damage such people have caused throughout history," he said.

"Being compared to individuals who murder others, or who have brought misery to millions upon millions of people -- well, I don't think I've ever done anything like that in my life," he said.





The furore in China came a day after 27-year-old Mbappe lost out to Harry Kane for the Ballon d'Or, the world's most prestigious individual award in football.

title: Svitolina announces end of marriage to Monfils as Ukrainian cites toll of war
text:
World number six Elina Svitolina said on Monday that she and former tennis player Gael Monfils were ending their marriage, with the Ukrainian adding that the emotional toll of Russia's war in her homeland left her needing to rediscover herself.

The couple married in July 2021 and welcomed a daughter, Skai, in October 2022.

Announcing the separation in an Instagram post, Svitolina described the personal struggles she has faced since Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022 and the impact they had on her life away from the tennis court.

"This is the most difficult thing I have ever had to share," Svitolina wrote. "Everyone knows how much Ukraine means to me. What I have rarely spoken about is what the war has done to me inside.

"Last year, I told you I needed to step away from the court because I wasn't in the right emotional space. Today, I want to open up a little more. What you didn't see were the sleepless nights, the doubts, and the feeling of slowly losing myself.

"Gael saw all of it. He never let go of my hand. We fought through this together for a long time, with everything we had. But some battles happen deep inside you, and no amount of love from someone else can win them for you."

Svitolina asked for kindness and privacy as the family navigates the separation, stressing there was no one to blame.

"With time, I came to understand that I need to find my way back to myself and that I cannot do that within our marriage," the 32-year-old Australian Open semi-finalist added.

"It is the hardest truth I have ever had to face and the hardest thing I have ever had to tell the person I love.

"Gael listened. He has respected what I need with a strength and grace I will never forget. Gael has loved me through my greatest joys and my darkest moments, and I have loved him with all my heart...

"Skai will always come first. Our marriage is ending, but our family is not. We will always be her parents, side by side, at every step of her life...

"There are only two people who loved each other deeply and a story that is changing shape."

On the court, four-times Grand Slam semifinalist Svitolina recently secured her place at the season-ending WTA Finals in Indian Wells, California.

Frenchman Monfils, 40, a former world number six and one of the most charismatic players of his generation, has retired from professional tennis, according to the International Tennis Integrity Agency.

He planned to retire at the end of 2026 and bid farewell at November's Paris Masters but the ITIA now lists him as retired.

title: Alexander Zverev to become new world number one
text:
Men's tennis confirmed it will crown a new world number one as Germany's Alexander Zverev was ensured the year-end honour on Monday after Carlos Alcaraz lost his third-round match in Shanghai.

The career-first will cap a stellar season for the 29-year-old, the current world number two, after he won the French Open in June and the US Open in September.

The French Open was his first-ever Grand Slam title.

"It's been a fantastic season for me winning in Paris and New York and knowing that I will finish the year on top of the rankings is just a dream come true," Zverev said in a statement shared by the ATP Tour website.

"So much work and effort have been put into achieving this goal, especially after coming back from the ankle injury," Zverev added.

He suffered a career-threatening ankle injury in his French Open semi-final in 2022.

Zverev will be the first German male player to finish his season as top-ranked in the world, and the oldest to lift the trophy, set to be presented in November, for the first time.

Germany's Angelique Kerber and Steffi Graf have both been the year-end number one women's tennis player.

Zverev's achievement comes in a year where the previous two players to hold the top ranking, Italy's Jannik Sinner and Spain's Alcaraz, have skipped months of competition due to injury.

Sinner, the current number one, has not competed since Wimbledon where he beat Zverev in the final. He announced last week his season was over due to a knee injury.

Alcaraz, ranked third, was sidelined for months with a wrist injury from April until the US Open.

Zverev, 6-foot-6 (1.98m), had been destined for the top from a young age, hailing from a tennis family where his mother and father both played the sport to a high level in the former Soviet Union.

But he plays in the shadow of domestic violence allegations made by two former partners, which he has strenuously denied.

The ATP Tour investigated one claim and found insufficient evidence to punish Zverev.

Another led to a 2023 penalty order and fine from a German court which later dropped the case after a settlement was agreed in June of 2024 -- hours before he was due to play in the French Open semi-finals.

title: Djokovic crashes out of Shanghai Masters in his first match
text:
Novak Djokovic went down in straight sets to Hubert Hurkacz on Friday, exiting the Shanghai Masters in his first match after memorably winning the China Open this week.

Hurkacz, the 2023 Shanghai champion and world number 34, beat Djokovic 6-4, 6-3 in the second round as the 39-year-old faltered against his big-serving opponent a decade his junior.

The former world number one turned in a disappointing performance just three days after claiming the 102nd professional title of his career in Beijing, where he has never lost a match.

It was Hurkacz's first victory against the Serbian veteran in nine meetings, and he sent down 13 aces across the one-hour-and-28-minute encounter.

Djokovic, who has struggled for fitness in recent months, hunched over and squatted down between points on a cool Shanghai evening while his opponent sprinted across the court.

Djokovic double-faulted in the fourth game of the second set to give Hurkacz a 3-1 lead, and the Pole held serve through his win.

Hurkacz will face either Italy's Lorenzo Musetti or Chinese wildcard Zhou Yi in the third round.

title: Alcaraz, Sinner set for '1 Point Slam'
text:
The Australian Open will revive its innovative "1 Point Slam" in 2027 with Carlos Alcaraz, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Jannik Sinner among those agreeing to take part Thursday.

The sudden-death contest was played for the first time at Melbourne Park this year ahead of the opening Grand Slam of the year, pitting 24 professionals alongside 24 amateurs and celebrity wildcards.

Each match consisted of just one point -- win and you advanced, lose and you were out.

Against the odds, amateur Jordan Smith sensationally upset the star-studded field at a packed Rod Laver Arena to collect a Aus$1 million (US$670,000) prize.

"It creates an opportunity for grassroots tennis players to share the spotlight with some of the biggest names in the game," said Tennis Australia's Tom Larner.

"Having stars like Carlos Alcaraz, Coco Gauff, Naomi Osaka and Jannik Sinner locked in to play, alongside everyday Australians ... captures exactly what this event is about, bringing people together through tennis."

The amateur field will again comprise winners of eight state championship rounds played across Australia, along with eight others who come through qualifying.

More than 1.3 million fans attended the 2026 Australian Open, and organisers are planning to increase viewing capacity and seating even further for the 2027 tournament which runs from January 17-31.

title: Alcaraz, Djokovic clinch titles in Tokyo and Beijing
text:
Carlos Alcaraz and Novak Djokovic produced contrasting victories on Tuesday as the two tennis stars returned from injuries in impressive fashion with title wins in Tokyo and Beijing.

In Tokyo, top seed Carlos Alcaraz successfully defended his Japan Open title, defeating Czech Republic's Jiri Lehecka 7-6 (7-4), 6-4 to claim his first trophy since returning from a four-month injury layoff.

The victory was Alcaraz's third title of the year and the 27th singles title of his career. It was also his second tournament since recovering from a wrist injury, following his run to the US Open quarter-finals.

Alcaraz admitted he was unsure how quickly he would rediscover his best form after returning from injury.

"I don't want to take anything for granted," the Spaniard said. "I didn't know if I was going to win a tournament this soon or if I was going to win a tournament this season."

The 22-year-old said his focus was simply on giving his best at each tournament rather than setting expectations.

"I just want to arrive at a tournament, give my best, try to play my best and let's see how the tournament goes," he added.

Against Lehecka, Alcaraz was forced to work hard from the beginning after being broken in the opening game. He recovered with a break of his own before edging a closely contested first set in a tiebreak.

Lehecka continued to challenge the defending champion in the second set, but Alcaraz eventually secured a crucial break and held his nerve to close out the match.

The triumph was particularly meaningful for Alcaraz because it came on the same Tokyo court where he won last year despite suffering an ankle injury in the opening game of his tournament.

"Winning the tournament after my injury, back to back here, it means a lot," Alcaraz said. "Everything I've done to be in this position, everything I've worked for, for this moment, it feels even more special."

Meanwhile, in Beijing, Novak Djokovic claimed his seventh China Open title after Australia's Alex de Minaur was forced to retire with a groin injury.

Djokovic won the opening set 7-6 (7-3) before de Minaur took a medical timeout. The Australian returned with his left thigh heavily bandaged and managed to win the opening game of the second set, but was unable to continue.

De Minaur, the fifth seed, apologised to the fans during the trophy presentation.

"I don't feel great ... I want to say sorry to all the amazing fans," he said. "I didn't want to finish like this... hopefully see you next year."

For sixth-seeded Djokovic, the victory extended his remarkable record at the tournament to 34 consecutive wins and ensured that he has won at least one singles title in every season for 21 consecutive years.

The 39-year-old Serbian continues to show remarkable longevity at the top level, adding another milestone to an already extraordinary career.

The contrasting finals highlighted the different paths taken by the two champions. Alcaraz battled through a competitive two-set match to prove that he is quickly regaining his best level after injury, while Djokovic benefited from de Minaur's unfortunate retirement.

Alcaraz, who also competed at the Laver Cup in London last week, was scheduled to travel to Shanghai for the Masters event. He said his Tokyo title gave him confidence despite admitting he was still some way from his best.

"I think at this tournament I was way far from my best level," Alcaraz said. "But in terms of finding solutions and playing the best level that I could in the most important moments, I think it was a great week."

With both Alcaraz and Djokovic adding titles to their remarkable seasons, their victories in Tokyo and Beijing offered another reminder of the depth of experience and resilience among the game's biggest stars.

title: World No.1 Sinner's season over due to knee injury
text:
World number one Jannik Sinner will not compete again in 2026 after opting to continue his recovery from a knee injury that has sidelined him since his triumphant Wimbledon campaign in July, the Italian said on Tuesday.

Sinner has not played since beating Alexander Zverev in the All England Club final on July 12, with the 25-year-old missing the North American hardcourt swing, the US Open as well as the ongoing slate of tournaments in Asia.

He will now miss the European indoor hardcourt swing as well as the season-ending ATP Finals in Turin, where he won the title in the last two years.

"Me, together with the doctors, have decided that I need a course of treatment for my knee which means the 2026 season is officially over," Sinner said in a video posted on X.

"The last couple of years, especially the ending in Turin, gave me so many beautiful feelings and emotions which this year is going to be way different.

"But at the moment, I also need to think about my long-term career. So I'll do everything possible to get back 100%."

Sinner's team said in a statement that he would follow a course of treatment for inflammation in his knee.

"The decision has been made to have the treatment now to give Jannik the necessary time to recover before beginning preparations for 2027," it added.

Sinner's absence could open the door for Zverev to finish the year at the top of the world rankings. The German world number two has cut the gap to Sinner after winning the French Open and US Open titles.

title: Medvedev says 'terribly sorry' for hitting fan with ball
text:
Novak Djokovic advanced to the China Open final on Monday after Daniil Medvedev was disqualified in the second set, when a ball that came off the Russian's racquet hit a spectator.

A man sitting in the stands behind Medvedev's side of the court was seen holding his face and escorted out of his seat after being hit, as Djokovic was serving for the match with the score at 7-5, 5-3.

Eleventh-ranked Djokovic will play world number nine Alex de Minaur for the title on Tuesday in Beijing.

The Australian had advanced over Hubert Hurkacz after the 29-year-old from Poland retired from their semi-final with an adductor strain.

Medvedev hit the ball with a backhand at the edge of the stands when he failed to return a point, with the chair umpire stopping play.

"Terribly sorry to the spectator, first of all," he told reporters afterwards, adding it was "100 percent an accident" and that he wished to apologise to the fan in person.

It had been a physical battle before Medvedev's disqualification.

A valiant Djokovic, 39, put on a dazzling performance and saved 16 break points, diving at the baseline and sprinting to the net.

"I didn't see what happened, to be honest," he told the crowd afterwards.

"I'm sure that Daniil didn't... do it intentionally. It happened by accident. Sorry for the crowd," he said, adding that it had been a tough match.

Djokovic was red-faced and hunched over between points, with both players forcing each other through gruelling rallies, until the Serbian took control in the second set.

Image

Earlier in the women's draw, former world number one Iga Swiatek staged a comeback to advance to the last 16, while home hope Zheng Qinwen survived another three-set test.

Swiatek overcame frustration to cling on as her opponent served for the set, dominating a must-win tie-break to beat Croatia's Donna Vekic 4-6, 7-6 (7/0), 6-2.

"I was just angry, wanted to change something, because clearly it wasn't working," the 25-year-old from Poland said on court.

"Sometimes if you care a bit less because you're... probably going to lose, it also helps you a bit," she later told reporters.

She will face American teenager Iva Jovic for a spot in the quarter-finals.

- 'Gave everything' -

China's Zheng was tested by Marie Bouzkova, enduring her third three-setter of the tournament to beat the Czech player 7-6 (7/3), 4-6, 7-5.

Zheng voiced frustration in each set at movement outside the court, including as she tried to salvage the second set on Bouzkova's serve.

But she pulled out some of her most accurate tennis to clinch the last two games and win the match when 27th-ranked Bouzkova fired long.

"I gave everything," said Zheng, who had already spent more than five hours on court in the first two rounds.

"Truthfully speaking, I felt a lot of pressure today," the 23-year-old told her home crowd, thanking fans for their support.

Zheng, the current world number 54, next plays 118th-ranked Alina Charaeva, who sent out top seed Elena Rybakina in the second round.

Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova also advanced and will face Ekaterina Alexandrova in the last 16.

title: Battling Djokovic stuns top seed Zverev
text:
