Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to oust Alexander Zverev from the China Open on Sunday, beating the top seed 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up a blockbuster semi-final with Daniil Medvedev.

The 39-year-old Serbian electrified a packed crowd in Beijing, where he extended an astonishing winning streak to 32 matches and is a firm fan favourite.

He got off to a poor start, double-faulting twice in the first game to help Zverev, a decade his junior, break serve instantly.

Boos filled the stadium soon afterwards when the umpire agreed to replay a point Djokovic had won, after Zverev complained about a flicker in the LED panels during play.

The German saw out the first set from there, but a valiant Djokovic roared back to seal the second with a cross-court winner to break serve and force a decider.

The 24-time Grand Slam champion faced 19 Zverev aces throughout the match but held steady on his own serve to go 5-4 ahead in the final set.

He then broke the world number two to take the set and the match, seemingly defying his recent physical difficulties with victory in a gruelling two hours and 34 minutes.

Djokovic will face Medvedev in the final four after the former world number one dispatched Francisco Cerundolo 7-6 (7/4), 6-3.

Poland's Hubert Hurkacz also advanced to the semi-finals after beating Karen Khachanov, and will play Australia's Alex de Minaur who survived a gruelling test to beat Andrey Rublev 1-6, 6-2, 6-3.



Image Photo: AFP

- Sabalenka swept out -

Aryna Sabalenka was swatted aside in straight sets in the third round, leaving the women's draw without its top two seeds.

Czech player Nikola Bartunkova, 20, sent down four aces to beat the former world number one 6-4, 6-3 in one hour and 35 minutes.

"I focused on myself, to be calm," 34th-ranked Bartunkova said.

"She's a legend... so I'm really happy that I won the match," she said of the four-time Grand Slam champion.

Bartunkova next faces Austria's Sinja Kraus in the round of 16.

A frustrated Sabalenka tossed her racquet at a break down in the fourth game of the second set, and lost on the first match point when she returned into the net.

Top seed Elena Rybakina -- who replaced Sabalenka as world number one weeks ago -- is also out, having lost to Alina Charaeva in the second round.

French Open champion Mirra Andreeva of Russia set up a fourth-round match with Ukraine's Daria Snigur, while Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova breezed past Viktorija Golubic 6-2, 6-1.

Noskova next faces 28th-ranked Russian player Ekaterina Alexandrova.

Naomi Osaka, the 2019 champion, beat Sara Bejlek and will face either Karolina Muchova or Liudmila Samsonova, scheduled to play each other Sunday night.

title: Zverev, Agassi defend 'spectacular' Laver Cup
text:
Grand Slam champion Alexander Zverev and American legend Andre Agassi led a staunch defence of the Laver Cup ahead of the latest edition of the polarising event in London this week.

In the midst of the packed tennis calendar, Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Taylor Fritz and rising stars Rafael Jodar and Jakub Mensik are among the stars appearing in the exhibition at the O2 Arena from Friday to Sunday.

The Laver Cup is a three-day tournament on hard courts, pitting players from Europe against opponents from the rest of the world in a rare team event in a sport dominated by singles competition.

Although the Davis Cup is well established as the number one team competition in tennis, the Laver Cup was launched in 2017 as the brainchild of Roger Federer and Tennis Australia.

The plan was to emulate the drama of golf's Ryder Cup -- which featured teams from the United States and Europe.

Unlike the Ryder Cup, the Laver Cup has yet to capture the imagination of the sporting public.

There are also concerns about cramming another tournament in the already hectic schedule for players at risk of burnout.

But to hear two-time major winner Zverev, and Agassi, who is serving as captain of Team World, speak with such conviction about the Laver Cup tells a different story.

"It's really exciting. The arena is spectacular. It is one of the great events of the year," Agassi told reporters in London on Wednesday.

Agassi, an eight-time Grand Slam champion, added: "All these players are out there, maybe on some level trying to impress each other.

"The competition and intensity is always high."

- 'I try to be loyal' -

World number two Zverev could have been forgiven for opting out of the Laver Cup after winning the US Open on September 13 to cap a golden year.

The 29-year-old German, who had never won a major until this year, wanted to show solidarity with an event that has supported him in the past.

"The Laver Cup is something I always try to play. I am a person that values loyalty quite a lot and the event has been loyal to me. I try to be loyal to them," said Zverev, who will be with seven-time Grand Slam winner Alcaraz on Team Europe.

"I enjoy being here. I enjoy being among these team-mates, great guys. I hope to have a great week."

Just four years ago, Britain's Arthur Fery was in the stands at the O2 watching Novak Djokovic in the Laver Cup and now he is part of the show himself.

Fery is an alternate for Team Europe -- on standby to compete if any players are ruled out -- and his presence at the event is the latest milestone in his remarkable rise.

The 24-year-old burst onto the scene with a remarkable run to the Wimbledon semi-finals as a wildcard in July.

"Really pleased to be here. I've had a really good year. It's something that has come with the good results," he said.

"It's amazing to be around all these tennis greats. It's going to be great to be around those guys here. Spend some time with them and pick their brains.

"It's all a little surreal obviously. I am taking the positives out of it and trying to feel like I belong here," he said.

title: Alcaraz quizzes Zverev about US Open championship point
text:
Alexander Zverev has revealed to rival Carlos Alcaraz what was going through his head as he served for the US Open title in New York earlier this month — absolutely nothing.

Zverev secured his first title at Flushing Meadows with a four-set victory over Ben Shelton but returned to the baseline as if to prepare for another game after his American opponent hit long on championship point.

"I thought it was 4-1," Zverev said after Alcaraz quizzed him about the moment as the Team Europe teammates prepared for the Laver Cup on Tuesday.

"If it were 5-2, I'd have been so nervous, for sure.

"There was completely nothing in my head. This is what helps, you know? When you're stupid, it helps," Zverev added with a laugh.

Alcaraz, who exited in the quarter-finals, said he could not understand what was going on.

"I was watching at home and I was like, 'what the heck?," said the Spaniard.

Team Europe, captained by Yannick Noah, are attempting to reclaim the Laver Cup after last year's defeat by Team World in San Francisco.

The three-day event begins on Friday in London and will also feature Casper Ruud, Flavio Cobolli, Jakub Mensik and Rafael Jodar for the Europeans.

Andre Agassi's Team World features Taylor Fritz, Learner Tien, Brandon Nakashima, Alex de Minaur, Alexander Bublik and Francisco Cerundolo.

title: Bangladesh women’s kabaddi team out of Commonwealth medal race in Gujarat
text:
Bangladesh’s women’s kabaddi team were knocked out of the medal race at the Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship after suffering a 31-20 defeat to Sri Lanka at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex in Ahmedabad, Gujarat on Monday.

A second defeat in three matches left Bangladesh third in the five-team group with two points, four behind leaders Sri Lanka, who have six points from four matches, and two behind Kenya, who have four points from two matches.

Only the top two teams will advance to the semifinals, securing at least bronze medals.

Bangladesh trailed 15-9 at half-time and failed to recover in the must-win match, being all out twice against Sri Lanka.

title: Men fall, women rise as Bangladesh endure mixed day
text:
Bangladesh endured mixed fortunes at the Commonwealth Kabaddi Championship in Ahmedabad, India, on Sunday, as the men suffered a narrow defeat to Kenya while the women bounced back with a commanding victory over Scotland.

The men's team went down 32-31 to Kenya at the Veer Savarkar Sports Complex, extending their disappointing run following a poor showing at the recently concluded Asian Games in Japan.

Bangladesh had made a flying start to their campaign on Saturday, thrashing Canada 67-28, but failed to maintain that momentum against Kenya, who had lost twice to Bangladesh at the Bangabandhu Cup in Dhaka.

The defeat left Bangladesh second in the six-team standings, with Kenya leading the table. However, the championship is missing several of the world's leading kabaddi nations, including Iran, Chinese Taipei, South Korea, Nepal and Pakistan. Pakistan, despite being a Commonwealth member, did not participate in the championship in India.

In the women's section, Bangladesh registered their first win of the tournament with an emphatic 75-15 victory over Scotland.

Having lost 34-25 to Kenya in their opening match, Bangladesh will face joint leaders Sri Lanka today in a crucial encounter. A victory would boost their hopes of reaching the semi-finals, with Bangladesh currently third in the five-team standings, behind Kenya and Sri Lanka, who have both won their opening two matches.

title: Antonelli looks to seal title 'in style' after US Grand Prix win
text:
Kimi Antonelli said his mindset will not change as he heads to next week's race in Mexico seeking the two points he needs to become Formula One’s youngest world champion.

The 20-year-old Italian delivered a well-executed and dominant drive to claim his ninth victory this year for Mercedes in Sunday’s United States Grand Prix and move within reach of the title.

Antonelli is on the brink of smashing the previous record for youngest champion, held by Sebastian Vettel who was 23 years and 133 days old when he won his first title in 2010

He is also set to become the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

"The best way, the perfect way, would be to finish off in style and then just enjoy the rest of the season,” he said.

"I'm very aware that it's very close but the mindset doesn't change.

Image

"I want to finish the season on a high in order to then go with high hopes into 2027. But we'll first focus and worry about finishing this well, and then we'll see."

After Sunday’s triumph at the Circuit of the Americas he leads with 365 points ahead of nearest rival and team-mate George Russell on 242 and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari on 241.

He will be champion if he finishes in the top nine or, if he doesn't score, Russell or Hamilton fail to win.

But on current form, after winning again for the first time in four races, he looks certain to take the title in his own happy, generous and infectious style.

"That was the perfect way to end the weekend,” he said.

“It was an incredible team effort, especially from strategy, to believe in me and go for one stop because I wasn't sure whether one or two stop was the quickest.

Image

"But I’m really happy that we made it stick. Today was a really important victory for me and for the team, especially after having a couple of difficult races, so being back on top feels very good."

Antonelli's ability on the track and infectious attitude off it have landed him numerous admirers around the paddock, including 1996 world champion Damon Hill.

“The team love him, he's enjoying everything he's got in F1 and he's very grateful for all the breaks they've given him at Mercedes," Hill said on the BBC.

"But he delivers. He's such a nice kid. It's incredible. Twenty years old and he's on the verge of winning his first championship, which I'm sure will be the first of many.”

title: Double delights for Imran and Shirin
text:
Sprinters Imranur Rahman and Shirin Akter completed their campaigns on a high note, winning gold medals in their respective 200m sprints on the concluding day of the Koko 18th National Summer Athletics Championships at the National Stadium on Sunday.

Both athletes completed sprint doubles after winning the 100m events on the opening day of the three-day competition, which saw nine national records set. Bangladesh Army re-established their supremacy, finishing on top with 21 gold, 20 silver and 19 bronze medals. Bangladesh Navy finished runners-up with 18 gold, 17 silver and 10 bronze medals.

Imranur, representing Bangladesh Navy, clocked 21.18 seconds to win the men's 200m gold, his second title in the event since his first triumph at the National Athletics Championships at Banani Army Stadium in 2022. The England-based sprinter was also part of Navy's gold-winning 4x100m relay team, earning him the best male sprinter award of the championships.

Bangladesh Army's Santo Karmokar and Rakibul Hasan finished second and third in the 200m, clocking 21.63 and 21.77 seconds respectively.

“It's double joy! The feeling is amazing,” Imranur said after winning the 200m.

“Actually, I participated in this event mainly as part of training, to see how it goes. I tried it in a casual and fun manner. Whatever the result has been, Alhamdulillah, I am quite satisfied with it. I have the intention to do better with better training in the future.”

In the women's 200m, Shirin set a new national record by clocking 24.35 seconds, finishing ahead of Bangladesh Army's Sharifa Khatun and Borsha Khatun, who recorded 25.11 and 25.33 seconds respectively.

Despite Shirin's record-breaking performance, teammate Priya Akter was adjudged the best female athlete of the championships after winning three gold medals in the 800m, 1,500m and 3,000m events. She also set national records in the latter two events.

title: Daily Star journalists finish runners-up at BSPA awards
text:

Ashfaq was among the runners-up in the print and online feature category, won by Shahjahan Kabir of Dainik Kaler Kantho. Firoz finished runner-up in photography, where Shamsul Haque Tenku of Prothom Alo claimed the top prize.

Rahenur Islam, senior sub-editor at Dainik Agamir Shomoy, was named Sports Journalist of the Year 2025 for the second time, having previously won the award in 2023. He received the Towfiq Aziz Khan Trophy and a cheque for Tk 1 lakh after securing the highest marks from an independent panel of judges.

Prothom Alo sports editor Tarek Mahmud and Dhaka Post senior reporter Arafat Zubayer were joint runners-up for the overall award.

Rahenur also won the print and online interview category, receiving the Ataul Haque Mallik Trophy. Tarek and Tanzim Ahmed of Bangla Tribune were the joint runners-up.

In other categories, SM Iqbal Kawsar of Somoy TV won the exclusive report award, while Arafat Zubayer of Dhaka Post took the series report prize.

Shuvo Debnath of News24 won the television interview category, and SK Shawon of Ekhon TV claimed the television documentary award.

In the exclusive report category, Tarek Mahmud and Zahir Uddin of Prothom Alo, along with Riyasad Azim of The Riyasad Azim, were the runners-up. In the series report category, Rahenur and Rubel Rehan of T Sports finished runners-up.

Sanjay Saha Piyal of Dainik Samakal was the other runner-up in the print and online feature category, while Rowshan Sharif of Ekhon TV and Rahul Roy of T Sports shared the runners-up places in television documentary.

Mosharaf Hossain of Dainik Agamir Shomoy joined Firoz among the runners-up in photography.

Youth and Sports State Minister Mohammad Aminul Haque presented the awards at a ceremony held at Fars Hotel in Paltan. Engineer Golam Mohammad Alamgir, chairman of Max Group and senior vice-president of the Bangladesh Swimming Federation, attended as special guest.

Sponsored by Max Group, the BSPA held the awards for the 11th consecutive year. Senior sports journalist Mostafa Kamal and veteran sports writer Major (retd) Shahabuddin Chakladar also received special honours to mark World Sports Journalists Day.

title: From one-season wonder to Ballon d'Or winner: Kane gets his golden due
text:
Harry Kane's Ballon d'Or triumph is the crowning moment for a player whose trophy collection does not do justice to his remarkable talent and consistency.

The Bayern Munich striker, 33, is the first Englishman to win football's most coveted individual honour since Michael Owen in 2001.

Lighting up for the world's best footballer ❤️ https://t.co/G5lB4KcNeM — Wembley Stadium (@wembleystadium) October 26, 2026

Kane's numbers are staggering and the England captain appears to be improving with age, with 73 goals for club and country last season.

In September he became the fastest player to reach 100 Bundesliga goals, hitting the landmark on his 98th league appearance for Bayern.

He is also Tottenham's all-time leading scorer with 280 goals, England's record scorer with 91, and the highest-scoring English player in the Champions League (58).

London has a new king tonight 👑 https://t.co/gm7NY7CGXp — FC Bayern München (@FCBayern) October 27, 2026

But for all his personal achievements in club and international football, Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023.

He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and was in England teams that twice lost the European Championship final.

Kane's lethal finishing is not the only string to his bow.

Honing an instinct he first developed as a youth team player, Kane has also blossomed into a gifted playmaker.

"I feel like I've always had the passing range and the vision and the football brain -- the game understanding -- throughout my whole career, and I think that's just flourished these last couple of years especially, these last few years since I've been here at Bayern," he told UEFA.com.

Ageing like fine wine



The clean-cut Kane, married to his childhood sweetheart Katie Goodland, is an understated throwback in an era of football bling.

But it has not always been plain sailing for a player who struggled to make an impression early in his career with Tottenham and was farmed out to other clubs on loan.

There were almost two years between Kane's first Spurs goal, against Shamrock Rovers in 2011, and his next, against Hull in 2013.

Even after his breakthrough season in 2014/15, he was dubbed a "one-season wonder", an accusation that has proved laughably wide of the mark.

Bayern boss Vincent Kompany has spoken of Kane's numerous qualities, including his distribution, work rate and "game intelligence".

"To combine that side of his game with the numbers he has, you have to do the job to help the team progress and then still arrive in the box, so it is not an easy thing," Kompany said.

"That is something we have seen and been able to enjoy, and that was maybe underestimated at the time in England, but he is ageing like fine wine so I am just enjoying seeing that side of his game for us as well."

Bayern teammate Jonathan Tah praised Kane's remarkable work ethic after seeing it up close.

"I played against him a lot and every time he got better -- now I'm playing with him I see why," he told the Times.

"He's never satisfied, you see him working before and after training. He's the greatest finisher I've seen in my life -- and he's still working on it."

title: Kane finally gets his golden moment, beats Yamal and Mbappe to taste Ballon d'Or glory
text:
Harry Kane became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years in his native city of London on Monday, beating out stiff competition from Lamine Yamal and Kylian Mbappe.

Alexia Putellas claimed the women's prize for a third time to extend Spain's domination of the award, thanks to her role in leading Barcelona to last season's Champions League before moving to London City Lionesses.

009 https://t.co/UpalGgPJmx — FC Bayern München (@FCBayern) October 26, 2026

The first ever Ballon d'Or ceremony on English soil got off to an inauspicious start as the London traffic caused a delay of nearly an hour, with many of the star names arriving late.

Image

But there was a happy ending for the hometown hero as Kane collected the crowning glory of his career to date.

The 33-year-old Bayern Munich forward struck a remarkable 73 goals in 65 games for club and country last season, propelling the German giants to a league and cup double.

He also scored six times as England finished third at the World Cup.

"Without you guys (his Bayern Munich team-mates) and the rest of the team it wouldn't be possible, the way you guys push me, the way we compete. So thank you very much," he said after collecting the award.

Kane's medal collection is limited to German domestic triumphs since he arrived at Bayern in 2023.

He was on the losing side for Tottenham in the 2019 Champions League final against Liverpool and twice tasted bitter defeat in the final of the European Championship with England.

Image

But his remarkable goalscoring consistency has earned him the highest individual award in football.

"Making the move to Bayern Munich was a big step in my career," Kane told AFP earlier. "Some people saw it as a risk but for me it was always about improving and seeing if I could get better around the team-mates, the team, the club and it has pushed me onto another level.

"Being a number nine for Bayern and England you are expected to score goals and to do that the number of times I did last year is something I'm really proud of," he added.

Putellas back on top



Winner in 2021 and 2022, Putellas's third Ballon d'Or caps her return back to the top of the women's game after an anterior cruciate ligament injury derailed her rise four years ago.

Image

Putellas succeeds Spain team-mate Aitana Bonmati, the winner the past three years who was sidelined by a leg break for most of last season.

"Ever since I suffered the injury, I've been trying to enjoy every moment as if it were my last, because you never know if it'll happen again," Putellas told AFP in an interview last month.

"I never felt that the (Ballon d'Or) trophy was 'mine'... Having already experienced it once, I’m able to enjoy it even more now," she added.

Yamal made the boldest fashion statement of the contenders with a pink flower on the front of his black suit.

The Barcelona winger scooped up the first award of the night for young talent of the year for the third consecutive time.

But the 19-year-old fell short of becoming the youngest ever Ballon d'Or winner after he failed to produce his best form during Spain's World Cup success.

Mbappe got the better of Yamal with two goals as Real Madrid edged Barcelona 2-1 in El Clasico on Sunday.

But his wait to win the Ballon d'Or goes on despite his prolific year for France and Real Madrid.

Luis de la Fuente beat out Paris Saint-Germain's Luis Enrique and Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta to be named men's coach of the year after leading Spain to World Cup glory.

"I'm really privileged to work with a team of such high quality on a professional and human level," said de la Fuente.

Barcelona's Pere Romeu scooped the prize for women's coach of the year.

Arsenal's Bukayo Saka won the Socrates award for his humanitarian work.

Paris Saint-Germain missed out on any of the main individual awards despite winning a second consecutive Champions League, but did have the consolation of men's club of the year.

Spanish duo Unai Simon and Cata Coll were named best men's and women's goalkeeper.

title: Two defeats, familiar flaws: Barcelona's big-game problems remain unresolved
text:
After a superb start to the season Barcelona were brought crashing back down to earth by Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain last week, raising fresh doubts about the Spanish champions' ability to compete against the strongest opponents.

Hansi Flick's side have dominated in Spain over the last two seasons, winning back-to-back La Liga titles, but notably in Europe have fallen short on high-pressure nights.

The Catalan giants have played sumptuous attacking football this season and won their first 11 games across all competitions, but once the quality of their opponents rose, it was a different story.

Barca were beaten 4-2 in Paris by European champions PSG on Tuesday, showing they are still some way from matching Luis Enrique's side.

That was compounded by Sunday's painful 2-1 home defeat by Jose Mourinho's Real Madrid in La Liga, in which Barcelona's defensive frailties were laid bare again.

A draw would have been an acceptable result and maintained their six-point lead on Madrid in the top flight, but they left far too much space for Los Blancos to exploit in the final stages.

With three minutes to go Eduardo Camavinga raced through on goal and squared for Kylian Mbappe to net his 100th Madrid goal and second of the night to snatch victory.

"In the end sometimes in the big, big games, small things are important and they decide the game and which way they end, and today that was not on our side," Flick told reporters, pledging to improve.

"We know what we have to make better. We speak about this in every training. We will do it, I'm not worried about that.

"It's a part of this game to lose also. In this week, we had two (losses) and it's too much."

However it is a discourse which the German coach has repeated during his tenure.

"We are a young side and we have to mature," said Flick, after Inter Milan ousted Barcelona in the Champions League semi-finals in May 2025.

"We are working on it and we have to improve in defence and in other aspects."

Image

- Lack of 'freshness' -

Despite spending good money on Anthony Gordon, Rodri and others this summer, and trying to bring in Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez, Barcelona did not sign a centre-back.

Instead Flick has persisted with Gerard Martin, a converted left-back, playing alongside Pau Cubarsi.

Martin has done well, considering his technical limitations and change of position, but against the world's best strikers is clearly out of his depth.

The defender's poor clearance handed Madrid their first goal against Barca, with Mbappe gleefully capitalising.

To Martin's credit, he did defend well to stop Jude Bellingham and Mbappe in a two-on-one situation early in the second half, which exposed a more structural problem Barca have.

Their high-line defence is easy to breach when the team's pressing is not executed perfectly, with high energy.

Flick suggested Barcelona lacked "freshness" against Madrid, after a gruelling schedule, although his team had an extra day to recover midweek and the coach waited until the final minutes to introduce Gabriel Jesus and Karim Adeyemi.

Barca do have injury problems at the back, with Eric Garcia, Jules Kounde and Andreas Christensen all missing the Clasico, along with midfielder Dani Olmo.

"This may be the most important point, the injuries we have," explained Flick.

Barcelona still hold a three-point lead on Madrid, third, in the title race. They are more than capable of going on another run of victories, but the weeks ahead will pose further interesting tests.

Aston Villa visit Camp Nou in the Champions League on November 3, before Barcelona head to Atletico Madrid on November 8. A month after that, Manchester City come to the Camp Nou.

Flick has been promising improvement in these type of matches for over two years -- perhaps now he will finally focus on implementing it.

title: Topu calls for collective defensive effort
text:
Fit-again centre-back Topu Barman has stressed the importance of collective defending as Bangladesh prepare to begin their SAFF Championship campaign against Bhutan in Dhaka on November 5.

Under German-American coach Thomas Dooley, Bangladesh have conceded 14 goals in four matches, including nine against Indonesia, while scoring only four. Topu missed the last three matches of the FIFA ASEAN Cup after scoring both goals in Bangladesh’s 2-1 win over San Marino in June.

His absence exposed the backline against stronger opposition, with Tariq Kazi, Shakil Ahad Topu and Zidane Yousuf struggling to contain the pressure. However, the Bashundhara Kings defender believes Bangladesh can improve with a collective effort as they began preparations for the SAFF Championship at the National Stadium on Monday.

“When you concede goals, the goalkeeper and defenders have to face it. But I think the most important thing is team defending, which is very important in world football. If we can perform as a team defensively, we will definitely not concede so many goals,” Topu told reporters.

Recalling the ASEAN Cup defeats, he said: “We conceded three goals in the first match [against Malaysia] and nine in the last match [against Indonesia]. It is very disappointing, and I don't know when we last conceded nine goals. If I can play, I will give my best and have a role in guiding others from the back.”

Image Saad Uddin, Mohammad Ridoy and Bishwanath Ghosh in training. Photo: BFF

Topu is expected to partner young defender Zidane, who featured in all three ASEAN Cup matches after playing in the AFC U-20 Asian Cup Qualifiers in Uzbekistan. The experienced centre-back believes the exposure will benefit his younger teammate.

“He is very young but has already played at a high level in the ASEAN Cup. He has gained good experience. At this level, a defender needs a strong mentality, physical strength and good performance, and he has all those qualities,” Topu said.

Having trained with Zidane in the previous camp, Topu expects the pair to develop a good understanding during the nine days before Bangladesh’s opening match.

Bangladesh will also be without Hamza Choudhury against Bhutan, but Topu believes the team can compensate for his absence through collective effort.

“We will miss our most important player, Hamza, especially for the first match. But if we can play well as a team, we can cover his absence. The first match is very important,” he said.

Bangladesh are targeting their first SAFF Championship title in 23 years, with the tournament being held on home soil.

“You have to beat everyone to become champions, and we have to go onto the pitch with that mentality. SAFF is very special for us, and we want to win the trophy again,” Topu said.

title: Mahe relishes chance to learn from childhood hero Hamza
text:
Newly called-up striker Mohammed Mahe Khan is relishing the prospect of sharing the dressing room with his childhood hero, Hamza Choudhury.

“I am very excited. Since childhood, I have been watching Hamza [Choudhury ] play for Leicester City, because Leicester is near our home. The person whom I have grown up watching since childhood, now I have got the opportunity to play in the same team with him — it is a huge honour for me,” Mahe told reporters ahead of the national team's first training session at the National Stadium on Monday.

Having grown up watching Hamza play for Leicester City, Mahe described the opportunity to represent Bangladesh alongside the midfielder as a huge honour, particularly given the experience Hamza has gained at the highest level of English football.

“He has played at the top level of football and he has a lot of experience. I will get the opportunity to learn a lot from him,” Mahe added.

However, the 18-year-old will have to wait to share the pitch with his childhood idol in Bangladesh's opening match of the upcoming SAFF Championship, as both Hamza and Farhaan Ali Wahid are set to miss the game against Bhutan due to FIFA international window restrictions.

Mahe is no stranger to Bangladesh football, having represented the country in the AFC U-20 Asian Cup qualifiers and come off the bench in all three matches during the team's campaign in Uzbekistan.

The young forward is determined to make the most of his maiden call-up to the senior national team camp.

“I am extremely proud and happy. At just 18 years old, I have received my first call-up to the senior national team camp. I am proud of myself, and my whole family is also very happy,” he said.

The England-based forward is also confident of handling the responsibility of playing as the team's traditional No. 9, a position that comes with the expectation of scoring goals and leading the attacking line. He believes he is ready to meet head coach Thomas Dooley's expectations.

“I am fully confident. Even before coming to the camp here, I worked very hard personally. So, InshaAllah, I will be able to score goals. I clearly know what the coach expects from me. On the pitch, I will try to implement the coach's game plan 100 per cent, and hopefully, I will score goals,” he said.

“Now is the time for us to work hard and, InshaAllah, we will also win the SAFF title.”

The teenager, however, acknowledged that playing in such a crucial position would inevitably bring pressure, although he insisted that his focus remained on giving his best whenever the opportunity arose.

“There will be some pressure. But my only aim is to go onto the pitch and give my best. I have full faith in myself and in my ability, so I am not very nervous. If I get a chance in the starting XI, I want to deliver my best performance,” he added.

Asked about the hand injury he sustained during the qualifiers, Mahe said he had fully recovered.

“My hand is completely fine now. After returning to England, I had a check-up and also played matches. There was no problem. If I can give my best in training, hopefully, I will get the main striker position in the starting XI,” he said.

Reflecting on the Under-20 team's difficult campaign in Uzbekistan, Mahe admitted that the side had fallen short of expectations but expressed hope that the experience would help him prepare for the challenges of senior-level football.

title: ‘Definitely not like last year’: Sammy laughs off memories of Mirpur’s black wickets
text:
West Indies head coach Darren Sammy could not help but laugh when reminded of the black wickets that grabbed attention during the team’s white-ball tour of Bangladesh last year.

The unusual surface had become a talking point during the series, with spinner Akeal Hosein joking that he had thought something was wrong with his television while watching the game at home.

With the West Indies set to begin a two-match Test series against Bangladesh on October 28 at the Sher-e-Bangla National Stadium in Mirpur, Sammy was asked whether the wickets looked anything like those from the previous visit.

When asked by The Daily Star after the press conference whether he had inspected the wicket, Sammy replied, “Yes I have.”

“Is it like last year?” came the follow-up question.

Sammy burst into laughter, seemingly recalling the much-discussed black surfaces.

“No! It’s definitely not like last year,” he said with a hearty laugh.

Image

The pitch, however, is only one of the talking points ahead of the series. Unlike the surfaces seen during last year’s white-ball matches, the wicket has so far appeared more sporting, although conditions in Mirpur could still offer assistance to the spinners as the Test progresses.

The difference between the conditions for white-ball cricket and a red-ball series could prove significant for the visitors, who will be looking to finish their World Test Championship campaign on a positive note.

There was also a hint of mind games during Sammy’s press conference, with the West Indies coach sharing a history with Bangladesh head coach Phil Simmons. Sammy had been part of the West Indies side that won the T20 World Cup in 2016 under Simmons, who is now in charge of the Tigers.

With West Indies currently eighth in the World Test Championship standings and set to conclude their campaign with the Bangladesh series, the stakes are significant for both sides.

Bangladesh, meanwhile, will be keen to make the most of home conditions as they look to strengthen their position in the race for a place in the World Test Championship final.

Asked whether the pressure would be greater on Bangladesh given their ambitions, Sammy refused to single out the hosts.

“I think the stakes are high for both teams,” he said.

“Everybody is playing Test cricket to win. When the Test Championship started, we had our goals where we want to finish. Looking at what we have, the opposition, and we're in a very good position to achieve that goal. And that's life,” he added.

Rather than speculate about the pressure on Bangladesh, Sammy suggested the question should be directed at his former coach.

“About the pressure for Bangladesh, you'll have to ask their head coach that question,” he said.

The West Indies coach will take confidence from his team's recent performances, having drawn their T20I series against India 2-2. Sammy also made it clear that his side would not be travelling to Bangladesh merely to make up the numbers.

He expects an entertaining contest against a side that has established a reputation for being difficult to beat at home, particularly in Test cricket.

“I'm excited to finish the Test Championship against a team like Bangladesh who have proven to be extremely difficult to beat at home, especially coming from some good results in this year's Test cycle,” Sammy said.

“So hopefully we entertain, but when we entertain West Indies come out victorious,” he added.

title: Gardner says cricket offers escape amid personal turmoil
text:
Australia vice-captain Ashleigh Gardner says cricket has provided a welcome escape during a challenging period in her personal life, as she thanked teammates for their support following the breakdown of her marriage.

Gardner's marriage broke down earlier in the year, with her former partner Monica Wright criticising the cricketer for her relationship with Australia teammate Georgia Voll on social media.

Cricket Australia knew about the relationship before Wright's comments and the governing body backed the all-rounder to continue as vice-captain despite scrutiny over her leadership position.

Speaking at the Sydney Sixers' season launch in Sydney on Monday, Gardner acknowledged the toll of a difficult period for her personally but said her cricket commitments had helped her maintain perspective.

"Challenging, but cricket has been a fantastic escape," she told reporters.

"Being able to win the World Cup and have success in The Hundred campaign as well was great.

"I have had some fantastic people around me to be there when I've needed them, and cricket has been great because I know the people around me support me. They know the type of person I am."

Sixers captain Gardner apologised in August in a statement for the pain caused by her marriage breakdown and thanked Cricket Australia for backing her leadership.

The Sixers also stood by Gardner, announcing in July she would remain captain for the Women's Big Bash League season.

“Obviously this club means a lot to me (and) to have the backing from the people at the top,” she said.

title: Who will win the Ballon d'Or this time?
text:

Set to begin at 2:00 am Bangladesh time, the ceremony will feature awards across multiple categories, but the spotlight, as always, will be on the player who claims the ultimate prize.

Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Lamine Yamal and Michael Olise could all get their hands on a maiden Ballon d’Or, while Lionel Messi could make history by winning the award for a record-extending ninth time.

With the 2026 FIFA World Cup also set to play a major role in the race, the final outcome could hinge on performances on the biggest stage in international football.

Voted for by journalists representing the top 100 nations in the FIFA rankings, the award often leaves room for surprises, with the final tally determining who comes out on top.

Here, we take a look at the leading contenders, their numbers and the titles they have won:

Harry Kane (Bayern Munich and England)

Goals: 73

Assists: 8

World Cup: 6 goals and 1 assist in seven matches, helping England finish third.

Titles won: Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal, and German Super Cup.

Lamine Yamal (Barcelona and Spain)

Goals: 26

Assists: 21
