Based on the Hindu epic “Ramayana”, the film is planned as a two-part release. The first instalment is scheduled to reach cinemas on November 5, while the second was originally slated for Diwali 2027.

The cast features Ranbir Kapoor as Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita, Yash as Ravana and Sunny Deol as Hanuman.

title: From National Award to indie recognition: Sunerah does it all
text:
Sunerah Binte Kamal was among the first anchors of Blender’s Choice–The Daily Star OTT & Digital Content Awards, when the ceremony was launched in 2022. Five years later, the actress returned to the stage at the fifth edition of the awards on October 9, performing a duet with Irfan Sajjad.

Image Photo; Sheikh Mehedi Morshed

The evening was also special for the National Film Award-winning actress, as her film “Daagi” won the People’s Choice Award. In an interview with The Daily Star, she spoke about her performance, her background in classical dance and more.

“I hosted the very first edition of The Daily Star’s OTT awards, even though hosting is not something I am particularly comfortable with because I am a very shy person. I have only gradually become more comfortable speaking during interviews. Before, I could barely speak as much as I do now,” she said.

Image Photo: Hridoy

“Not many people knew that I had a classical dance background, so I think everyone enjoyed seeing that side of me through my performance of ‘Patar Bashori’,” she said.

Sharing the stage with Irfan Sajjad was another enjoyable part of the experience. Although they have different personalities, she said they get along well. Their contrasting approaches to preparation, however, made rehearsals interesting.

Image Photo: Sheikh Mehedi Morshed

“I stood there and taught him the steps myself. I had to keep rehearsing with him repeatedly. I think that actually improved my performance because I ended up practising more!”

Beyond her performance, Sunhera reflected on the recognition “Daagi” has received. “People really love ‘Daagi’. Another interesting thing I have noticed is that people have been asking me the same question since the film was released and started winning awards: ‘Why weren’t you nominated? Why aren’t you receiving any awards?’”

Image Photo: Hridoy

She said her performance had generated considerable discussion. However, she believes awards are not the only measure of appreciation.

“I do not believe that recognition comes only through awards. Of course, I want the film to do well because I played a character in it, and its success matters to me,” she said.

The actress recently travelled to the Venice Film Festival for the premiere of Rubaiyat Hossain’s film “The Difficult Bride”. During the screening, she closely observed the audience’s reactions, wanting to see how viewers responded to the film.

Image Photo: Hridoy

“They genuinely enjoyed the film. Everyone appreciated the story, the filmmaking and our acting,” she said.

One audience member even asked how she managed to maintain her bridal look throughout the film. Sunerah recalled wearing a heavy lehenga, full bridal makeup and fabric on her hands and feet to resemble the traditional application of alta. Getting ready each day took several hours.

Image Photo: Hridoy

“Once the veil on my head was secured, I could not even go to the washroom until the shooting was finished! That was a real challenge, but the look turned out beautifully on screen.”

Meanwhile, with audiences increasingly turning to YouTube dramas, Sunerah believes the industry is adapting to changing viewing habits.

“Audiences today want content quickly, having grown accustomed to watching reels and continuously swiping to the next video. The easy access to free YouTube content has also contributed to its growing popularity.”

“OTT platforms, meanwhile, need to offer the kind of content we sit down to watch on services such as Netflix. We need that kind of work as well. Sometimes I watch films, sometimes series, and sometimes television dramas. We should have all kinds of content because each format caters to a different audience,” she added.

title: Lapse of security taints stellar concert: ‘Rock & Rhythm 5.0’ at JFP
text:
As I tried to enter the concert premises at Jamuna Future Park, a large group surged through security barriers made of bamboo poles tied with rope and covered with thin black fabric. A policeman was being overwhelmed and assaulted by a group. On the other end of the spectrum, a lone law enforcement officer waved his stick at people trying to flee. Elsewhere, armed police and security personnel stood watching, while some merely blew their whistles.

It took me more than 30 minutes to reach backstage. By then, I had missed a lot of the action.

The stark contrast between what happened on stage and off it defined "Rock & Rhythm 5.0: No Limits in The Zone". Organised by Adventor Communications at the Carnival Arena of Jamuna Future Park on Friday, October 23, the concert offered memorable performances alongside troubling security failures.

Image

“Looks like they have overbooked the venue,” a performer from one of the night’s standout acts remarked during a conversation in the green room.

From intimate, ticketed concerts in living rooms to large festivals, audiences have been finding different ways to engage with the arts. Young people have been a visible part of that participation. Friday’s concert offered another reminder of the enthusiasm surrounding live music—and the responsibility that comes with bringing so many people together.

Beyond the disorder, the night delivered musical moments that a social media reel could only partly convey.

The programme opened with A K Rahul featuring Black Zang, followed by Hasan with Ark. Oni Hasan’s band, featuring Jamshed Chowdhury, then tore through the venue with the heaviest setlist of the night. Later, Shunno took to the stage with original member Shaker Raza for a mesmerising performance.

Image

During Aurthohin’s set, Shishir ascended on a boom lift to perform atop four stacked shipping containers. Bassbaba emerged through the middle of the stage on a scissor lift, performed his signature bass flip, and played with his teeth.

Image

Warfaze followed, bringing Oni Hasan on stage midway through their set. Like Bassbaba, he emerged from the middle of the stage. For roughly 25 minutes, "Na", "Purnota", and "Boshey Achi" brought an earlier chapter of the band’s history back into view. It was a chance for younger listeners to experience that lineup and for longtime fans to revisit it.

Image

Another standout was Dibbomoy Chakraborty Rizu, the new drummer in Oni Hasan’s band. Playing his first major show, the teenager delivered one of the night’s most commanding performances.

Image

In the final hour, James held the crowd spellbound with Nagar Baul classics.

Image

The staging was ambitious. The lifts and towering containers gave the performances a striking visual dimension, while entrances from beneath the stage added an element of surprise. Yet those moments sat uneasily alongside the disorder at the entrance.

Image

Adventor Co-founder Nehal Hossain acknowledged that the evening had not gone as intended.

“As organisers, we always try to add new things to our audience’s concert experience. This time, we also tried to host the biggest open-air concert of the year, bring in a memorable lineup, and try things that have never been done before. We tried our best, but things didn’t go as planned. I am having mixed feelings. We will try to recover from this,” he told The Daily Star.

He also appealed to those forcing their way into concerts:

“To the people who mob and ruin everyone’s concert experience – please at least try to respect the artistes and organisers. We put a lot of effort and funding into arranging a show. We never oversell tickets, but because of the mobs, we get a lot of blame. I hope they will stop.”

The performances gave the audience plenty to remember, but the scenes outside the stage area served as a stark reminder that a great concert experience also depends on being able to enter, watch, and leave safely.

title: Feedback’s 50: Bangladesh to witness legendary band’s grand celebration
text:
“For a band to remain in listeners’ hearts for five decades is truly a cause for joy. This journey belongs to more than just us; it has involved countless members, lyricists, composers and, above all, our millions of fans and listeners,” said Foad Nasser Babu, a veteran who has woven magic with his ephemeral keyboard riffs for 50 years, before today's press conference at The Daily Star’s A S Mahmud Hall.

Feedback, a cornerstone of Bangladesh’s band music scene, will soon celebrate its five-decade journey with a series of special concerts and attractions under the banner “Feedback: 50 Not Out”.

Founded in October 1977, Feedback has entered its 50th year, marking the occasion with a year-long programme featuring fresh renditions of popular songs, new releases and concerts across Bangladesh.

Image Hamin Ahmed pays tribute to Feedback at the event.

“We will start with Chattogram because we feel like we have more fans there,” continued Babu, outlining the plans for the year-long celebration.

“We want to bring our old members and the people who have been part of this journey together and make the occasion memorable,” he said.

“Feedback is not out. We plan to go on for a long time. There is no retirement in this profession,” said Labu Rahman. Labu’s energising guitar playing has been a hallmark of the band, and he has also been an inspiration for generations of guitarists who went on to become famous.

Image

The occasion also brought together musicians who have shared different chapters of Bangladesh’s band music history with Feedback.

Recalling the early days of the country’s band music scene, Miles frontman Hamin Ahmed said, “The two bands started their journey from Hotel InterContinental. There was a sense of brotherhood in sharing the same amplifier. Feedback was the first band that came to our minds when Miles was looking to release Bangla songs.”

The host, Hasibul Hossain Upal, also highlighted the musical contributions of Miles and Feedback, pointing to the quality of their musicianship and arrangements.

The programme also included tributes to Feedback’s first guitarist, Selim Haider, whose contribution to the band’s history was remembered.

Pilu Khan of Renaissance praised the musicians and their character, saying, “All the best musicians seemed to be in one band, and that was Feedback back in the 1970s. They are not only fine musicians, but the finest human beings.”

Sayed Hasan Tipu of Obscure recalled how Feedback had helped younger musicians find their footing in the industry.

“When we first came here, we didn’t know anything. We learned our basics from them. Feedback acted like a guardian to Obscure,” he said.

Since the mid-1980s, Feedback has developed a distinctive sound blending folk, pop and modern rock, helping shape the evolution of Bangladesh’s band music scene. Over the years, musicians including Maqsoodul Haque, Pearo Khan and Labu Rahman have contributed to the band’s musical journey.

The group’s repertoire includes songs such as “Melay Jaire”, “Ei Din Chirodin Robe”, “Ek Jhak Projapoti”, “Jhau Boney”, “Udashi”, “Moushumi”, “Chithi”, “Sukhi Manusher Bhire” and “Geetikobita”. Among them, “Melay Jaire” has become closely associated with Bengali New Year celebrations and is widely regarded as an unofficial anthem of the occasion.

As Feedback approaches its golden jubilee, “50 Not Out” is intended to celebrate not only the band’s musical achievements but also its enduring connection with generations of listeners. With new music, concerts and a reunion of former members in the works, the band is looking to honour its past while continuing its musical journey.

title: Chaos erupts at James’s concert as crowd breaks through security
text:
Chaos erupted at the “Rock N Rhythm 5.0: No Limits in the Zone” concert at Jamuna Future Park in Dhaka on Friday evening, as thousands of people reportedly broke through security barriers and entered the venue without tickets before James took the stage.



The disorder occurred ahead of a performance by popular singer Mahfuz Anam James and his band, Nagar Baul, on October 23.



The uncontrolled entry left ticket-holding audience members struggling to enjoy the concert. Overcrowding and poor crowd management drew complaints from those who had paid to attend the event.



Image



As the situation went out of control, the organisers were forced to open the main gates. The move further angered audience members who had purchased tickets.



One person who entered the venue without a ticket said, “It is not possible to get in like this; I had to struggle a lot to get inside.”



Videos circulating on social media showed audience members chanting “fake, fake” amid the chaos. In one video, a person complained, “The management is not proper. Many people have entered without tickets.”



Another video appeared to show security personnel restraining and beating an audience member.Police were deployed to manage the situation and attempted to disperse the crowds gathered at the concert entrances.

title: Kabir-Lalon Bhavasangit Utshab celebrates music and humanity in Chattogram
text:
The philosophy and humanist teachings of Sant Kabir and Fakir Lalon Shah can guide humanity towards building a peaceful, violence-free world, speakers observed at the seventh edition of the Kabir-Lalon Bhavasangit Utshab in Chattogram on Friday.

Inaugurating the festival, renowned flautist of the subcontinent and Ekushey Padak recipient Ostad Azizul Islam said the teachings of Kabir and Lalon transcend geographical boundaries, time, language, religion, caste and creed, strengthening the bonds of universal humanity.

Image

The divisional music festival was held at the premises of the Chattogram District Shilpakala Academy, organised by Lalon Bishwo Shangho with the support of the Ministry of Cultural Affairs. The programme began with the lighting of lamps by Ostad Azizul Islam.

Chattogram Divisional Commissioner Dr Md Ziauddin attended the event as the chief guest, while Dr Md Sheikh Sadi, professor of the Department of Bengali at the University of Chattogram, was present as the special guest. The programme was presided over by Abdel Mannan, chief executive of Lalon Bishwo Shangho and a researcher of Kabir and Lalon.

A major highlight of the evening was a musical narrative titled “Kabir theke Lalon: Chironton Premer Ek Oikyo Bandhon” (From Kabir to Lalon: An Indestructible Bond of Eternal Love), performed by artistes of the Kabir-Lalon Musical Mission.

Image

According to the organisers, the festival draws inspiration from nearly 500 years of spiritual and humanist traditions represented by figures such as Sant Kabir and Fakir Lalon Shah. Their messages of love, humanism and communal harmony, they said, offer a way to overcome divisions and hostility and build a peaceful global society.

Emphasising the importance of practising indigenous cultural traditions, Divisional Commissioner Dr Md Ziauddin said, “The more we practise and study Kabir and Lalon, the more a society driven by love will flourish.”

He also expressed concern over the tendency to embrace Western cultural influences while overlooking the country's rich cultural heritage.

“While we often lean towards consuming Western cultural leftovers, we possess a glorious thousand-year cultural heritage. If we internalise the cultural teachings of love left behind by Sant Kabir and subsequently Fakir Lalon Shah, and continue to practise them, our society will naturally transform into one filled with love,” he said.

title: Guitarist Russell Khan passes away after suffering from dengue, chikungunya
text:
Guitarist Russell Khan, who accompanied many of the country’s leading singers for more than three decades, died at his elder sister’s home in Dhaka’s Banani this morning. He was 52.

Instrumentalist Azmir Babu confirmed the news to Prothom Alo.

According to the report, Russell had been unwell for several days after contracting dengue and chikungunya. He collapsed in the bathroom at his sister’s home this morning. A doctor later examined him and pronounced him dead. The report said the doctor attributed his death to a stroke.

Throughout his long career, Russell played alongside many of Bangladesh’s leading singers, becoming a familiar presence on stage. Alongside playing the guitar, he occasionally performed as a vocalist.

His last stage performance was at an event in Manikganj on October 13.

News of his death prompted an outpouring of grief from colleagues, artistes and well-wishers. Many took to Facebook to share condolences and memories of working with him.

His namaz-e-janaza was held at 3:30pm today at a mosque near his elder sister’s home in Banani. Afterwards, his body was being taken to his ancestral home in Bikrampur for burial at the family graveyard.

Russell is survived by his wife, a son and a daughter.

title: Hamin Ahmed becomes first Bangladeshi elected to APMA executive committee
text:
Hamin Ahmed, frontman of the legendary Bangladeshi band Miles and an advocate for music creators’ rights, has been elected to the executive committee of the Asia-Pacific Music Creators Alliance (APMA) for the 2026–2029 term.

He is the first representative from Bangladesh to join the alliance’s executive committee, marking a milestone for the country’s representation in regional music policy and copyright advocacy.

“When I received the call from CISAC, I was elated. Representatives from over 20 countries are currently cooperating through this organisation, and I will put my best foot forward to ensure that our voice is heard,” said the musician.

CISAC is the International Confederation of Societies of Authors and Composers.

Hamin’s election places a Bangladeshi music industry leader in a key regional forum dedicated to protecting songwriters’ and composers’ rights. Whether he will take on an additional leadership role remains under discussion.

“That is still an ongoing conversation. It is currently under discussion whether I will hold a specific leadership post or not,” he said.

Image

Hamin serves as CEO of the Bangladesh Lyricists, Composers and Performers Society (BLCPS) and president of the Bangladesh Musical Bands Association (BAMBA). His election to the APMA executive committee is expected to strengthen Bangladesh’s voice in discussions on intellectual property rights across Asia.

Established in November 2016 during the World Creators Forum in Beijing, APMA is a regional coalition of music creators and their representative organisations. It is affiliated with the International Council of Music Creators (CIAM) and CISAC, two international bodies dedicated to advancing creators’ interests and rights.

“APMA works to address critical challenges such as unfair copyright buyouts, inadequate remuneration for private copying, and the value gap between the revenue generated by digital music platforms and the income received by creators,” Hamin explained.

“The alliance also promotes awareness of creators’ moral and economic rights and supports the development of collective management organisations in territories where such systems are still emerging.”

These issues are particularly relevant to Bangladesh, where ensuring fair compensation remains an ongoing challenge—one that the Miles musician has been working to address for over a decade. Under Hamin’s leadership, BLCPS is in the process of obtaining CISAC membership.

The current APMA committee brings together representatives from organisations involved in music rights and collective management across countries and territories including Australia, Bangladesh, China, India, Indonesia, Japan, Macau, the Philippines, South Korea and Thailand.

For Bangladesh, Hamin’s election offers an opportunity to expand its participation in global discussions that increasingly shape how music is created, distributed, licensed and monetised. As digital platforms continue to transform the industry, regional cooperation on copyright protection and fair remuneration has become vital to the livelihoods of songwriters, composers, performers and other music professionals.

title: Harry Styles debuts unreleased track in tribute to Liam Payne
text:
Harry Styles has performed an unreleased song written in memory of his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne during a concert at Madison Square Garden.

The singer played the track, titled "What Is Enough", on the second anniversary of Payne’s death. Payne died in October 2024 after falling from a hotel balcony in Buenos Aires, Argentina.

Image

Addressing the audience during his “Together, Together” tour residency in New York, Styles paid tribute to his late colleague.

"There are so many people in my life, friends and people that I've worked with that I wouldn't have been able to do this without," Styles said. "And two years ago today, I lost one of those friends."

Image

Introducing the acoustic track, Styles encouraged the crowd to support one another through grief and hardship.

"I'm sure a lot of you have been through similar things," he added. "Really, it's just about looking after each other."

Styles and Payne achieved global prominence alongside Niall Horan, Louis Tomlinson, and Zayn Malik in One Direction, formed on The X Factor in 2010. Following the group's 2016 hiatus, Styles launched a successful solo career, earning multiple Grammy Awards, including Album of the Year for Harry's House.

title: 101 theatre practitioners demand restoration of Mahila Samity subsidy
text:
A total of 101 theatre artistes and practitioners have called for the restoration of government subsidies for staging plays at Bangladesh Mahila Samity’s Dr Nilima Ibrahim Auditorium, citing mounting financial pressure on theatre troupes.

In a joint statement issued today, October 25, the signatories urged the Ministry of Cultural Affairs to approve the requested Tk 14.3 lakh allocation and increase overall financial support for theatre, ensuring regular funding.

Signatories include Syed Jamil Ahmed, Sara Zaker, Mamunur Rashid, Ramendu Majumdar, Ferdousi Majumdar, Masum Reza, Tropa Majumdar, Fazlur Rahman Babu, Azad Abul Kalam and Samina Luthfa.

The statement was issued on their behalf by playwright Apu Mehedi, executive editor of the theatre magazine Khyapa.

According to the statement, theatre troupes have had to pay Tk 11,500 per shift at the auditorium since January, up from Tk 5,000, following the withdrawal of the ministry’s subsidy. The increased expense has discouraged troupes from performing at the venue, with ticket sales often insufficient to cover production costs.

“We believe government subsidies must be restored promptly to keep theatre practice alive on the Mahila Samity stage,” the statement said.

The signatories said special allocations for this purpose began in June 2017. The last allocation, Tk 11 lakh, was made in the 2024-25 fiscal year, while no funds were allocated for 2025-26.

For the 2026-27 fiscal year, Mahila Samity has sought Tk 14.3 lakh, calculated at Tk 6,500 per performance for 20 shows a month over 11 months.

The statement highlighted the venue’s historical significance, saying it was where Bangladesh’s ticketed theatre culture began in 1973. It also recalled that the road housing the venue was formally named “Natak Sarani” by then mayor Sadeque Hossain Khoka on August 26, 2005.

“Government support for theatre in Bangladesh is already very limited. It is disappointing that even this modest support has been withdrawn,” the statement said.

The signatories called on the ministry to act swiftly, arguing that sustaining the subsidy was part of the government’s responsibility towards the country’s theatrical heritage.

The Daily Star previously reported on the financial strain caused by the subsidy’s withdrawal. An August 12 letter from Mahila Samity General Secretary Tamanna Rahman to Cultural Affairs Minister Nitai Roy Chowdhury sought funding to maintain regular performances at the auditorium.

Speaking to The Daily Star for that report, State Minister for Cultural Affairs Ali Newaz Mahmud Khaiyam said the ministry would look into the matter and address the funding request.

title: ‘Animal Farm’ returns to Shilpakala for two shows
text:
“Animal Farm”, presented by the theatre department of Rabindra Srijonkala University, returns to the stage with two performances at the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy on October 26 and 27.

Both shows will begin at 7:00pm at the main auditorium of the National Theatre Hall in Dhaka.

Directed by Saidur Rahman Lipon, the play has been adapted by Nazrul Syed from George Orwell’s political allegory “Animal Farm”, published in 1945.

The production explores the abuse of power, the betrayal of revolutionary ideals, political deception, the distortion of history and the denial of ordinary people’s rights—themes that continue to resonate today.

title: ‘Novera’ returns to stage today after seven-year hiatus
text:
After a seven-year hiatus, Dhrupodi Art Center’s debut production, the solo play “Novera”, is returning to the stage, with its 30th performance scheduled for today at the Nilima Ibrahim Auditorium of Bangladesh Mahila Samity on Bailey Road in Dhaka.

The play explores the life and artistic journey of Novera Ahmed, a pioneering sculptor in Bangladesh, delving into her art, love, solitude and complex identity as an artist. The performance is scheduled for 7pm.

The production first premiered in 2016. Based on the original work by Hasnat Abdul Hye, the play has been adapted for the stage by Samiun Jahan, who also performs as the sole actor. Shajjad Rajib has directed the production.

Novera Ahmed holds a distinctive place in the history of modern sculpture in Bangladesh. She developed her own artistic language beyond conventional ideas of art and established social norms. Her life and creative practice were shaped by aspirations for freedom, individuality, love, loneliness and a continuous search for artistic expression.

Although Novera gradually withdrew from public life, the play brings her back to the stage through an exploration of her art and inner world.

Running for one hour and 10 minutes, the solo production uses a single performer to portray the sculptor’s multifaceted personality and artistic identity. Through this intimate theatrical approach, the play seeks to capture the tensions, experiences and creative impulses that shaped Novera’s life.

title: Kamrul Hasan Lipu’s first solo exhibition opens in Japan
text:
Bangladeshi artist Kamrul Hasan Lipu’s first solo exhibition in Japan is underway at Gallery Shimizu in Yokohama, bringing together 41 paintings inspired by Bengali cultural motifs, memory and identity.

Titled “DOT: The Beginning of Everything”, the exhibition opened on October 20 and runs until October 25. Its works feature women’s faces, water lilies, sari patterns and elements of folk art, reflecting the artist’s connection to Bangladesh and his experiences of living in Japan.

The exhibition was inaugurated at 3pm on Tuesday, with Matsudo City Council member Mir Kazue as the chief guest. Japanese artist Asano Yasunori, paper-cutting artist Mita Chikako and Gallery Shimizu representative Shimizu Kazue were also present.

The title reflects Lipu’s artistic philosophy: a dot develops into a line, a line into a shape, and shapes combine to form the visible world. The idea draws on his own journey, from childhood drawing and years of practice to his experiences in Bangladesh and Japan.

Women’s faces are a recurring subject in Lipu’s work. Details such as sari folds, jewellery, flowers in the hair and facial expressions evoke familiar aspects of Bengali life. His paintings explore beauty alongside sensitivity, dignity and emotional resilience.

Works including “The Bede Girl”, “Madhabi”, “Mrinalini” and “Beyond the Blue” reflect different aspects of this exploration.

Using acrylic, oil and mixed media, Lipu moves between figurative imagery and abstraction. Layers of colour, free-flowing lines, brushstrokes and textures give his subjects varied forms and expressions.

The exhibition catalogue features messages from artists Rafiqun Nabi and Jamal Ahmed, Professor Shahjahan Ahmed Bikash, and Japanese graphic designer and art critic Ikufumi Fukuzawa. Their reflections address Lipu’s sustained practice, use of colour and texture, engagement with cultural memory and artistic experimentation.

The exhibition is open daily from 11am to 6pm at Gallery Shimizu. On October 25, the final day, visitors can view the works until 4pm.

title: ‘Verses of Flame’: An exhibition where fire becomes art
text:
Fire is often associated with destruction, but in the hands of an artist, it can become a medium of creation. In “Verses of Flame”, artist Sheikh Mehedi Kamal explores the possibilities of fire as an artistic medium, using unconventional techniques to express human experiences and emotions.

Image



The solo painting exhibition was inaugurated at Gallery Chitrak on October 14 by emeritus professor and artist Rafiqun Nabi. Mostafizul Haque, a professor at Shanto-Mariam University of Creative Technology, attended the event as a special guest.

Image



After nearly two decades, Kamal has returned with a solo exhibition featuring works created using two uncommon artistic techniques. Both methods rely on heat to bring images to life and differ from conventional painting practices.

Image



One of the techniques is pyrography, an art form that uses heat to create images on a surface. Although it has been used for centuries to decorate materials such as wood, wool and leather, applying it to thick paper offers different artistic possibilities. The artist applies a special chemical treatment to the paper before using a heated metal tool or needle to draw lines and develop images.

Image



The second technique is even less common. It resembles watercolour painting in the way washes are used to create different tones. However, the images emerge through the application of heat to the paper, making the process both unusual and technically demanding.

In both techniques, the final image takes shape through the interaction between the treated surface and heat. The process requires patience and precision, as the artist must carefully control his marks to achieve the desired effect.

Image



Beyond the techniques themselves, the exhibition explores the pain and emotions of people who have endured hardship. Kamal attempts to capture their struggles and inner experiences on paper and translate them into visual forms.

Image



The title “Verses of Flame” reflects the central role of fire in the exhibition. One of the paintings, titled “Agun Pakhi”, evokes the image of a mythical bird from a fairy tale, adding a symbolic dimension to the artist’s exploration of suffering and transformation. Other works, titled “Poroshmoni”, “Aguner Poroshmoni” and “Onol Prokriti”, also draw attention to the recurring presence of fire and nature. Their titles suggest connections between the individual paintings and the broader themes explored throughout the exhibition.

Image



Rafiqun Nabi praised the precision of the works and the relationship between their themes. “I can confidently say that this is an exceptional exhibition,” he said. He also noted that the paintings had been created with great care and that their subjects were connected to one another.

Image



Special guest Mostafizul Haque described the use of such unconventional techniques as a courageous artistic undertaking.

Through “Verses of Flame”, Kamal moves beyond conventional painting materials to explore fire as a medium of artistic expression. Combining unconventional techniques with reflections on human suffering and lived experiences, the exhibition offers a fresh perspective on the possibilities of visual art. The exhibition concluded on October 22.

Image

title: Schoolchildren rethink waste and carbon footprints at Goethe-Institut exhibition
text:
What if waste wasn’t waste? It is a question with endless answers, some of which are on display in the auditorium of Goethe-Institut Dhaka. No, it is not simply waste on show, but objects created by upcycling discarded materials.

Titled “Reimagining Waste”, the exhibition aims to raise awareness about consumption, upcycling and reducing carbon footprints. It opened on October 17 in the presence of Goethe-Institut Director Frank Werner.

Image

The exhibition grew out of a workshop led by environmentally conscious artists in collaboration with Urukku, a platform for sustainable art. Designed and developed by Urukku and organised by Goethe-Institut and PASCH schools, the project brought students and artists together to generate ideas, rethink discarded materials and turn them into something useful or decorative.

Image

Goethe-Institut selected students from four English-medium schools in Dhaka under the PASCH initiative for the month-long workshop. The mentors and artists were Tarannum Ali Nibir and Manzoor Ahmed from Urukku, Farah Naz Moon, Rituparna Saha, Shafrin Islam, Md Mazharul Haque Tonmoy, Protiti Iqbal, Mahbub Ratan and Habibur Rahman.

Image

Throughout the workshop, students learnt different techniques for creating things out of waste. Mentor Rituparna Saha taught them fabric manipulation, helping them create tiny artistic pieces from discarded fabrics. Artists Tonmoy and Protiti used mud to add texture to canvas, with sackcloth holding it together, creating brilliant abstract paintings. Farah took the children to a park to collect materials they could upcycle. The results were adorable.

Image

The students also learnt to make papier-mâché creations. There were paintings on discarded glass and stories on used paper, among other works.

A short cultural programme followed the exhibition’s inauguration, with students singing, reciting poems and staging a puppet show. They also received certificates of recognition from Goethe-Institut and Urukku. After a break, Argha Dev Sarker performed a short concert.

Image

The week-long exhibition includes several events, among them a thrift sale and a papier-mâché workshop. It closes on October 23 with a “Chader Buri” reading session by Herstory.

title: Liberation DocFest selects 17 films from 188 entries
text:
The 13th Liberation DocFest Bangladesh will screen 17 documentaries selected from 188 submissions at the Liberation War Museum in Agargaon, Dhaka, from October 29 to 31.

The festival’s national and international competition sections will run alongside “Best of the Fest”. This year’s theme is “Presence in Absence”.

An eight-member preview committee selected the films from entries submitted by filmmakers in different countries. The committee comprised Jihan Karim, Biplob Sarkar, Mehedi Mostafa, Partha Sarathi, Sharmin Doza, Chaitali Samaddar, Kamrul Ahsan and Kazi Arefin Ahmed.

The selected films are grouped into eight thematic sections: “Bodies and Belonging”, “Gender Equality and Resistance”, “Resistance and Reform”, “Generational Memory”, “Displacement and Statelessness”, “1971: Living Archives”, “Ecology in Crisis” and “Ancestral Roots and Livelihoods”.

The national and international competitions will each award a prize of Tk 1 lakh. A separate nine-member youth jury will select a film for recognition, with the winner receiving a crest and certificate.

The national jury comprises filmmaker Shabnam Ferdousi, visual artist and filmmaker Dilara Begum, and Sajjad Hossain, a faculty member at the University of Liberal Arts Bangladesh.

The international jury includes cultural personality M Hamid, filmmaker Shamim Akhtar, and human rights activist Asif Munier.

A seminar on documentary filmmaking in higher education will accompany the screenings. The discussion will examine the scope and practical challenges of assigning documentary production as a classroom project, while considering how the form can connect younger generations with the history and memory of the Liberation War.

The seminar is scheduled for 4 pm on October 30 in the museum’s seminar room.

Established in 2006, Liberation DocFest Bangladesh promotes documentary filmmaking centred on freedom, human rights and social struggles. The festival also seeks to connect Bangladeshi filmmakers with international documentary cinema and encourage younger generations to engage with the form.

title: Protest held at Shahbagh over attack on CPB office
text:
Leaders of the Bangladesh Chhatra Union and Bangladesh Jubo Union on Tuesday protested an alleged attack on their activists and the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) headquarters in Dhaka’s Purana Paltan.

Speaking at a rally in Shahbagh in the evening, they said the incident reflected an increasingly hostile environment for political expression and called on the BNP to abandon its “anti-people stance”.

The event was arranged jointly by the two organisations in response to Monday night’s violence, during which activists of Bangladesh Chhatra Union and Bangladesh Jubo Union were allegedly assaulted and Mukti Bhaban, the CPB’s central office, came under attack.

Mahir Shahriar Reza, president of Bangladesh Chhatra Union, alleged that their activists had faced repeated attacks.

He accused BNP activists of creating a mob outside their office and questioned whether the incidents were part of a broader plan.

Jahangir Alam Nannu, general secretary of the Bangladesh Jubo Union, said people were being harassed and subjected to mob violence over allegations of links to Awami League.

He also condemned the attack on CPB office, describing it as another instance of mob violence.

He said they would not accept attacks on the values of Liberation War or freedom of expression.

The rally was chaired by Nannu and conducted by Bangladesh Chhatra Union General Secretary Bahaunddin Shuvo.

title: ‘Awami League has always departed in humiliation and disgrace’: Shafiqur
text:
Leader of the Opposition and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman today described the Awami League, whose political activity remains banned, as a “club of fascists”.

“Awami League has never left power under normal circumstances. It has always departed in humiliation and disgrace,” he said while addressing a discussion at the Institution of Diploma Engineers, Bangladesh, in Dhaka’s Kakrail.

He warned that anyone following the same path would face a similar fate.

“Referendum verdict was given for a change in politics. People wanted a change that would serve the country and its people and leave no scope for anyone to become a fascist again,” he said.

Addressing the government, the Jamaat chief said those now in power had forgotten their experience of suffering under fascism for a long time.

“Friends, there is nothing to gain by forgetting,” he said.

Urging the government to reform the constitution to fulfil public expectations, he said, “We are still urging you to come back, come back, and fulfil the people's expectations by establishing a Constitution Reform Council.”

He said Jamaat would continue its struggle against injustice if the government failed to meet those expectations.

“We have never bowed to injustice in the past, and we will not do so now. We will continue to fight for the people, for justice and fairness, for building a humane Bangladesh, and for bringing the perpetrators of all killings to justice,” he said.Referring to the October 28, 2006, attacks and killings involving logi-baitha (boat hooks and oars) in Dhaka’s Paltan and elsewhere in the country, Shafiqur said those responsible for killing Jamaat-e-Islami and Islami Chhatra Shibir leaders and activists must be brought to justice.

The Jamaat chief alleged that although cases were filed over the killings, the Awami League government later removed the case documents and withdrew the cases after coming to power.

He also said the sacrifices of those killed during the Awami League's 15-and-a-half-year rule, particularly during the July Uprising, must be remembered.

Calling for an end to violence and killings in the name of politics and urging the establishment of humane politics, Shafiqur said those involved in politics in Bangladesh must work for the welfare of the people.

title: Mamunul warns of tougher movement if EC fails to ensure neutral local polls
text:
Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis Ameer Maulana Mamunul Haque has expressed concern over whether the upcoming local government elections will be held neutrally, warning that the Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance will launch a major programme against the Election Commission (EC) if it fails to act impartially.

“Election Commission must play a neutral role. If there is any deviation in ensuring people’s voting rights, the 11-party alliance will not remain silent," he said while briefing journalists after a meeting of the alliance’s top leaders at the Leader of the Opposition’s official residence on Minto Road in Dhaka this afternoon.

He also voiced concern over the commission’s role in the upcoming Thakurgaon by-election.

Mamunul expressed dissatisfaction with the government, saying the alliance had so far pursued its programmes with restraint in its efforts to establish people’s rights.

He said the alliance had played a responsible role both inside and outside parliament and had shown a willingness to cooperate with the government. However, he alleged that the government had shown little sincerity in accepting cooperation from the opposition.

“In this situation, we will launch tougher programmes if necessary to secure people’s rights,” Mamunul said, urging the government to take necessary steps in line with people’s aspirations and expectations.

The meeting also discussed preparations for the Dhaka-Khulna-Kushtia long march scheduled for October 31, Mamunul said.

He said the programme would press for the implementation of the referendum verdict, the trial of those responsible for the July massacre, and solutions to shortages of electricity, fuel, gas and fertiliser.

It would also demand measures to curb rising prices of essential commodities and end corruption, extortion and land grabbing, he added.

The long march would also highlight demands for an independent and effective judiciary and justice for all killings, including those committed during the July massacre, the Shapla massacre and the killing of Sharif Osman Hadi, he said.

The programme will begin with an opening rally at the south gate of Baitul Mukarram National Mosque at 7:00am on Friday. It will pass through several locations before ending in Kushtia, Haque said.

He said the alliance had sought cooperation from law enforcement agencies and the administration to ensure the peaceful conduct of the long march.

Asked whether the alliance feared possible untoward incidents as the procession will pass through Gopalganj, he said it did not anticipate any such situation. He expressed confidence that the programme would proceed normally if law enforcement agencies remained alert.

title: EC declares Aliza Zaman’s nomination valid for vacant reserved seat
text:
The Election Commission (EC) has declared the nomination paper of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)-nominated candidate Aliza Zaman valid for the reserved women’s seat-23 by-election in the 13th National Parliament after scrutinising her nomination paper.

The scrutiny was scheduled for today.

After reviewing Aliza’s nomination paper at his office at the EC headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka, Md Moin Uddin Khan, returning officer and EC joint secretary, declared it valid.

EC officials said no other political party or independent candidate had submitted nomination papers for the by-election, leaving Aliza Zaman as the sole contender.

Once the legal process is completed and the deadline for disposing of any appeals has passed, she will be officially declared elected unopposed after the deadline for withdrawal of candidature.

According to the election schedule announced on October 12, appeals against the nomination scrutiny decision may be filed on October 28, while appeal hearings will be held on October 29.

The last date for withdrawal of candidature is November 1. Election symbols will be allotted on November 2, and voting is scheduled for November 12.

title: Campaigning ends in Thakurgaon-1 as candidates make final push ahead of by-polls
text:
Candidates from different political parties, including the BNP and Jamaat-e-Islami, made their final campaign rounds across Thakurgaon-1 today, the last day of canvassing ahead of the by-election scheduled for October 29.

During the campaign, BNP-backed candidate Mirza Faisal Amin and party leaders pledged to accelerate development by taking advantage of opportunities available through the ruling party. In contrast, Jamaat-e-Islami-backed candidate Delawar Hossain and his supporters promised to ensure the proper and transparent use of government funds and uphold the rule of law.

The three other candidates also highlighted their priorities and plans if elected.

On the final day of campaigning, Mirza Faisal, younger brother of President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, began his mass-contact programme in Akhanagar union of Thakurgaon Sadar in the morning, addressing gatherings at nine locations.

He later visited Dholarhat union, where he attended three separate meetings, before joining an election rally at Kumarpur High School ground in Bhulli. BNP central leader Moyazzem Hossain Alal attended the rally as chief guest.

Meanwhile, Jamaat-backed candidate Delawar Hossain exchanged greetings with party leaders and activists at the party office in the Purba Goalpara area of Thakurgaon municipality before visiting Gorea, Chilarang and Jagannathpur unions.

He addressed voters at more than 10 locations and attended an election rally at Telipara in Salandar union of Thakurgaon Sadar in the evening.

Khademul Islam, the Islami Andolan Bangladesh-backed candidate with the hand fan symbol, led an election procession in the afternoon following a rally at the Thakurgaon Public Library premises.

Bangladesh Khelafat Andolan-backed candidate Abdul Alim Nizami, contesting with the banyan tree symbol, campaigned in the town using a loudspeaker mounted on an easy-bike. Bangladesh Congress candidate Muhammad Omar Farukh, whose symbol is the green coconut, distributed leaflets among voters.

Addressing campaign rallies, Mirza Faisal said he would play an active role in implementing development projects, including the establishment of a public university, a medical college, an economic zone and an engineering college, initiatives he said had been pursued by his elder brother.

He also pledged to work for the reopening of Thakurgaon Airport as quickly as possible.

Delawar Hossain said that if elected, he would work to ensure the corruption-free use of public funds, uphold the rule of law and build a society free from drug abuse.

Returning Officer and District Election Officer Quamrul Islam said voting in the by-election would be held from 8:00am to 4:00pm on October 29 at 185 polling centres across the constituency.

The constituency has 516,138 registered voters, including 258,659 women, 257,475 men and four third-gender voters.

The seat fell vacant after former Thakurgaon-1 MP Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was elected president and took oath of office.

Asked about election preparations, Quamrul said a motorcade comprising district administration and police officials, along with personnel from various law enforcement agencies, toured different parts of the constituency today.

title: Jamaat slams IGP's 'crossfire' remarks, warns of return to ‘culture of fear’
text:
Strongly condemning and protesting the remarks made by Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir on bringing back "crossfire" if the government allowed it, Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami today said the statement indicated a return to a "culture of fear" and earlier practices of the Awami League regime.

“Police are servants of the citizens, not their rulers... As the head of the law enforcement agency, he has violated his service rules by making such remarks,” Jamaat Assistant Secretary General Ahsanul Mahboob Zubair said in a statement today.

Earlier in the day, the IGP at an event in Dhaka's Chawkbazar said, “Where crossfire is necessary, if the government allows it, we will do it.”

Referring to the previous fascist regime, the Jamaat leader said, “Citizens of this country had no security of life and property and no freedom of speech. People were killed without trial. Citizens were picked up by people identifying themselves as members of law enforcement agencies and subjected to killings, crossfire, and enforced disappearance.”

He alleged that the IGP had threatened and hinted at a return to the same practices, adding that his remarks were contrary to the constitution and the rule of law. Zubair expressed hope that the government would take action in this regard.

Describing the IGP’s remarks as unacceptable and unwarranted amid a severe deterioration in the law and order situation, Zubair said, “His remarks indicate a move to bring the country back to a culture of fear.”

Alleging that law enforcement agencies had failed to rein in BNP activists involved in violence, stop extortion and eliminate drugs, Zubair urged law enforcers to take effective measures to ensure greater safety for citizens.

title: Govt inaction over IGP's ‘crossfire’ remarks would signal approval for extrajudicial killings: Hasnat
text:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Senior Joint Convener, MP Hasnat Abdullah, today said if the government failed to take action against Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir over his "crossfire" remarks, it would suggest that the government was moving towards legitimising extrajudicial killings and enforced disappearances.

"The police chief threatened to bring back extrajudicial killings and compared himself to former senior police officials Harun, Benazir, and Biplob" he said at an NCP public outreach programme in Dhaka’s Mugda in the afternoon.

The controversial police officials in question are -- former DMP Detective Branch chief Harun-or-Rashid, former RAB DG and IGP Benazir Ahmed, and former DMP joint commissioner Biplob Kumar Sarker.

Earlier today, the IGP said police could resort to "crossfire" if necessary and with government permission. “Wherever crossfire is necessary, if the government allows it, we will do that," he said at a programme in Dhaka's Chawkbazar.

Reacting sharply, Hasnat said in any civilised country, this IGP could not have remained in office after making such remarks.

He alleged that the conduct of officers such as Fakir was damaging the reputation of the entire police force at a time when many officers were trying to regain public confidence.

"We want to see what decision the government takes regarding the IGP," he added.

Addressing police personnel, Hasnat urged them not to work for any political party during the upcoming elections.

"For God's sake, you do not need to work for Salahuddin (home minister) or the BNP in the next election. You do not need to work for the NCP or Jamaat either," he said.

"Your uniforms are bought with taxpayers' money. Work for the people, and the people will ensure your security," he added.

Hasnat also demanded the release of a female entrepreneur arrested in Mymensingh after expressing regret over voting for the BNP government.

He alleged that she was arrested merely for admitting that voting for the BNP had been a “mistake”.

He also demanded information on the whereabouts of Miraj Sheikh of Mongla, alleging that Coast Guard personnel were involved in his disappearance.

Criticising the government, Hasnat accused it of politicising public institutions and undermining the confidence of young jobseekers.

He alleged that members of the Public Service Commission had been forced out, and questioned changes proposed to recruitment and teacher appointment procedures.

Hasnat also raised concerns over the transparency of upcoming elections, accusing Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed of attempting to influence institutional reforms.

Expressing support for NCP Senior Joint Convener Nasiruddin Patwary, he said he believed Patwary would be elected mayor of Dhaka South City Corporation with the people's mandate.

title: IGP’s ‘crossfire’ remark evokes memories of ousted regime: Gazi Ataur
text:
Islami Andolan Bangladesh Secretary General Maulana Gazi Ataur Rahman has described Inspector General of Police (IGP) Ali Hossain Fakir’s remarks on crossfire as alarming, saying they evoke memories of the police under the ousted regime.

“We want to believe that Ali Hossain Fakir made the remark in a light-hearted mood, although someone holding such an important position cannot afford to make such comments in a light-hearted manner,” Gazi Ataur Rahman said in a statement issued today.

Earlier today at an event, IGP Ali Hossain had said police would use “crossfire” if necessary, if the government allows it.

Criticising the police’s official accounts of crossfire incidents, the Islami Andolan leader said police had traditionally described such incidents as cases in which they returned fire after being shot at by criminal gangs, resulting in the alleged criminal’s death in an exchange of gunfire.

“Although the reality is different, the police have always described it this way,” he said.

“The way the IGP spoke today about carrying out crossfire killings amounts to an official admission that police use the term ‘crossfire’ to describe the deliberate shooting and killing of a person.

“What is particularly alarming is that the police chief is publicly declaring an intention to carry out an act that is outside the law and judicial process and violates human rights in every sense,” Gazi Ataur said.

“Even if the government wants it, a police force funded by public money cannot engage in such crimes against humanity,” he added.

Criticising the tendency to follow government orders in violation of the law and human rights, he said, “It was this tendency to obey government orders even when they violated the law and recognised human rights that made life unbearable for people during the ousted fascist regime. The police displaying the same attitude even after the mass uprising is unacceptable.”

title: Nahid accuses BNP of seeking to monopolise power
text:
National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam today accused the BNP of trying to monopolise power whenever it was in office and failing to cooperate in a peaceful transfer of power.

He made the remarks at a press conference at a restaurant in Munshiganj town around 12:00pm, ahead of the NCP’s regional coordination meetings to review organisational progress across the country and plan for local and national elections.

Nahid said the caretaker government system had a long history, with the demand emerging during the mass uprising of the 1990s and being accepted by all political parties involved in the movement.

He said the BNP held a one-sided election in 1996 but failed to sustain its rule and was eventually forced to step down amid a movement.

“In 2006 as well, BNP played dramas regarding the caretaker government. They politicised the judiciary, trying to install their own judge as the head of the caretaker government. In the same manner as the Awami League, the BNP has always tried to monopolise power. However, while the Awami League succeeded, the BNP did not,” he said.

Nahid alleged that the BNP was again delaying the process over the caretaker government system and conspiring to install its own people. He warned that such attempts would not be allowed to succeed.

NCP Senior Joint Member Secretary Sarjis Alam and other central and local leaders were present at the press conference.

title: BNP picks Aliza Zaman for vacant reserved seat
text:
BNP has nominated Aliza Zaman for the November 12 by-election to reserved women’s seat-23 in the 13th parliament, which fell vacant following the resignation of Ferdousy Ahmed Misty earlier this month.

Aliza submitted her nomination papers today, the last day for filing nominations.

Her nomination was confirmed in a list signed by BNP Acting Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi.

Aliza is a member of the BNP’s central executive committee and the No. 1 joint convener of its Pirojpur district unit. She previously served as the Barishal divisional organising secretary of Mahila Dal.

The seat fell vacant after Ferdousy resigned on October 1 following instructions from Prime Minister and BNP Chairman Tarique Rahman.

Her resignation came amid allegations that people close to her were involved in an attack, vandalism and looting at the Radda Mother and Child Care Centre in Mirpur, Dhaka.

A total of 68 women submitted nomination forms seeking the BNP’s ticket for the seat. The party interviewed the aspirants at its chairman’s political office in Gulshan on October 19 before finalising its candidate.

According to the Election Commission’s schedule, it will scrutinise nomination papers tomorrow, and the deadline for withdrawing candidature is November 1.

title: Thakurgaon-1 by-polls: Jamaat alleges administration not acting impartially, seeks army deployment
text:
Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami has demanded army deployment in the Thakurgaon-1 by-election, alleging that the administration is not acting impartially and a rival candidate is violating the electoral code of conduct.

Jamaat leaders made the allegations at the Election Commission headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka, this evening.

Earlier, a six-member Jamaat delegation held an hour-long meeting with chief election commissioner (CEC) and submitted a written complaint outlining nine allegations and three demands, including army deployment.

Jamaat’s two other demands are: legal action against those responsible for violating election rules and a review of the neutrality of the relevant upazila nirbahi officer (UNO), followed by necessary action if warranted.

After the meeting, Jamaat-e-Islami Secretary General Mia Golam Porwar alleged that the administration, election officials, and law enforcement agencies involved in conducting the Thakurgaon-1 by-election were not acting neutrally.

"If the current situation does not change, the election will not be fair," he said.

Porwar said a central team of Jamaat visited Thakurgaon yesterday to assess the situation on the ground and gather information from local residents. Based on its findings, the party submitted complaints to the CEC along with photographs, images of injured party activists, and what it described as evidence of electoral code violations.

He alleged that an upazila nirbahi officer (UNO) was working “in favour of a rival candidate”.

"The official (UNO) reportedly attended a meeting at the candidate's residence at night and shared social media posts that appeared to campaign for the sheaf of paddy [BNP] candidate. There are also allegations of violations of the electoral code, monetary transactions, and voter intimidation. Despite these allegations, the official has not been withdrawn," Porwar said.

He further alleged that Jamaat leaders and activists had come under attack in the constituency, leaving both men and women injured, but police and other law enforcement agencies had failed to take effective action.

Porwar also alleged that the BNP candidate held campaign meetings inside mosques, used coloured electoral symbols in violation of the code of conduct, and used loudspeakers before the permitted time. According to him, the authorities did not take effective action against those violations.

The Jamaat leader said members of the Hindu community, government employees and teachers, were being threatened in the constituency. He also alleged that free medical camps were being operated in several unions in violation of restrictions on providing services to voters during the campaign period.

He said increasing the number of law enforcement personnel alone would not ensure a fair election, stressing that those assigned to election duties must act impartially.

Referring to the controversial Magura by-election of 1994, Porwar warned that the government and the Election Commission should remain mindful of the consequences if the Thakurgaon-1 election was allowed to move in a similar direction.

He claimed that the commission had not outlined any firm measures capable of reassuring his party. However, he said Jamaat had not decided to withdraw from the race and remained committed to contesting the election while continuing to demand conditions conducive to a fair vote.

title: ‘If money is coming from across the border, why are you in government?’: Shafiqur
text:
Leader of the Opposition and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman has warned that attempts to implement the July Charter through constitutional amendments could be struck down by the courts, urging instead that reforms be carried out in line with the referendum verdict.

“If you amend it again, a court will completely whitewash it. We are not accustomed to following this futile path and repeating the mistakes of the past,” he said at a discussion organised by Jamaat at the National Press Club in Dhaka to mark the first anniversary of the signing of the July Charter.

“The ‘No’ vote was swept away by people's aspirations, and 70 percent voted ‘Yes’. The people have made it clear that they no longer want to see the rotten, outdated politics of the past. We want change and reforms,” he said.

Referring to the special committee formed to amend the constitution, Shafiqur said the opposition was being asked to join a process that could leave the referendum verdict unimplemented. He argued that the existing constitution had not only given birth to fascism but had also sought to make it permanent.

“The government will be bound to implement this referendum verdict,” he said, adding that Jamaat would continue its movement to establish people's rights rather than pursue party-specific demands.

Shafiqur also responded to remarks made by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in Rajshahi on October 20, when the premier alleged that the ousted regime was sending money from across the border to a political party accused of spreading misinformation and trying to create instability.

“If money is coming from across the border, why are you in government? Why can’t you stop it from entering the country?” Shafiqur said, also questioning the government’s failure to prevent weapons and drugs from being smuggled across the border.

“A government that is incapable of preventing such unwanted activities has no right to govern the country,” he added.

Leaders of the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance also spoke at the discussion.

title: ACC sues ex-land minister Saifuzzaman, wife and 13 others over Tk 63.77cr embezzlement
text:
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) on Tuesday lodged a case against former land minister Saifuzzaman Chowdhury, his wife and 13 others over their alleged involvement in embezzling Tk 63.77 crore from Islami Bank in Chattogram through 27 forged deeds made in the name of Aramit Cement.

The case was filed at the ACC’s Chattogram-1 Integrated District Office, ACC Deputy Director Mashiur Rahman said today.

ACC Deputy Assistant Director Rubel Hossain filed the case.

The other accused are Saifuzzaman's wife and Aramit Cement Managing Director Rukmila Zaman; Aramit Cement Chief Financial Officer Mohammad Shah Alam; Aramit Cement Assistant General Manager (AGM) AKM Maruf; Classic Trading owner and Aramit AGM Mohammad Jahangir Alam; Islami Bank Jubilee Road branch Principal Officer Md Mohiuddin; Principal Officer (Investment) Mohammad Akhtar Hossain; Principal Officer and General Banking In-charge Mohammad Abdul Haque; Investment In-charge Md Abdul Kader; Vice-President and Jubilee Road branch manager Muhammad Abdul Karim; Senior Principal Officer (SPO) Md Shahidullah; First Assistant Vice President (FAVP) Muhammad Nizam Uddin; Senior Vice President (SVP) Abul Kalam Azad; SVP Mohammad Mohsin Ali; and SPO Ridwanul Haque.

According to the case statement, Mohammad Jahangir Alam, an AGM (Accounts) and an employee of a company under Saifuzzaman Chowdhury’s Aramit Group, was shown as the owner of Classic Trading, which was presented as the supplier, while Aramit Cement was shown as the recipient of the goods through fraud and abuse of power.

“Without supplying any goods, forged documents containing false information were prepared and submitted to the bank to secure approval for Bai-Murabaha deals (loans). The funds were then transferred to a bank account in the name of an employee of a company under Saifuzzaman Chowdhury’s Aramit Group,” the statement said.

During its investigation, the ACC found no office or warehouse at the address listed for Classic Trading. It also found no evidence of the company’s import or export activities.

title: On the way to buy land, woman in Raozan robbed of Tk 25 lakh at gunpoint
text:
Six armed robbers allegedly snatched Tk 25 lakh from a woman at gunpoint in Chattogram’s Raozan upazila around noon today.

The incident took place in the Mangal Khali area of Raozan Sadar union when the woman was on her way to the upazila's sub-registry office to buy land, police said.

Raozan Police Station Officer-in-Charge Saiful Islam said the victim, Shamsun Nahar, 50, was travelling in a CNG-run auto-rickshaw with two relatives when two motorcycles carrying six men blocked their way at a secluded spot.

Two of the robbers pointed pistols at her and snatched a bag containing the money, he said.

Shamsun had withdrawn the money from a bank a few days earlier to buy land and kept it at home before setting out for the sub-registry office today, the OC added.

“She came to the police station after the incident. We have recorded details of the incident from her and started an investigation. Efforts are underway to identify those involved,” he said.

title: Man allegedly beaten to death by elder brother, brother’s in-laws over land dispute in Magura
text:
A 42-year-old man was allegedly beaten to death by his elder brother and the latter’s in-laws over a family property dispute in Magura’s Shalikha upazila today.

The deceased was identified as Masud Rana of Naghosa village under Talkhari union, police said.

According to family members and locals, Masud and his elder brother, Siddique, had an altercation over a piece of land around 11:30am. The argument soon escalated into a scuffle.

As Siddique’s in-laws live in the same village, his father-in-law and other family members rushed to the scene after learning about the incident.

At one stage, they allegedly attacked Masud with bamboo sticks, leaving him critically injured.

Masud collapsed from his injuries. His wife and several local residents were also injured when they tried to save him.

Locals later rescued Masud and took him to a clinic at Naghosa Bazar, where a physician declared him dead.

As news of his death spread, angry villagers surrounded the houses of the accused and confined two women to a room before informing police.

Shalikha Police Station Officer-in-Charge Ashiqur Rahman confirmed the incident, saying preliminary information suggested that a man had been killed following an altercation involving his brother in Naghosa village.

“Two women have been detained in connection with the incident,” the OC said.

He added that the body had been sent to the morgue for an autopsy and that preparations were underway to file a murder case.

title: BNP MP’s son questioned over JCD leader’s killing in Natore
text:
A local leader of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal (JCD) from Natore died last night -- 12 days after being attacked by a group of assailants.

The deceased, Md Shakil Islam, 30, was the joint general secretary of the Gurudaspur upazila unit of JCD.

“Shakil succumbed to his injuries at about 8:30pm on Monday while undergoing treatment at PG Hospital [Bangladesh Medical University] in Dhaka,” Gurudaspur Police Station Inspector Md Riazul Hasan said, declining to comment further until the investigation is complete.

According to the police, a group of helmet-wearing assailants attacked Shakil in the Chachkoir Bazarpara area on October 14.

The attackers hacked him with sharp weapons, leaving him critically injured. He was first taken to Gurudaspur Upazila Health Complex, then transferred to Rajshahi Medical College Hospital and subsequently moved to Dhaka for advanced treatment, the inspector said.

On October 19, Shakil’s father filed a case with Gurudaspur Police Station, accusing eight to 10 unidentified individuals.

Meanwhile, a team of the Detective Branch (DB) of police picked up Md Nuruzzaman Mintu, son of Natore-4 BNP lawmaker Md Abdul Aziz, for questioning over the incident.

“We have picked him up for the sake of investigation. We will interrogate him,” said Md Nazrul Islam, officer-in-charge of DB in Natore.

Asked why the lawmaker’s son was being questioned, the DB officer said he could not disclose details at this stage.

Local residents alleged that the lawmaker’s two sons, Nuruzzaman Mintu and his younger brother Mahamuduzzaman, had been locked in a long-standing rivalry for political dominance in the area. They suggested that Shakil’s killing might have been linked to the dispute.

Denying the allegation, MP Abdul Aziz said the dispute between his sons was strictly a "family matter" and had no connection to Shakil’s death.

Instead, Abdul Aziz claimed that Awami League, whose political activity remains banned, might be responsible for the killing of the JCD leader.“The loss of Shakil feels like losing my own child. I want those responsible for his killing to be punished, even if it is my own son. I fully cooperated with police when they came to take my son from the house,” the lawmaker said.

“I will not seek bail for my son unless his innocence is proven,” he added, calling for a thorough investigation to identify those responsible.

A Natore court this evening placed Nuruzzaman on a three-day remand.

The Detective Branch (DB) of police produced him before the court with a petition seeking a 10-day remand. After a hearing, Senior Judicial Magistrate Md Mahmudul Hasan granted a three-day remand.

Meanwhile, news of Shakil’s death sparked protests among local party activists in Gurudaspur. Angry JCD members brought out a procession demanding exemplary punishment for the attackers.

Md Kamruzzaman Bepari, secretary of the Natore district JCD unit, told The Daily Star that the killers must face exemplary punishment.

“Shakil was a devoted JCD leader. He was always vocal against drugs and irregularities. Criminals killed him mercilessly. We want the real culprits to be identified through a proper investigation and punished,” he said.

title: ICT to deliver verdict in case against Hanif, three others on Oct 29
text:
The International Crimes Tribunal-2 will deliver its verdict on October 29 in a crimes against humanity case against Awami League Joint General Secretary Mahbubul Alam Hanif and three other party leaders over the killing of six people in Kushtia during the July Uprising.

The three-member tribunal announced the date today.

The three other accused are Kushtia district Awami League President and former Zila Parishad Chairman Sadruddin Khan, district Awami League General Secretary Azgar Ali, and Kushtia city Awami League General Secretary Ataur Rahman Ata.

The prosecution concluded its arguments on October 5, seeking the maximum punishment for all four accused, who are absconding.

The tribunal framed charges against Hanif and the three others on November 2, 2025.

title: Ex-Jubo Dal leader among two shot in separate incidents in Khulna
text:
Two people, including a former Jubo Dal leader, were shot in separate incidents in Khulna within a few hours.

Salman, 25, an office assistant at a Japan Tobacco dealer point, was shot in the right side of his abdomen by unidentified assailants in front of the dealer point on Road 17 in Nirala Residential Area around 11:15am today.

According to police, five men arrived on two motorcycles, shot Salman and snatched his laptop bag before fleeing.

His colleagues rescued him and took him to Khulna Medical College Hospital, where he is receiving treatment.

Khulna Police Station Officer-in-Charge Lokmon Hossain told The Daily Star that Salman is out of danger. Police were investigating the motive behind the shooting and trying to identify those involved.

Earlier, around 12:30am, Md Sohel Sheikh, 34, a former joint convener of the Batiaghata upazila unit of Jubo Dal, was shot in front of Boro Karia Government Primary School in Batiaghata upazila.

According to police sources, Sohel was sitting on a motorcycle on a paved road when unidentified assailants opened fire and fled. He suffered bullet wounds to his right hand and the right side of his abdomen.

Locals took him to Khulna Medical College Hospital, where doctors referred him to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment.

Khulna Additional Superintendent of Police Abir Siddiqui Shuvro said police records show that Sohel has been named in seven cases involving drug-related offences, violations of the Explosives Act and assault, among other charges.

Police are continuing operations to identify and arrest those involved in the shooting. Patrols have also been intensified in the area to maintain law and order.

The two incidents came amid a series of shootings and other violent crimes in Khulna.

On October 24, Ramim Biswas, 32, a Jubo Dal leader, was injured in a shooting in Terokhada upazila. The assailants arrived on a motorcycle and opened fire at him.

On the night of October 17, a young man was shot and his mobile phone snatched at the Amtala intersection in West Tutpara of Khulna city.

Between January and October 23 this year, at least 71 people were killed in Khulna in incidents involving firearms, sharp weapons and other forms of violence, according to police data. Police recorded 69 cases in connection with the killings, with fewer cases than victims because some incidents involved multiple deaths.

Police said most of the killings were linked to disputes over arms and drug trafficking, control of extortion, previous enmity and rivalries among criminal gangs.

title: Jubo Dal leader expelled over FB post on home boss
text:
A local leader of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal in Tangail was expelled from the party allegedly for ‘violating party’s discipline by making inappropriate comment about the government and the party’s senior leaders in social media’.

SM Rafiqul Bari, who was serving as the senior joint convener of Tangail’s Sakhipur upazila unit Jubo Dal, was expelled following a Facebook post on Friday.

“I am mentally hurt. I want resignation of the home minister,” read the Facebook post.

He, however, did not clarify the reasons for his grievance or the context in which he made this demand.

Following his expulsion, Rafiqul told journalists: “There are many political issues. The Home Minister’s flawed decisions are causing harm to many people, including the prime minister……That is why, he [home minister] should resign. I will continue to speak the truth.”

Contacted, the upazila unit Jubo Dal’s Convener Farhad Iqbal said Rafiqul made different types of inappropriate comment about several party leaders in the past. He was warned, but he remained unchanged.

title: Woman sent to jail over remarks criticising BNP
text:
A Mymensingh court yesterday sent a woman to jail this afternoon after she allegedly expressed frustration with the BNP government during a Facebook Live session over the theft of electrical wires from her business.

The woman, identified as Sathi Akter, owns a beauty parlour in Bhaluka upazila of Mymensingh.

Sathi went live twice on Facebook from an account named “Sathi Makeover” at around 2:00pm on Sunday, expressing anger over repeated thefts at her business.

At one point, she said, “I voted for the BNP government, and now I am the sufferer.”

As the videos circulated on social media and tension reportedly escalated, police took her into custody at around 8:30pm on Sunday.

The video triggered angry reactions among local BNP activists and supporters who took position in front of her shop.

In the videos, Sathi said she had been running her business for nearly 14 years but had suffered financial losses following a series of thefts this year. Last month, electrical wires connected to an air conditioner were stolen from one of her shops.

On Sunday morning, she discovered that electrical wires had been cut and stolen from two of her showrooms, while air-conditioner wires were also taken from one of them. She said wires had also been stolen from several nearby shops.

During the Facebook Live sessions, Sathi expressed frustration over her decision to vote for the BNP.

Guljar Ahmed, joint convener of Bhaluka upazila BNP, said party activists were angered by her remarks and, along with locals, went to the scene. Police later went there and brought the situation under control.

Mohammad Zahidul Islam, officer-in-charge of Bhaluka Model Police Station, said Sathi was taken to the police station to maintain law and order.

“No specific complaint has been lodged in connection with the incident so far,” he said.

The OC said the local businesswoman had made the remarks out of frustration over the repeated thefts at her establishment. He added that her comment about voting for the BNP and later suffering losses did not amount to an anti-state statement.

She was produced before a Mymensingh court on Monday afternoon under Section 151, the OC said.

ASM Mustasinur Rahman, court inspector in Mymensingh, said Sathi was produced before the court of Senior Judicial Magistrate Md Sajidul Islam, which sent her to jail.

Contacted, Mymensingh Additional Police Superintendent (Admin) Md Abdullah Al Mamun said if there is any scope for deterioration of law and order, police can arrest a person under Section 151.

title: Coal-laden cargo vessel sinks in Pasur river near Mongla port
text:
A cargo vessel, reportedly carrying 1,200 tonnes of coal, sank in the Pasur river near Mongla port early today after being hit by an oil tanker.

They said the nine crew members aboard swam to a nearby cargo ship and took shelter there. No casualties were reported.

Commodore Md Shafiqul Islam Sarker, member (harbour and marine) of Mongla Port Authority, confirmed the sinking of MV Fulbari and said, “The Pasur channel is completely safe. Vessel movement through the channel is continuing as normal."

He added that the vessel’s owners were taking steps to salvage the sunken ship.

According to crew members of MV Fulbari, the vessel was carrying 1,200 tonnes of coal from MV Yas Jupiter, a foreign commercial vessel anchored at Hiron Point in Mongla port, and was heading towards Dhaka when the accident occurred.

Crew members claimed the oil tanker MT Jannatul Ferdous struck MV Fulbari near Sundari Kotha in the Pasur channel, causing the coal-laden vessel to sink.

According to information provided by the crew, the sunken vessel is owned by IRS International.

MV Fulbari was scheduled to transport the coal to Badamtala in Dhaka.

title: ‘I didn’t feel any pain... I only saw my son lying in a pool of blood’
text:
With both legs bandaged, Azharul Islam lay on the floor outside the emergency department of Chittagong Medical College Hospital (CMCH), wailing inconsolably for his six-year-old son.

“Oh, my son! Oh, Rakib, where are you? Where have you gone?” he cried out in anguish, his voice breaking as he relived the horror of the crash while speaking to The Daily Star hours after the accident.
