Beside him sat his wife, Fatema Aktar, with visible injuries to her face and hands. She stared blankly ahead, too shocked and grief-stricken to speak.

The couple’s journey home turned tragic early today when a speeding lorry ploughed into passengers standing beside the Dhaka–Chittagong highway in Sitakunda early today, after their bus stopped there due to a mechanical fault.

Five people, including their six-year-old son, Rakib, was killed, and both parents were seriously injured.

A first-grader, Rakib was the younger of the couple’s two sons.

Azharul, a farmer, had travelled to Chattogram city to take his wife and son back to their village home in Madan upazila of Netrokona. Fatema works at a readymade garment factory in the Karnaphuli Export Processing Zone (EPZ), and lived in a rented house in the Narikeltola area under Patenga Police Station.

Azharul’s brother, Anwar Hossain, said the family boarded a Shapla Paribahan bus bound for Netrokona from Narikeltola at around 12:30am.

About an hour later, the bus broke down in Sitakunda and came to a halt. “We were standing beside the bus like 20 other passengers,” Azharul said.

The driver and his assistant were trying to fix the vehicle. As the heat inside became unbearable, some passengers, including Azharul, Fatema and Rakib, got off and stood beside the bus.

Moments before the crash, Rakib was only a couple of yards from his father.

“My son was just two yards away from me, and I could hear the driver talking to the bus owner over the phone,” Azharul said.

“All of a sudden, a tank-lorry, trying to overtake another vehicle, rammed right into the people standing beside the bus.”

Azharul said he saw his son lying in a pool of blood.

“Both my legs were injured, but I didn’t feel any pain. I only saw my son. I shouted for help to save him, and locals rushed to rescue us and brought us to CMCH, but they couldn’t save him,” he said, breaking down in tears.

Inspector Shamim Ahmed, officer-in-charge of Baro Awlia Highway Police Station, said at least five people, including three women and a child, were killed in the collision. Six others were injured and taken to CMCH.

Police have seized the lorry, but its driver fled the scene after the crash, he added.

title: Five killed, eight injured as lorry rams into people beside Dhaka-Chattogram highway
text:
At least five people, including three members of the same family, were killed and eight others injured when a speeding lorry ploughed into passengers standing beside the Dhaka–Chittagong highway in Sitakunda early today, after their bus stopped there due to a mechanical fault.

One of the deceased has been identified as six-year-old Rakib; the identities of the others could not be confirmed immediately.

The accident took place around 1:10am in the Chhota Kumira Royal Cement Gate area of Sitakunda upazila in Chattogram.

According to Sitakunda Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohinul Islam, a Dhaka-bound passenger bus from Chattogram developed a mechanical fault around 1:00am and pulled over to the side of the highway.

While the bus was being repaired, the passengers got off and were standing on the roadside. Suddenly, a speeding Dhaka-bound lorry ploughed into them, the OC said.

Three people died on the spot, while two others were declared dead after being taken to Chattogram Medical College Hospital (CMCH), he added.

The injured have been admitted to different wards of the hospital, and several of them are in critical condition, said Nurul Alam, in-charge of the CMCH Police Camp.

title: Cox's Bazar resort fire: 10 victims identified using DNA tests
text:
The identities of 10 people killed in the TupTup Resto and Resort fire in Ukhiya's Patuartek in Cox’s Bazar have been confirmed.

Among those identified were six members of one family and four members of another, both from Dhaka.

Four members of a family are Mohammad Nahidur Rahman, 41, an official of Grand Power Limited in Dhaka’s Shyamoli; his wife, Afsana Matin, 36; and their two daughters, Rozaina Inaya, 9, and Munaina Ihana, 6.

The victims of the other group are Moulita Mehzabin Alvi, 19; her cousins Layla Jahan Nabila, 25 and Israt Jahan Maliha, 27; their cousin Faria Kabir, 33; Faria’s six-year-old son, Mohammad Faizan Noor; and Faria’s brother, Mohammad Nafis Tehami, 24.

They lived in the Banasree and Khilgaon areas of Dhaka.

Nafis Tehami, also known as Jerif, was a student of the Chinese Language and Culture programme at Dhaka University’s Institute of Modern Languages in the 2020-21 academic year.

Moulita Mehzabin Alvi studied Population and Public Health Sciences at East West University, while Layla Jahan Nabila was a student of the chemistry department at Jagannath University.

Criminal Investigation Department (CID) confirmed their identities by conducting DNA tests on their charred bodies and matching them with their relatives.

Rimon Ghosh, the investigating officer in the case, said the bodies would be handed over to their families tomorrow. The authorities would also brief the media on the progress of the investigation.

The fire broke out on October 17 morning at the three-storey resort along the Marine Drive near Patuartek beach in Ukhiya, about 28km from Cox’s Bazar town.

Tourists were staying in eight rooms on the first and second floors, while the ground floor housed a restaurant and staff quarters.

Authorities initially reported recovering 10 bodies from the resort. However, 11 people remained on the missing list, raising questions about the discrepancy between the number of bodies recovered and the number of people reported missing.

A CID official seeking anonymity said the DNA of Nasrin Akter Mukta, 27, was not matched with samples.

Mukta, a teacher at Swapnabilash Niribili School in Ashulia, Savar, came to Cox’s Bazar with her two female friends for a vacation. Her husband, Dewan Faisal, is a former leader of the Dhaka district unit of Jatiyatabadi Chhatra Dal.

Police filed a case against 23 people over the fire, naming resort owner Mohammad Tanvir Sultan Mia as the prime accused.

Tanvir has remained absconding since the incident. Another resort owner, Newaz Morshed, is also reportedly in hiding. Assistant Manager Zahid Hossain is the only person arrested so far, according to police.

title: Man killed in fire at plastic factory in Keraniganj
text:
A man was killed in a fire at Aman Plastic factory in Narikelbagh area of Keraniganj, Dhaka, this afternoon.

The body was found at the factory after the fire was brought under control, said Talha Bin Jasim, an official of the Fire Service and Civil Defence media wing. The victim’s identity could not be confirmed immediately.

The fire service received information about the fire at 12:25pm and reached the scene at 12:32pm. Eight units worked to bring the blaze under control.

The fire was brought under control at 2:00pm, according to the fire service.

title: 10 killed, 23 hurt in road crashes in four districts
text:
At least 10 people were killed and 23 others injured in road accidents in four districts yesterday and on Friday night.

In Munshiganj, three people were killed and at least 16 injured as a bus of Darshana Paribahan plunged into a ditch beside Dhaka-Mawa Expressway in Hasara, Srinagar upazila while attempting to overtake a covered van early yesterday, said police and fire service.

The deceased are bus supervisor Rokunuzzaman Ranju, 57; helper Chanchal Biswas, 23; and passenger Salauddin Ahmed Sakib, 32.

Muhammad Shafiqul Islam, deputy assistant director of Munshiganj fire service, said the bodies were handed over to Hasara Highway Police.

The injured were undergoing treatment at Srinagar Upazila Health Complex and Dhaka Medical College Hospital.

In Jashore, three youths were killed and two others injured in a head-on collision between two motorcycles in the Natunhat Bazar area yesterday.

Siam Hossain, 18, Joy, 18, and Omar Ali, 17, died on the spot, said Kazi Babul Hossain, inspector (investigation) at Jashore Kotwali Police Station.

Rohan, 19, and Rifat, 17, were taken to Jashore General Hospital.

In Gazipur’s Tongi, a man and his son were killed after being hit by an unidentified vehicle while standing beside the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway near Kutumbari Hotel in the Gazipura area yesterday.

Tapan Chandra Das, 50, and his son Likhan Chandra Das, 20, were from Kaibartapara in Sherpur’s Dewanganj, said Nureja Akter, duty officer at Tongi East Police Station.

In Chattogram’s Satkania, a man and his two-year-old daughter were killed and five others injured as a passenger bus hit a CNG-run auto-rickshaw near Jafar Ahmad Degree College on Friday night.

The deceased were identified as Delwar, 30, and his daughter Jannat, 2, of Malihabad area, said Dohazari Highway Police Station OC Md Nurul Absar.

The victims were in the three-wheeler, he said.

Following the accident, locals set the bus on fire and blocked the highway, disrupting traffic from 8:00pm to 9:30pm.

When a patrol vehicle from Satkania Police Station went to the spot, people vandalised it, leaving a policeman injured, OC Nurul said.

A unit of the Satkania fire service later brought the fire under control.

title: Father, son killed in Gazipur road accident
text:
A father and his son were killed after being hit by an unidentified vehicle while standing beside the Dhaka-Mymensingh highway in the Gazipura area of Tongi, Gazipur, this morning.

The deceased were identified as Tapan Chandra Das, 50, and his son Likhan Chandra Das, 20. They were from Kaibartapara area of Dewanganj upazila in Sherpur.

Nureja Akter, duty officer at Tongi East Police Station, confirmed the deaths to The Daily Star.

Police said the father and son were standing near Kutumbari Hotel, on the eastern side of the BRT lane in Gazipura, when a vehicle hit them, leaving both seriously injured.

Police rescued them and took them to Tongi Shaheed Ahsan Ullah Master General Hospital, where doctors declared Likhan dead.

Tapan, who was critically injured, was referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for better treatment. He died while undergoing treatment there around 10:00am.

Mohammad Maksudul Alam, officer-in-charge of Tongi East Police Station, said the bodies had been sent to the morgue at Gazipur Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College.

title: Fire at Gazipur carton factory under control
text:
A fire that broke out at a carton factory in Gazipur’s Kashimpur area this morning has been brought under control after around three and a half hours of efforts.

Nine Fire Service units brought the fire under control at 1:50pm, Rashed Bin Khaled, duty officer at the Fire Service's Dhaka office, later confirmed the information to The Daily Star.

Image Photo: Collected

The fire originated at the carton factory of Supreme Garments in the Shailan area under Kashimpur Police Station in Gazipur city around 10:30am, said Ariful Islam, an official of Kashimpur Fire Service.

Ariful added that the cause of the fire was not yet known. The large quantity of empty cartons inside the factory intensified the blaze. No casualties have been reported so far

title: 3 killed as motorcycles collide head-on in Jashore
text:
Three youths were killed and two others seriously injured in a head-on collision between two motorcycles on the Jashore-Benapole highway in the Natunhat Bazar area of Jashore early today.

The deceased were identified as Siam Hossain, 18, Joy, 18 and Omar Ali, 17 while the injured as Rohan, 19 and Rifat, 17, police said.

According to police and locals, the youths were travelling on two motorcycles when the vehicles collided head-on in the Natunhat Bazar area around 1:00am, killing three on the spot and injuring the other two.

Locals and fire service personnel rescued the injured and took them to Jashore General Hospital.

Dr Bichitra Mallik, in charge of the hospital's emergency department, said three of the victims were declared brought dead. The two injured were admitted to the surgery ward and are undergoing treatment.

Kazi Babul Hossain, inspector (investigation) at Jashore Kotwali Police Station, said the bodies were handed over to the families around 5:30am after the completion of legal formalities.

Legal action in connection with the incident is underway, he added.

title: 3 killed, 16 injured as bus plunges into ditch on Dhaka-Mawa Expressway
text:
Three people were killed and at least 16 injured when a bus plunged into a roadside ditch while attempting to overtake a covered van on the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway in Munshiganj early today.

The deceased were identified as Rokunuzzaman Ranju, 57, a supervisor of Darshana Paribahan; bus helper Chanchal Biswas, 23; and passenger Salauddin Ahmed Sakib, 32.

The accident occurred on the Dhaka-bound lane of the expressway in Hasara, Srinagar upazila, according to police and fire service officials.

Muhammad Shafiqul Islam, deputy assistant director of Munshiganj Fire Service and Civil Defence, said the bodies of the three victims were recovered from the submerged bus and handed over to Hasara Highway Police.

The bodies would be handed over to the victims’ families after the completion of legal procedures, said Md Sohel Rana, officer-in-charge of Hasara Highway Police Station.

He added that the bus driver had been absconding since the accident.

According to fire service officials and locals, the Darshana Paribahan bus was travelling from Chuadanga to Dhaka when it attempted to overtake a covered van in Hasara. The bus lost control, reportedly due to reckless speeding, smashed through the guardrail, crossed the service lane and plunged into a deep roadside ditch.

After receiving information about the accident, two rescue units from Srinagar Fire Station rushed to the scene. Firefighters rescued 11 people from the submerged bus and took them to Srinagar Upazila Health Complex, while five others received first aid at the scene.

Dr Md Shahriar, an emergency medical officer at Srinagar Upazila Health Complex, said 11 people were taken to the hospital following the accident. Four of them received initial treatment before being referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, while the remaining patients were treated at Srinagar.

title: Sub-inspector, man killed as van hits police patrol team
text:
A sub-inspector (SI) of police and a local man were killed, and two others were injured, after an unidentified covered van hit a police patrol team in Kaliganj, Gazipur, early yesterday.

The accident occurred in front of Kaliganj Government Labour College. The deceased were identified as SI Mizanur Rahman, 30, of Kaliganj Police Station, and Rafiq Molla, 45, of the Tumulia area, said Moniruzzaman, duty officer at Kaliganj Police Station.

The injured were identified as SI Jabed Omar, 28, and Rabbi, 28. Jabed Omar is undergoing treatment in Dhaka.

Kaliganj Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Ashraful Islam said a patrol team led by SI Mizanur had gone to Tumulia searching for several suspected individuals when a Ghorashal-bound covered van hit them and fled the scene.

The injured were taken to Kaliganj Upazila Health Complex, where the doctor declared Rafiq dead, Ashraful said.

Mizanur and Jabed were later taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared Mizanur dead.

title: Father, 2-year-old daughter killed in Ctg road crash
text:
A man and his two-year-old daughter were killed and five others injured in a head-on collision between a passenger bus and a CNG-run auto-rickshaw in Satkania upazila of Chattogram yesterday.

The victims are Delwar, 30, and his daughter Jannat. They were residents of Malihabad in the upazila, said police.

The accident occurred around 7:45pm near Jafar Ahmad Degree College on the Chattogram-Cox's Bazar highway, said Md Nurul Absar, officer-in-charge of Dohazari Highway Police Station.

The victims were travelling in the three-wheeler to attend a fair at the upazila headquarters when it collided head-on with a passenger bus heading towards Chattogram, the OC said.

Following the accident, locals set fire to the bus and blocked the highway, disrupting traffic from 8:00pm to 9:30pm.

When a patrol vehicle from Satkania Police Station went to the spot to bring the situation under control, people vandalised it, leaving a police member injured, Nurul Absar said.

A unit of the Satkania Fire Service went to the scene and brought the fire under control.

Additional police arrived around 9:30pm and cleared the blockade, allowing traffic to resume. Additional police have been deployed at the scene, and legal action will be taken over the incident, the OC added.

title: Fire at Cox’s Bazar hotel sparks panic among tourists
text:
A fire at a hotel near Sugandha Point on Cox’s Bazar beach sparked panic among tourists on Friday, barely a week after 10 people died in a fire at Tuptup Resort in Ukhiya's Patuartek.

The fire broke out in the generator room on the ground floor of The Sea Princess Hotel shortly before 5:00pm. No casualties were reported, said Dolon Acharya, senior station officer of Cox’s Bazar Fire Service and Civil Defence.

More than 300 tourists were staying at the nine-storey hotel at the time of the incident.

Dolon said a unit from a nearby fire station rushed to the site after receiving information about the fire. However, the hotel authorities had brought it under control before firefighters reached the spot.

He said the fire was initially suspected to have originated from a short circuit in the generator.

Abdul Kader, managing director of the hotel, said all the tourists were safe.

He said the hotel had adequate firefighting equipment and that the prompt response of its staff had helped prevent a major accident.

Although no one was injured, the fire damaged the generator and several other facilities in the parking area, he added.

The incident triggered panic among tourists, many of whom rushed out of the nine-storey building.

title: Tongi gas fire: 16-year-old girl dies after parents
text:
A 16-year-old who suffered severe burns in a fire caused by a gas leak in Gazipur's Tongi died while undergoing treatment at a hospital this morning.

Tanisha, who had 86 percent burns in her body, died at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka around 8:00am today, the hospital informed the Tongi West Police Station this morning.

Her parents Lal Chan, 60, and Nasima, 50, died at the same hospital around 8:00pm on Wednesday, said Arifur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Tongi West Police Station.

Lal Chan had 95 percent burns and Nasima 85 percent on their bodies.

Arifur said Tanisha, her father and her mother were undergoing treatment in the intensive care unit (ICU) of the hospital since Wednesday.

With her death, the number of fatalities in the incident has risen to three.

On October 21, around 7:00am, the three suffered burns in a fire caused by a gas leak at their rented house in the Mudafa area of Tongi. Neighbours rescued them and took them to the burn institute in critical condition.

title: Six killed in separate Faridpur road accidents within an hour
text:
Six people were killed and seven others injured in separate road accidents within an hour on the Dhaka-Khulna highway in Faridpur today.

Three people were killed in Madhukhali upazila, while three others died in Faridpur Sadar upazila.

In Madhukhali, three people were killed and four others injured in a head-on collision between an ambulance and a bus on the Dhaka-Khulna highway in the Arkandi area around 2:00pm.

The deceased are Rabbi Hasan, Aishi, and Mohammad Atik, said Madhukhali Upazila Health and Family Planning Officer Dr Al-Amin Sarwar.

According to highway police and fire service sources, an ambulance heading to Magura from Faridpur collided head-on with a Dhaka-bound Kingfisher Paribahan bus in the Arkandi area. Three ambulance passengers died on the spot, while four others were injured.

On information, police and fire service personnel went to the scene, recovered the bodies and rescued the injured.

Abdus Salam, officer-in-charge of Karimpur Highway Police Station, said preliminary information suggested that all the victims were members of a volunteer organisation. They had travelled from Magura to Faridpur in the morning to attend a training session and were returning to Magura by ambulance when the accident occurred.

Police seized the bus, and further legal procedures were underway, the OC said.

In Faridpur Sadar upazila, three people, including a woman and her son, were killed when a sand-laden truck overturned onto an easy-bike in Kanaipur around 3:30pm today.

The deceased were identified as Sumi Begum, 32, wife of Palash Mia of Chapainawabganj, and her son Shawon, 7, said Sribas Baroi, senior station officer of Faridpur Fire Service.

According to sources at Karimpur Highway Police Station, Sumi’s family lives in Dhaka. Six family members had gone to visit her father’s house in Magura recently. As they could not get bus tickets to Dhaka from Magura, they were heading to Faridpur bus stand in an easy-bike to buy tickets.

On the way, a sand-laden truck coming from the opposite direction lost control at Tetultala and overturned onto the easy-bike and a private car.

Six easy-bike passengers were critically injured. Locals rescued them and took them to Faridpur Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared Sumi and Shawon dead. The easy-bike driver, who was trapped under the sand, was later recovered dead after nearly an hour of efforts, police said.

Karimpur Highway Police Station Officer-in-Charge Abdus Salam also confirmed the deaths.

title: Covered van hits police patrol in Gazipur, killing SI and local man
text:
A sub-inspector (SI) of police and a local man were killed and two others injured after an unidentified covered van hit a police patrol team in Kaliganj, Gazipur, early today.

The accident occurred in front of Kaliganj Government Labour College. The deceased were identified as SI Mizanur Rahman, 30, of Kaliganj Police Station, and Rafiq Molla, 45, son of the late Waz Uddin Molla of the Tumulia area, Moniruzzaman, duty officer at Kaliganj Police Station, confirmed the deaths to The Daily Star.

The injured were identified as SI Jabed Omar, 28, and Rabbi, 28. Jabed Omar is undergoing treatment in Dhaka.

Kaliganj Police Station Inspector (Investigation) Ashraful Islam said a team of officers led by Mizanur had gone to Tumulia for a patrol and was searching several suspected individuals when a covered van heading towards Ghorashal hit them and fled the scene.

Other police personnel rescued the injured and took them to Kaliganj Upazila Health Complex, where the on-duty physician declared Rafiq dead, Ashraful said.

After receiving initial treatment, seriously injured Mizanur and Jabed were later taken to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, where doctors declared Mizanur dead.

title: Couple dies after gas cylinder blast in Gazipur
text:
A couple died last night after suffering severe burns in a gas cylinder explosion at their home in Tongi on Wednesday.

The deceased were identified as Md Lalchan, 60, and Nasima Begum, 50, both garment workers.

Their daughter, Tanisa Akter, 16, is undergoing treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka.

The explosion occurred around 6:00am in the Mudafa area of Tongi’s Cherag Ali, reportedly due to a gas cylinder leak. The three were rescued and taken to the burn institute around 7:30am.

Dr Sultan Mahmud Shikder, a resident physician at the institute, said Lalchan had suffered burns to 95 percent of his body, Nasima 85 percent and Tanisa 86 percent.

Md Arifur Rahman, officer-in-charge of Tongi West Police Station, said the explosion was caused by a gas cylinder leak.

title: IGP’s ‘crossfire’ remarks embarrassing for govt: Rizvi
text:
BNP Acting Secretary General and Prime Minister's Political Adviser Ruhul Kabir Rizvi today said Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir's remarks about carrying out "crossfire" with the government's permission were embarrassing for the government.

Expressing concern over the comments, Rizvi said the police chief had spoken about "crossfire" at a time when BNP, which had long campaigned against enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings, was in power.

He made the remarks while inaugurating a free medical camp in front of the BNP central office in Dhaka's Nayapaltan, marking the 48th founding anniversary of Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal.

Referring to the IGP's statement, Rizvi questioned how the head of the police force, as part of the government, could speak about "crossfire".

However, the matter would be different if the remarks had been made unintentionally, he said.

Rizvi said BNP had fought against "crossfire", enforced disappearances, extrajudicial killings, bloodshed and fascist rule for 17 years, and that struggle had culminated in the events of July and August 5, 2024 with the BNP later coming to power through a free and fair election.

Following Tarique Rahman's election as prime minister, people across the country expect a more humane Bangladesh, he said. Against that backdrop, the police chief's remarks about crossfire had raised serious concerns, Rizvi added.

He said the country already had adequate laws to deal with crime and that law enforcement agencies should apply those laws properly.

Rizvi also expressed concern over rising juvenile crime and other criminal activities in several areas of Dhaka.

He said there were many honest and competent officers in the police force who should be allowed to perform their duties independently.

He also urged people holding responsible positions in various institutions to act and speak responsibly, warning that statements made merely to gain praise could harm the country.

Earlier on Monday, IGP Ali Hossain Fakir said at a programme in Dhaka's Chawkbazar that "crossfire will be carried out if necessary with the government's permission". Amid the criticism, Police Headquarters issued a clarification on Monday evening, saying the IGP had not used the term "crossfire" to suggest extrajudicial killings or punishment outside the legal process.

title: Police cannot carry out crossfire even if government orders it: Adviser Zahed
text:
The government cannot order police to carry out ‘crossfire’, and even if it does, officers cannot execute such an order because public servants are not obliged to obey "unlawful instructions", Prime Minister’s Adviser on Information and Cultural Affairs Zahed Ur Rahman said today.

He made the remarks in response to questions from journalists at the weekly press briefing at the Secretariat on the progress of various government activities.

Referring to Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir’s recent remarks that police would resort to crossfire if necessary and permitted by the government, Zahed said the police chief had subsequently acknowledged the problem with his statement and stepped back from that position.

“Through his subsequent explanation, he acknowledged that his remarks were problematic and stepped back from that position,” the adviser said.

Zahed further said the prime minister was currently abroad and would consider the government’s final position after returning from his important tour to Japan.

He questioned whether the IGP should be treated too harshly after retracting his position. “However, let me say again, when someone does not stick to their stance, are we being a bit too unkind to him?” he said.

Asked whether an explanation was enough to absolve someone of responsibility for such remarks, Zahed replied that he believed it could be, as the IGP had not maintained his original position.

Responding to a question about the return of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina, Zahed said she would have to face justice if she came back to Bangladesh.

He said she would not face mob violence or any other unlawful situation upon her return, and that legal proceedings would take place in accordance with the law.

Referring to an incident in which a freedom fighter’s burial was obstructed, Zahed said available information suggested that a political party had been involved.

Describing the incident as deeply regrettable, he said those responsible would have to face the consequences.

Asked about the rise of fundamentalism and the far right since the 2024 mass uprising, Zahed said the government was taking the developments seriously.

Referring to the killing of a person in Satkhira over allegations of defaming religion, he said the government had taken strict measures in response.

He added that some incidents were prevented through prior intelligence, although the public might not be aware of those interventions.

“The government takes action on those that you do see. This means the government is not indulging these, nor will it do so,” he said.

title: Govt forms 20 teams to monitor Dhaka cleanliness drives
text:
The government has formed 20 special monitoring teams to oversee cleanliness drives across Dhaka, warning of hefty fines for violations and cancellation of government housing allocations if unhygienic conditions or Aedes mosquito larvae are found.

LGRD State Minister Mir Shahe Alam issued the directives at a meeting at the Prime Minister’s Office in Tejgaon today.

“There will be no compromise on cleanliness,” he said, warning that government employees who fail to maintain hygiene in their residential quarters could lose their housing allocations.

According to a press release issued by the ministry, the meeting was held at Shapla Hall at 3:00pm, with State Minister for Housing and Public Works Ahmad Sohel Manzur attending as a special guest.

Mir Shahe Alam said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had personally visited government hospitals and residential quarters to assess their conditions, but recent cleanliness drives had found Aedes larvae and serious negligence at large government residential complexes, luxury apartments and hospitals.

He instructed committee members to take legal action and impose heavy fines wherever irregularities or mosquito larvae were found, saying government employees who could not keep their quarters clean had no right to government housing.

The government expects coordinated action by the teams to bring visible improvements to Dhaka within one to two months.

Of the 20 committees, 10 will operate in Dhaka North and 10 in Dhaka South, covering zones corresponding to the regional executive officers of the two city corporations. Director-level officials from the Prime Minister’s Office are heading the committees.

The state minister also said RAJUK and Dhaka South City Corporation were working to clean Hatirjheel, Dhanmondi, Banani and Gulshan lakes. Work is also under way to re-excavate 29 canals under Dhaka North and 26 under Dhaka South, alongside the construction of guide walls and installation of netting.

The government has also decided to introduce fibreboard dustbins after plastic and iron bins were stolen. The two city corporations will install the new bins in phases.

The meeting was chaired by Prime Minister’s Office Principal Secretary ABM Abdus Sattar and attended by members of the 20 monitoring committees.

title: Four-storey resort demolished over unauthorised construction in Cox's Bazar
text:
Authorities today demolished a four-storey resort building in Ukhiya's Inani as part of a joint drive against unauthorised hotels and resorts along Cox’s Bazar’s Marine Drive.

The demolition comes days after a fire at the three-storey TupTup Resort near Patuartek beach killed 10 tourists on October 17.

Led by the Cox’s Bazar Development Authority (CoxDA), the drive began this afternoon, with officials from the district administration, police, SRB, Fire Service, Department of Environment and Ansar.

An excavator arrived around 11:00am. Workers first demolished 10-12 ground-floor shops and those along the building’s two sides, then broke the glass fittings and began demolishing the main structure’s pillars.

CoxDA Secretary Sanjida Begum said the owner had received four notices to demolish the unauthorised building but had taken no effective steps. She said the structure had been built in violation of applicable laws and regulations.

However, owner Shahidul Haque claimed he began construction in 2014 after obtaining permission from the union parishad. He claimed that at least Tk 6cr was spent on the project.

The ground floor was intended for shops, the second for a restaurant, and the third and fourth for tourist accommodation. He had planned to inaugurate the resort soon.

Shahidul said he had replied to all four notices and possessed the necessary documents, but alleged that the authorities were ignoring them.

CoxDA Chairman Engineer Mohammad Jasim Uddin said numerous resorts, cottages and restaurants had been built along both sides of the 80-km Marine Drive, many without the required approvals. The joint drive was launched after unauthorised structures remained despite repeated notices, he said, adding that illegal establishments would not be allowed to remain.

Since CoxDA was established in 2016, around 1,700 building plans have been approved across Cox’s Bazar district, including the municipality area, Jasim Uddin said.

Despite restrictions on infrastructure development along Marine Drive, around 2,500 structures have been built there, including more than 200 hotels, resorts, and cottages. Apart from a few star-rated establishments, most lacked valid approvals, he added.

title: CDA partially demolishes 4 buildings, seals 2 in Chattogram over plan violations
text:
A mobile court of the Chattogram Development Authority (CDA) today partially demolished unauthorised sections of four buildings and sealed off two others in the port city's Khulshi and Chandgaon areas for violating approved construction plans.

The drive targeted six buildings, according to a CDA press release.

The extended portions of four buildings were partially demolished for deviating from approved designs, while two buildings were sealed off. Their owners were also required to submit written affidavits pledging to comply fully with building codes and regulations in future, the release said.

CDA also issued strict warnings to two other establishments, including Basket, a popular commercial store in Khulshi, over unauthorised structural modifications.

CDA Chairman Engineer Belayet Hossain said constructing buildings in violation of approved designs posed serious threats to planned urban development and public safety.

He added that drives against deviations from approved designs and construction irregularities would continue to ensure a planned, safe and liveable Chattogram, urging building owners to act responsibly.

The drive was jointly led by CDA Special Magistrate Hamimun Tanjin, a joint district and sessions judge, and Authorised Officer-01 Kazi Kader Newaz. Senior CDA officials, staff and an adequate number of law enforcement personnel were present during the operation.

title: Why president, PM are not getting a pay hike
text:
The new pay scale has brought higher salaries for government employees, with some top bureaucrats set to earn more in basic pay than the president and the prime minister. Yet the country’s top government executive and the head of state will continue with their previous salaries, as a proposed hike remains on hold.

Why has their remuneration not been revised alongside the pay scale for government employees?

Because it has yet to receive the prime minister’s approval.

Under the ninth pay scale, a secretary’s basic salary has been set at Tk 1.56 lakh, while the cabinet secretary and the principal secretary to the prime minister will receive Tk 1.72 lakh.

By comparison, the president’s monthly remuneration stands at Tk 1.20 lakh and the prime minister’s at Tk 1.15 lakh. Ministers receive Tk 1.05 lakh, while state ministers get Tk 92,000.

Government employees began receiving increased salaries in July. However, the remuneration of the president, prime minister, ministers and state ministers has not been revised alongside the new pay scale.

Why has the usual process of revising their remuneration stalled?

PM yet to give green signal

Cabinet division officials said laws governing remuneration increases for the president, cabinet members and judges are usually amended alongside the implementation of a government pay scale.

Accordingly, the cabinet division had prepared to increase the remuneration of the president, prime minister, ministers and state ministers. Two high-level sources at the prime minister’s office and the cabinet division told The Daily Star that Tarique Rahman put it on hold.

The remuneration, allowances and privileges of the president are governed by the President’s (Remuneration and Privileges) Act. The prime minister’s salary and facilities are determined under the Prime Minister’s (Remuneration and Privileges) Act, while those of ministers, state ministers and deputy ministers are fixed by the Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers (Remuneration and Privileges) Act.

An official at the Prime Minister’s Office, speaking on condition of anonymity, recently told The Daily Star that there was currently no initiative to increase the remuneration of ministers and state ministers, and that no such move was likely anytime soon.

On the day he was sworn in, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman announced that members of parliament would not take duty-free cars or be allotted government plots or flats.

Proposal raised three times

A high-ranking cabinet official, speaking on condition of anonymity yesterday, Sunday, said the proposal to increase the remuneration of public representatives had been brought to the prime minister’s attention soon after the new pay scale was implemented.

“At the time, instructions were given to bring it up later. The matter was subsequently brought to his attention twice more, but no green signal was given. So, it can be said that the remuneration of the president and cabinet members is not increasing for now,” the official said.

He said that the cabinet division was unlikely to raise it again since the prime minister has put it off for three time already.

title: Keeping envoy in Dhaka during PM’s Japan visit an internal matter of foreign ministry: Shama Obaed
text:
The decision to bring Bangladesh Ambassador to Japan Md Daud Ali back in Dhaka during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s upcoming visit to Japan is an internal matter of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, State Minister Shama Obaed Islam said today.

She made the remarks while responding to reporters after an event at the CIRDAP auditorium on Topkhana Road in Dhaka this afternoon.

The programme, titled “National Position Paper Unveiling and Dialogue”, was organised by ActionAid ahead of the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31), scheduled for November 9-20.

Tarique Rahman is scheduled to visit Japan from October 26 to 29. It emerged two days ago that Daud Ali had been asked to remain in Dhaka ahead of the visit and would not be in Tokyo during the prime minister’s trip.

Asked about the decision, Shama said, “It is absolutely an internal matter of the ministry. This is neither a national nor an international issue.”

She added, “It is a standard procedure. The decision on when an ambassador will be called back by the foreign ministry rests entirely with the ministry.”

Highlighting Dhaka’s ties with Tokyo, she said Japan had remained Bangladesh’s top trade and development partner for many years.

“Our relationship with Japan dates back to our Liberation War and has grown even deeper over time. You will notice that Bangladesh-Japan relations have advanced further under every BNP government,” she said.

Describing the prime minister’s upcoming visit as highly significant, Shama said a number of memorandums of understanding (MoUs) could be signed in areas including infrastructure, energy, technology, garments, education and health.

She also expressed hope that the visit would help attract new Japanese investment to Bangladesh.

“We believe the prime minister’s visit will create opportunities for fresh Japanese investment. A new Bangladesh Invest law has been enacted at the prime minister’s initiative, and through this framework we expect more Japanese investment to come to Bangladesh. Promoting that effort will be one of the objectives of this delegation,” she said.

title: Sports can protect youth from addiction, frustration: President
text:
Sports are the best way to protect the younger generation from drug addiction, mobile phone addiction and frustration, President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir said today.

“Sports teach young people discipline, perseverance and self-confidence,” he said at the inaugural ceremony of the 18th Arafat Rahman Koko National Summer Athletics Competition 2026 at the National Stadium this evening.

The president formally inaugurated the competition by releasing balloons.

He said expanding sports facilities and ensuring access to playgrounds were essential to protecting young people from destruction and building a healthy nation.

“Athletics is called the mother of sports. It is where an athlete's speed, strength, agility, discipline and endurance are truly tested. Strengthening this foundation will also enhance the country's capabilities in other sports,” he said.

Describing sports as a symbol of national pride and unity, Fakhrul said, “Seeing Bangladesh's flag flying on the international stage and hearing the national anthem played on the victory podium are sources of pride for the entire nation. At such moments, we have only one identity: we are Bangladeshis.”

He said the country must develop its own athletes and ensure that its teams achieve success on the international stage.

The President also called for equal opportunities for female athletes alongside their male counterparts to make sports more meaningful and inclusive.

He urged the authorities to organise competitions regularly at school, college, district and upazila levels so that no talent was lost due to financial constraints.

He also called on industrial enterprises, banks, insurance companies and the business community to join the government in providing long-term sponsorship to develop world-class athletes.

Highlighting government initiatives to develop sports, the president said, “Initiatives are being implemented to introduce sports cards and sports allowances, launch talent-hunting programmes at the grassroots level and establish modern sports villages at the district level and build playgrounds at every union level.”

“A new wave of enthusiasm has emerged in the country's sports arena. The prime minister is playing an important role in advancing all types of sports at the grassroots,” he added.

The president urged the relevant authorities to recover illegally occupied playgrounds, preserve existing fields and identify locations for new playgrounds.

He expressed hope that the competition would produce many talented athletes who would bring further glory to Bangladesh on the international stage.

The competition was dedicated to the memory of sports organiser and Tarique Rahman's brother Arafat Rahman Koko. The president prayed for the salvation of his soul before inaugurating the event.

State Minister Md Aminul Haque addressed the ceremony as a special guest, while Advocate Ali Imam Tapan delivered the welcome address. Bangladesh Athletics Federation President Mohammad Abdullah Zaber chaired the event.

Earlier, a march-past featuring 57 participating teams was held, followed by a performance of the competition's theme song. Veteran athletes Mohiuddin Ahmed and Sumita Rani Das lit the games' torch.

After the inauguration, the president watched the men's and women's 100-metre sprint competitions and presented medals to the winners in both categories.

The president arrived at the venue at 4:00pm, where he was welcomed by State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque, Dhaka South City Corporation Administrator Md Abdus Salam, Bangladesh Athletics Federation President Mohammad Abdullah Zaber and its General Secretary Advocate Ali Imam Tapan.

title: Curbs on secretariat visitor access on cards
text:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has asked officials to consider reducing visitor numbers and shortening visiting hours at the secretariat after noticing large crowds during recent visits to ministries.

At least three sources at the Prime Minister’s Office and the Ministry of Home Affairs confirmed the development to The Daily Star.

Visitor entry is currently barred on Mondays and Thursdays. However, on Thursday, October 15, the prime minister noticed large gatherings while descending from the 14th floor of Building 6 after inspecting the environment ministry.

He then summoned the home ministry’s deputy secretary (security), the deputy commissioner of police and the additional deputy commissioner responsible for secretariat security to his office in the complex.

After being briefed on visitor management, the premier instructed them to submit a proposal through the home ministry.

This correspondent spoke to at least five officials, including two who briefed the prime minister.

One official, requesting anonymity, said internal discussions were underway and the home ministry would submit a proposal after the Puja holidays.

“The prime minister asked us to consider limiting visiting hours to 2:00pm-4:00pm. We are also considering reducing visitor access to two days a week.”

Visiting hours currently run from 12:00pm to 4:00pm.

Another official said cancelling all temporary passes was also under consideration, but a decision would follow a review of the arrangements.

The official said some passes issued under successive governments for political reasons remained in use.

“Although they are issued in the names of businessmen and contractors, we will not make a decision on this; it must come from the political level.”

However, no changes are being considered for retired officials’ passes. Secretaries, additional secretaries and joint secretaries retain lifelong access to the secretariat after retirement.

Home ministry sources said at least 27,000 access cards are held by employees working inside and outside the secretariat, while around 2,500 visitors enter daily using one-time passwords (OTPs).

At least 7,000 passes have also been issued, including temporary passes for contractors, businessmen, former officials and people working on projects under the Ministry of Housing and Public Works.

Under existing rules, secretaries can issue five daily passes, additional secretaries three and joint secretaries two. Ministers and state ministers can issue 10 each.

The secretariat is one of the country’s key points of interest.

Previous prime ministers generally worked from the Prime Minister’s Office, visiting the secretariat for cabinet meetings and other important discussions.

Since taking office, Tarique Rahman has worked from the secretariat almost every day, occasionally holding meetings at the Prime Minister’s Office on Saturdays.

However, security arrangements have largely remained unchanged.

The Cabinet Division recently issued a nine-point directive to the home ministry to tighten security and regulate visitor access to the secretariat.

title: Cabinet Division asks govt offices to follow national flag rules
text:
The Cabinet Division has directed ministries and government agencies to ensure compliance with national flag rules following reports that some officials are displaying the flag in their offices without authorisation.

This was confirmed in a letter signed by Deputy Secretary Sharmin Yasmin on October 11.

In the letter, the Cabinet Division said some officials and individuals working in government and statutory bodies were displaying the national flag on poles behind their chairs or sofas, despite not being entitled to do so.

Some offices were also keeping the national flag on display round the clock, in violation of the People's Republic of Bangladesh Flag Rules, 1972.

Under the rules, the national flag can generally be displayed only between sunrise and sunset, except on motor vehicles, vessels and aircraft. The rules also allow the flag to be displayed at night on buildings on certain special occasions.

The Cabinet Division further observed that some offices were using the flag as interior decoration or as a backdrop for personal and official purposes without maintaining its prescribed size, proportions and colours.

Such practices constitute direct violations of the Bangladesh National Anthem, Flag and Emblem Order, 1972, and the national flag rules, the letter added.

The division asked senior secretaries and secretaries to take necessary measures to ensure proper respect for the national flag and issue corresponding instructions to offices under their authority, including constitutional and autonomous bodies.

The letter, however, did not identify the officials or institutions involved or mention any specific action against those violating the rules.

title: HSC 2026 results on October 31: How to check your results online and via SMS
text:
The results of this year's Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on Saturday (October 31), with students able to check their results online, via SMS and through their educational institutions.

According to a notice issued by the Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee, the results will be announced at a programme beginning at 11:00am at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka.

The notice, signed by committee president Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, also chairman of the Dhaka Education Board, said students would be able to access their results through the available channels following the formal announcement.

How to check results online

Students can visit eduboardresults.gov.bd or educationboardresults.gov.bd, or the websites of their respective education boards.

They will need to select the examination, education board and examination year (2026), then enter their roll and registration numbers and other required details to view their results.

Educational institutions can download result sheets through the “Result” section of the websites by selecting their board and entering their Educational Institution Identification Number (EIIN). Students can also collect their results directly from their institutions.

How to check results via SMS

Students can check their results by sending an SMS to 16140 from a mobile phone.

They need to type HSC, followed by the first three letters of their education board's name, roll number and examination year, separated by spaces.

For example, a Dhaka Board candidate should type: HSC Dha 123456 2026

The message should then be sent to 16140.

Re-evaluation applications

Students wishing to have their results re-evaluated can apply online from November 1 to 7. Details of the application process will be available on the respective education boards’ websites.

A total of 12,70,583 candidates registered for this year's HSC and equivalent examinations under 11 education boards.

The results were initially scheduled to be published on October 29 but were later deferred to October 31.

title: HSC results date revised to October 31
text:
The results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations will be published on October 31, two days later than the date announced earlier.

Prof Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chairman of the Dhaka Education Board and head of the Bangladesh Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee, confirmed the revised date to The Daily Star today.

Education ministry and board sources said the change came amid complications over obtaining the prime minister’s consent to publish the results.

However, Prof Akhtaruzzaman dismissed the speculation, telling this newspaper that the new date had been finalised after consultation with the education minister.

The results were initially scheduled to be published on October 29.

On October 24, the committee issued a notice, signed by Akhtaruzzaman, announcing that date. The notice also said a press release detailing the arrangements would be issued on October 26.

However, no such press release was issued yesterday.

This year’s HSC and equivalent examinations began on July 2, with 12,70,583 candidates registered under 11 education boards.

Written examinations under most boards ended on August 8.

However, flooding forced the postponement of several papers under the Chattogram Education Board, where written examinations continued until September 9.

title: Four new textbooks for classes 4 and 6
text:
The National Curriculum Coordination Committee (NCCC) yesterday approved four new textbooks for Classes 4 and 6 for the 2027 academic year, subject to necessary revisions.

The approved Class 4 books are Culture of Bangladesh and Sports, while the Class 6 books are Learning with Happiness and My Technical Education.

NCTB Chairman Prof Mohammad Fakhrul Mawla said the new subjects were designed not to increase students’ academic burden and would not be assessed through conventional grading.

title: Four new textbooks approved for Classes 4 and 6 for 2027
text:
The National Curriculum Coordination Committee (NCCC) today approved four new textbooks for Classes 4 and 6 for the 2027 academic year, subject to necessary revisions.

The approvals came at two separate meetings held at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka.

The approved Class 4 books are Culture of Bangladesh and Sports, while the Class 6 books are Learning with Happiness and My Technical Education. The National Curriculum and Textbook Board (NCTB) has been preparing the books for introduction next year.

Earlier, NCTB Chairman Prof Mohammad Fakhrul Mawla told The Daily Star that the new subjects were designed not to increase students' academic burden and would not be assessed through conventional grading.

Education and Primary and Mass Education Adviser ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon attended both meetings as the chief guest.

The meeting on the Class 4 textbooks was chaired by Primary and Mass Education Secretary Jesmin Nahar. Education State Minister Bobby Hajjaj, Prime Minister's Special Assistant Gias Uddin, Chief Information Commissioner Nahrin Islam Khan and Prime Minister's Press Secretary Abu Abdullah M Saleh were also present.

The meeting on the Class 6 textbooks was chaired by Secondary and Higher Education Division Secretary Abdul Khaleque. Gias Uddin and Nahrin Islam Khan were among those present.
